articles.title: OCC Asks Community Banks to Issue Payment Stablecoins, Citing GENIUS
articles.text:
US OCC calls on community banks to become payment stablecoin issuers
The announcement followed the banking regulator finalizing its rules for the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin law to be implemented in January
The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has petitioned community banks to enter the payment stablecoin market as part of the regulator’s rules on the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act.
In a Monday X post, the OCC said that it was “encouraging the development of payment stablecoin capabilities within the community banking sector,” citing its finalized rules for the GENIUS Act. The payment stablecoin law is set to be enforced starting in January, and the OCC finalized its rules for the bill last week.
“Interested community banks are encouraged to consider applying to become, or for a subsidiary to become, a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, as applicable,” said the US banking regulator.
The plea to community banks came as many banking advocacy groups pushed back against the OCC’s proposed rules on stablecoin yield, with some arguing that they went against the congressional intent behind GENIUS. If enough community banks were to enter the stablecoin market, they could challenge the market share of crypto companies and financial institutions.
Community banks are already engaged in legal action against the OCC over the regulator’s approval for charter applications from crypto companies. Earlier this month, the Independent Community Bankers of America filed a lawsuit alleging that crypto companies had an advantage over community bankers by not being subject to the same regulatory requirements.
Related: Ex-Trump crypto adviser profited after helping pass stablecoin bill: WSJ

articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra, Its Half-Good AI Model at Half the Price - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, with standard API prices 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra.
- It is available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and to developers as gpt-6.1-terra.
- In OpenAI's internal test, Terra's rate of factual errors at low reasoning effort fell from 53.6% to 16.7%, and at maximum effort it solved 50.3% of Terminal-Bench 4.0 tasks versus 21.5% for GPT-5.6 Terra.
OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Monday, an upgrade to the middle model in its lineup that it says costs developers 50% less than GPT-5.6 Terra and handles computer tasks faster and more accurately.
Terra is the everyday model, built for routine office work like reading what is on a screen, clicking through apps, and drafting replies. That skill is called computer use, meaning an AI that sees your screen and clicks and types the way you would. The 50% cut applies to standard API prices, the rates developers pay to plug the model into their own apps.
“It’s a significant step up over GPT-5.6 Terra, with 50% lower standard API prices,” OpenAI said in its announcement, adding that “GPT-6.1 Terra is rolling out now and is available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex.”
ChatGPT Work is OpenAI’s agent mode inside ChatGPT, which can work across apps and browse and complete tasks on websites for you, and Codex is OpenAI’s coding tool. Free users get to use the lower-tier GPT-5.6 Luna.
On an internal OpenAI test built from prompts designed to trick models into making mistakes, the rate of factual errors at low reasoning effort, a setting that controls how long the model thinks, fell from 53.6% for GPT-5.6 Terra to 16.7%. At maximum effort it fell 18 points to 4.3%.
On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which tests coding agents on tasks run through a computer’s command-line terminal and scores the share of tasks completed successfully, Terra at maximum effort solved 50.3% of tasks versus 21.5% for GPT-5.6 Terra. OpenAI also says Terra finishes tasks more than three times faster on average than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. All of the figures are OpenAI’s own, and the error test is an internal one.
OpenAI introduced Terra on June 26 as part of the GPT-5.6 family in a limited preview requested by the Donald Trump administration, then opened it to the public on July 9 as a model competitive with GPT-5.5 at about half the cost.
In September the company launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna minutes after Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, with no new Terra.
For in-depth research or complex coding, OpenAI still points users to GPT-6.1 Sol or GPT-6 Astra.

articles.title: Injective Expands AI Derivatives With Five-GPU Index
articles.text:
Injective launches onchain futures market tracking Nvidia GPU rental costs
The new index tracks rental prices for five Nvidia GPUs, offering leveraged trading and potential hedging against fluctuations in AI computing costs.
Layer-1 blockchain Injective has launched a perpetual futures market tracking the rental prices of five Nvidia GPUs, allowing traders to bet on changes in AI computing costs with up to 10x leverage.
The Super Intelligence Compute Index (SICI) tracks rental prices for Nvidia’s H100, B200, H200, A100 and RTX 4090 chips, using data from compute marketplaces compiled by London-based market data firm LO:TECH.
According to Monday’s announcement, the index assigns the largest weight to the H100 at 40%, followed by the B200 at 25%. It is updated hourly using a trailing seven-day average of rental prices. Traders can take positions on whether the index will rise or fall, using USDC as margin.
The launch builds on Injective’s August 2025 introduction of a market tied to Nvidia H100 rental prices, expanding the offering from a single GPU model to a five-chip index.
Companies developing AI models often rent computing power from cloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius rather than purchasing Nvidia GPUs outright. As rental prices rise and fall with demand, Injective said the futures market could help developers hedge against higher computing costs while allowing GPU providers to protect against declining rental revenue.
Related: Injective, BDACS plan Korean won stablecoin settlement for tokenized assets
AI infrastructure boom raises financial concerns
The launch comes as companies renting out AI computing power face questions about whether they can recover the cost of building and operating GPU infrastructure.
Research firm Gartner warned in October that more than 80% of specialist AI cloud providers, known as neoclouds, could cease operating independently by 2030 as they struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.
Elon Musk echoed those concerns Sunday, saying more than 200 neocloud providers could face failure or consolidation as lenders become reluctant to finance companies dependent on AI data center revenue.
Musk has financial interests in the sector through SpaceX, whose “Super Intelligence” business recently reported $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 830% year over year, partly driven by new cloud services agreements.
Source: Elon Musk
Meanwhile, major technology companies are restructuring their operations to contain costs as they pour billions of dollars into AI infrastructure.
On Monday, Bloomberg reported that Microsoft, which has forecast roughly $175 billion in capital expenditures for 2026, is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees as it seeks to reduce costs amid rising AI infrastructure spending.
Meta, which has already invested more than $100 billion in AI, cut 8,000 jobs in May as part of a restructuring aimed at reducing costs.
Magazine: AI agents help rescue ETH’s Glamsterdam fork, ‘Steal My Bitcoin’ site: Hodler’s Digest

articles.title: Unitree Stock Jumps as Investors Bet Chatbot AI Will Finally Give Robots a Brain - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Unitree shares have risen about two-thirds since Oct. 15, closing at 672 yuan on Monday and lifting the Chinese robot maker's market value to 271.8 billion yuan ($40.8 billion).
- Founder Wang Xingxing said at an Oct. 22 conference that large models will break through in physical AI within one to three years, and that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra can already direct robots with zero training.
- JPMorgan upgraded Unitree to overweight from underweight on Oct. 26 and raised its price target.
Shares of Chinese robot maker Unitree Robotics have jumped more than 60% since Oct. 15, lifting its market value to 271.8 billion yuan (roughly $40.8 billion). Investors are betting that smarter AI will give its robots the brains they lack.
The wager is that the technology behind chatbots can soon operate machines in the physical world, a field called physical AI. If it can, a robot that tidies a room or folds laundry on command stops being a lab demo, and the companies that build the bodies, motors, and joints profit.
Unitree founder Wang Xingxing fueled the rally on Oct. 22 at the World Physical AI Conference in Hangzhou, the company's first partner conference in a decade of operation. He said large models, the chatbot-style AI systems trained on vast amounts of data, could break through in physical AI within a few years.
“If everything goes well, it will take one to two years, otherwise it will take two to three years,” Wang said.
Unitree shares hit the 20% daily limit on Friday, the most a stock may rise in one session, and closed at 624 yuan ($93.55). They rose another 7.69% on Monday to 672 yuan ($100.75).
JPMorgan upgraded Unitree to overweight from underweight on Monday, which is analyst shorthand for owning more of a stock than the market does, and raised its price target to 995 yuan ($149.17). The bank had argued the company leaned too heavily on hardware and was weak in software. It changed its view after hearing from Wang and other executives and reviewing the humanoid lineup in Hangzhou.
Unitree went public on Aug. 19 on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market, a tech-focused board. Its G1 humanoid costs roughly $16,000, cheaper than rival humanoids. Researchers have flagged security flaws, including audio, video and spatial data streaming to outside servers without users being notified but the premise has proven interesting enough to push its valuation up.
Unitree already sells robots, while Tesla has only just started producing Optimus robots at its Fremont, California, factory and expects outside deliveries around the end of 2027. Figure AI partnered with OpenAI on its humanoids back in 2024, using OpenAI’s models to power its robots.

articles.title: Canada Opens Consultation Under Stablecoin Act, Expecting Implementation in 2027
articles.text:
Canada opens consultation on stablecoins, citing US GENIUS Act
As part of the potential implementation of its Stablecoin Act, the Canadian government will hear from the public on a proposed framework for tokens from non-financial institutions.
Lawmakers in the Canadian government opened a 60-day public consultation on regulations proposed to address non-financial institution stablecoin issuers, including a potential prohibition on yield payments.
On Saturday, the government of Canada gave notice that it would be open to public comment on the stablecoin regulations until Dec. 23. The proposed framework cited efforts to be consistent with stablecoin regulations in the United States and other jurisdictions, to “reduce the overall regulatory burden on multi-jurisdictional issuers.”
Notably, the proposed regulations said that non-financial institution stablecoin issuers would be restricted from offering interest or yield to discourage HODLing the tokens. They would also be required to redeem stablecoins within three business days of requests from tokenholders, and not charge a fee greater than 1% of the coins’ total value.
The regulations fell under Canada’s Stablecoin Act, which was passed in March and intended to address non-financial institution issuers. According to the government, the proposed rules were required to enact the policy and include provisions for issuers to register with Canada’s central bank.
“The intention is for the proposed Regulations to come into force in fall 2027,” said the government. “Once the proposed Regulations are in effect, issuers of stablecoins in Canada who are not financial institutions would be required to apply for registration with the Bank of Canada prior to issuing a stablecoin.”
The GENIUS Act, which establishes a regulatory framework for stablecoins in the US, is scheduled to take effect in January 2027. Meanwhile, the European Union’s regulations, Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA), could give exchanges until January to halt services for stablecoins not in compliance with the framework, likely including Tether’s USDt (USDT), the largest stablecoin by market capitalization.
Related: Bank of Canada lays out criteria for ‘good money’ stablecoins

articles.title: NBA Embraces the CFTC on Prediction Markets as the NFL Fights It in Court - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- The CFTC and NBA signed a memorandum of understanding to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets, agreeing to share information and flag abuses like insider trading and fraud.
- The NBA joins MLB and NHL in partnering with the regulator.
- It lands amid a federal-vs-state jurisdiction fight—the CFTC is defining event contracts as “swaps,” the NFL is battling Kalshi at the Supreme Court and has balked at signing on.
The NBA has struck a deal with the top U.S. derivatives regulator to help police prediction markets, becoming the latest major sports league to formalize an integrity partnership as betting on games moves onto federally regulated platforms.
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Monday it signed a memorandum of understanding with the basketball league to protect the integrity of professional basketball in prediction markets.
Under the agreement, the two will share information and communicate regularly on integrity matters while working to keep the markets fair and transparent.
“The NBA joins the MLB and NHL in taking a responsible step toward protecting sports integrity and market participants from abuses in prediction markets like insider trading and fraud,” CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said in a statement, thanking Commissioner Adam Silver for prioritizing “the integrity of professional basketball and America’s financial markets.”
The pact reflects how quickly sports-outcome betting has migrated to CFTC-regulated venues like Kalshi and Polymarket, which let users trade “event contracts” on real-world outcomes, including who wins a given game.
That shift has raised integrity concerns familiar to the gambling world, chiefly the risk that insiders could trade on nonpublic information. The league-regulator MOUs are meant to build a channel for flagging suspicious activity, following the NHL’s move to become the first major league to license its trademarks to a prediction market and MLB’s integrity agreement tied to a Polymarket deal.
The NBA is a pointed addition, given the league is still reeling from one of the biggest betting scandals in recent memory. An October 2025 FBI operation led to the arrest of Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier and a coach over alleged involvement in gambling schemes, including one centered on manipulating game outcomes to influence bets. The case put a spotlight on exactly the kind of insider misconduct these partnerships are meant to catch, making the NBA’s cooperation with the CFTC especially resonant.
The partnership also lands amid a fierce jurisdictional fight over whether these markets fall under federal or state authority.
The CFTC recently moved to define event contracts as “swaps” squarely within its remit while excluding casino-style gambling, and a court battle pitting the NFL against Kalshi has drawn the Supreme Court’s attention. Notably, the NFL has so far balked at signing on, making the NBA’s cooperation a contrast among the major leagues.
The stakes are only growing. Analysts at Bernstein have projected prediction markets could generate billions in revenue by the end of the decade, and new entrants keep arriving, with Blockchain.com among the latest to seek CFTC approval to offer event contracts.

articles.title: Anthropic Files S-1 Registration for IPO, Expected in November
articles.text:
AI company Anthropic announces IPO, expected as early as November
The artificial intelligence company disclosed more than $16 billion in revenue and an $80 billion net loss for the first half of 2026.
Anthropic announced that it had filed S-1 registration with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for an initial public offering on Nasdaq, marking a significant step for artificial intelligence companies.
A Monday S-1 filing with the SEC suggested that Anthropic could be aiming for a mid-November IPO, listing its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol ANT. The company disclosed more than $16 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026 and an $80 billion net loss over the same period.
Anthropic was founded in 2021 by many former executives of AI company OpenAI. Reports have suggested that the company could raise up to $100 billion for an IPO, giving it a $2 trillion valuation. OpenAI has already delayed its own IPO plans, with CEO Sam Altman reportedly saying in September that 2026 was an “ill-advised moment” to pursue a public offering.
The company behind the AI assistant Claude reported holding more than $112 billion in cash and cash equivalents, along with $19 billion in short-term investments, as of June 30.

articles.title: South Korea Arrests Seven in First Big AI-Assisted Hacking Case - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Seoul police arrested seven people over a campaign that used generative AI to hack about 90 organizations and steal 8.2 million records, which police call South Korea’s first large-scale AI-assisted hacking arrests.
- The alleged ringleader, 32, taught himself hacking and added an AI coding agent and an autonomous penetration-testing tool in late August; police say he breached 60 companies in 44 days.
- Emails to 38 victims demanded a combined 360 million won, about $272,000, but the only confirmed payment was 300,000 won, about $210.
Police in Seoul have arrested seven people in a hacking campaign that used generative AI to break into about 90 organizations and steal 8.2 million records.
The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case Monday and called it the first time in South Korea that suspects in a large-scale AI-assisted hacking operation have been apprehended.
The targets included hospitals, universities, private cram schools, golf courses and subsidiaries of large conglomerates, according to police—places that hold the names, contact details and records of ordinary people. One funeral services provider lost 1.22 million records, and one report said data from the academies included information on minors.
The alleged ringleader is a 32-year-old who studied arts and physical education and has no IT background, per local reports. He told investigators he taught himself hacking through YouTube and online blogs, though police say he also did simulated attack work at a security company from 2019 to 2022.
He started with website vulnerability scanners, software that probes a site for weak spots. In late August, reports say, he added an AI coding agent—a program that writes and runs code on its own—and an autonomous penetration-testing system, a tool that automates the mock break-ins companies normally hire experts to run. Police say he then breached 60 companies in 44 days, from August 31 to October 13.
Police said an attack of this size once required a hacking group, and that AI now lets one person pull it off in a short time. Local reports name the autonomous tool as Artex. The campaign ran about 13 months, from September 2025 through this October, and the case opened in June after one victim filed a complaint.
Criminal use of AI has been building for years, mostly in reports from AI companies rather than police. WormGPT, a ChatGPT clone built without safety guardrails, was used in 2023 to write convincing phishing emails—fake messages designed to trick people into handing over money or passwords.
In August 2025, Anthropic said a single criminal used its Claude Code tool to run a vibe hacking extortion campaign against at least 17 organizations, with ransom demands from $75,000 to $500,000 in Bitcoin. In November, the company said a Chinese state-sponsored group used Claude to carry out 80% to 90% of an espionage campaign against about 30 targets, though only a small number of the intrusions succeeded.
Researchers at Cambridge, Edinburgh, and Strathclyde universities pushed back on the hype in a recent study of 97,895 cybercrime forum threads. They found AI’s main impact so far in already-automated areas such as SEO fraud, social media bots and romance scams, with little sign that coding tools helped low-skill actors beyond pre-made scripts.
The ringleader was referred to prosecutors in custody on Friday and faces charges under South Korea’s information and communications network law, plus extortion and attempted extortion. Police said they will keep investigating the six accomplices and try to identify additional victims, and 15 organizations have reported damage so far.

articles.title: NBA Expands Prediction Market Access Amid Legal Battles
articles.text:
NBA names Kalshi, Polymarket preferred exchanges, signs CFTC deal
The US professional basketball league is expanding into prediction markets with official data agreements and safeguards against insider trading.
The National Basketball Association has named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction market exchanges and signed an information-sharing agreement with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) aimed at protecting the integrity of basketball-related markets.
According to Monday’s announcement, the agreements will give Kalshi and Polymarket access to official NBA data supplied by Sportradar, the league’s designated data distribution partner, for settling authorized markets. Both platforms will have rights to use NBA intellectual property and conduct promotional activities in the United States.
The partnerships include integrity safeguards, prohibiting NBA and team personnel from trading NBA event contracts and requiring cooperation on suspicious trading investigations.
Beyond the two exchanges, the NBA expanded its existing agreement with DraftKings to cover prediction markets and said it expects to announce similar arrangements with other industry operators in the coming weeks.
In a separate announcement, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig said the agreement with the NBA would strengthen information sharing to address insider trading and fraud in prediction markets. The NBA joins Major League Baseball and the National Hockey League in establishing similar arrangements with the regulator.
Related: Kalshi strikes deal with S&P Dow Jones Indices to expand financial event contracts
States challenge federal oversight of prediction markets
The NBA’s agreements come amid an ongoing legal battle over whether federal commodities rules supersede state gambling laws governing sports prediction markets.
The dispute has produced conflicting court decisions. In September, the 6th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled against Kalshi in a case involving Ohio and Tennessee, following a similar decision by the 9th Circuit. An earlier ruling by the 3rd Circuit, however, allowed Kalshi to continue operating in New Jersey while its appeal proceeds.
State enforcement actions have continued. On Oct. 20, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown sued Kalshi, alleging that the platform had facilitated illegal betting in the state since 2024. Utah officials are seeking to recover an estimated $30 million to $60 million in profits allegedly earned by Kalshi and other defendants.
Kalshi event contract. Source: Kalshi
The US Supreme Court has been asked to review the New Jersey dispute, with 39 states and Washington, DC, supporting the petition. The National Football League, which has not entered into commercial partnerships with prediction market exchanges, also backed the petition, arguing that certain sports event contracts threaten game integrity because they are susceptible to manipulation. The justices have not yet agreed to hear the case.

articles.title: AI Agents Found a Way Into Anthropic's Business Systems in Under 12 Hours - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Cathedral says AI agents found paths into Anthropic's internal systems in less than 12 hours by exploiting weaknesses in third-party administrative and sales software.
- Anthropic confirmed access to a limited set of sales, HR and IT systems, but says customer conversations, Claude responses, source code and model weights were not reached.
- Anthropic says Cathedral overstated the national security implications and did not disclose all of its testing; Cathedral says it kept data access to the absolute minimum.
Researchers at a cybersecurity startup said AI agents found paths into Anthropic's business systems in less than 12 hours, according to a Washington Post report published Monday.
The way in was not Claude, Anthropic's AI assistant, but third-party administrative and sales software, the kind of programs companies use to track customers and manage staff. Many other companies use the same software.
The startup, Cathedral, was founded months ago by four former staffers of the Department of Government Efficiency, the Donald Trump administration's cost-cutting team better known as DOGE. The startup raised $160 million at a $1.4 billion valuation in July.
Cathedral tested Anthropic through a program that works like a bug bounty, in which a company rewards outside experts for reporting flaws instead of exploiting them. Its AI agents, which carry out multi-step tasks without a person approving each move, found routes to meeting transcripts, salary and job-offer details, and Slack messages about Anthropic's advanced models, per a draft of its report.
“Our monitoring flagged some of Cathedral's activity before they reported it to us,” Anthropic told the Washington Post, “we shut off their access the same day.” The company says the researchers reached “a limited set” of sales, HR, and IT systems holding business contact details and basic user account records.
Customer conversations with Claude, source code and model weights, the billions of numbers that make up the trained AI, were not accessed, Anthropic said. It has no evidence that anyone other than Cathedral exploited the flaws.
Anthropic said Cathedral overstated the national security implications and did not fully follow the program's rules because it did not disclose all of its activity. Cathedral's draft report said “data accesses were kept to the absolute minimum in accordance with security research best practices.”
A senior Trump administration official, speaking anonymously, said the report has circulated in government and raised national security concerns. “If a bunch of kids who have just started a company can do this,” the official said, “then potentially, the Chinese aren't far behind.”
In November 2025, Anthropic said Chinese state-sponsored hackers used Claude Code, its coding tool, to attack roughly 30 organizations, with AI handling 80% to 90% of the tactical work. In July, Anthropic disclosed that Claude models had hacked real organizations in three incidents during its tests.
Anthropic disabled the affected software until the vendors confirmed fixes, and the vendors have not been named.

articles.title: South Korea Weighs Another Delay on 22% Crypto Tax, Pushing to 2029
articles.text:
South Korea lawmakers mull pushing crypto tax implementation to 2029
The Seoul government is reportedly weighing another delay for a 2020 income tax policy on digital assets, citing concerns with receiving data from US officials.
Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing a delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently expected to be implemented in January 2027.
According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.
The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains — 20% from income and 2% as part of a local tax — for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually has already seen several delays since it was first proposed in 2020.
“We are discussing postponing the implementation of virtual asset taxation,” said an official from the Blue House presidential residence.
The US is scheduled to begin participating in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in 2029, while South Korea will implement the rules starting in 2027. A South Korean official reportedly said that the country was considering another delay for the crypto tax as the US “accounts for nearly half of the virtual asset market.”
As of Monday, South Korea’s National Tax Service listed Jan. 1, 2027 as the start date for the crypto tax.
Related: France advances stablecoin tax, eyes self-custodial wallets and exit tax proposals

articles.title: Why Prediction Markets Got the Brazilian Election So Wrong - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Polymarket priced Lula at about a 20% chance of victory before Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, but beat Flávio Bolsonaro to win a fourth term.
- One whale blamed retail traders for propping up Bolsonaro's odds, while other experts pointed to Brazil's prediction market ban.
- Ultimately though, experts say that something with an 80% chance of happening won't happen 20% of the time—and this just might be that time.
Prediction markets got the results of Brazil's presidential election wildly wrong, with Polymarket putting Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's chances at just 20% before election day, when he ultimately won out.
Experts say the whiff is the result of Brazil banning prediction markets in the country and a wave of retail investors diluting the expertise of the money on the line.
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, commonly referred to as Lula, beat right-wing rival Flávio Bolsonaro in the Brazilian presidential election on Sunday. Bolsonaro came out ahead after the first round of voting at the start of October, but hadn't reached a majority, and a second round of votes was required. That second round is what Lula won, with a majority this time, and he will serve his fourth term as president.
Going into election day, Lula hovered around a 20% chance of victory with Bolsonaro sitting at 80%, per Polymarket. Even once polls and results started to roll out, one Polymarket whale told Decrypt that the market was slow to push up the odds.
"Sharps [a term for professional, high-stakes predictors] knew the market was mispriced, probably closer to 30-40% on [event] day. Mispricing was most evident during live trading, Lula was nearly a lock by 6:15 pm ET when Lula ‘Yes’ was 60c," pseudonymous Polymarket whale FhantomBets said. "Retail traders were so against Lula that you could get unlimited size at 60-80c when Lula had [essentially] already won."
Prediction markets settle at $1, with prices below that—such as $0.60 on a “yes” bet for Lula in Brazil’s election—providing implied odds of that event occurring.
The Polymarket trader added that many whales, including himself, were selling off long-term positions to get liquid capital so they could add more size to the Brazil market. Essentially, FhantomBets is claiming that retail traders with less prediction market experience inflated Bolsonaro's chances right until the very end.
Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, pushed back on this notion and said Polymarket results reacted as polling results were released throughout the night.
"I don’t think more users are inherently a problem. They can bring liquidity and different perspectives, including local knowledge. What matters is whether participation brings different information, and whether traders can act on it," Nolan told Decrypt. "I would be wary of explaining the result simply as professionals being right and retail being wrong."
Instead, Nolan suggested Brazil’s ban on prediction markets is likely a bigger reason why the market was so harshly mispriced. Einar Knobel, CEO and co-founder of sportsbook and prediction market firm TxODDS, agreed.
"The price was set mostly by people outside the country," Knobel told Decrypt. "They were trading the first-round result, poll headlines, and the story built around them."
Brazil issued a sweeping ban against prediction market platforms in April, citing investor protection concerns and the rise of gambling addiction in the nation. Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the platforms violated betting regulations and lacked proper regulatory oversight.
Knobel added that liquidity was also relatively thin, with the market attracting just 4.5% of the volume that the 2024 U.S. presidential election garnered. "With fewer participants and almost no local knowledge in the book, little was there to correct the price," Knobel said.
Nolan believes predictors put too much weight on Bolsonaro's first-round performance, underestimated the increase in voter turnout for the second round, and assumed how voters would transfer based on the eliminated candidates.
"That said, Lula was priced at around 20% before the vote," Nolan said. "That is still some form of meaningful chance of winning. I think there are good reasons to question whether the market underestimated him. Ultimately, something that has an 80% chance of happening does not happen 20% of the time."
The mispricing of the Brazilian election was a significant upset, but Nolan cautioned against seeing it as a massive failure. He said prediction markets continue to price things better than traditional betting platforms—pointing to Betfair giving Hillary Clinton an 83% chance the day before the 2016 U.S. election.
"Across enough events, outcomes given a 20% chance should happen roughly 20% of the time. We should also compare their performance with other forecasts available at the same time," Nolan told Decrypt. "The concern would be a persistent pattern of overconfidence or a failure to incorporate relevant information, rather than an individual upset."

articles.title: Kalshi, S&P Dow Jones Partner on Prediction Market Indexes
articles.text:
Kalshi strikes deal with S&P Dow Jones Indices to expand financial event contracts
The agreement adds S&P Dow Jones gauges to a growing list of Wall Street firms expanding their involvement in prediction markets.
S&P Dow Jones Indices has partnered with prediction market platform Kalshi in a deal that will allow the exchange to offer event contracts tied to the financial index provider’s benchmarks.
According to Monday’s announcement, Kalshi will become a preferred platform for contracts linked to S&P DJI indices, with settlement based on official index values published by the company.
S&P DJI will also explore developing indexes using Kalshi’s prediction market data, potentially tracking expectations around economic developments, political outcomes and sporting events. The gauges would use prices from Kalshi’s event contracts to measure market expectations about future outcomes, rather than tracking the performance of traditional financial assets.
The companies did not disclose a timeline for either initiative. S&P DJI did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s request for additional details.
Related: Utah AG sues Kalshi, pursues profits from prediction market company
The agreement follows moves by traditional financial market operators into prediction markets. Intercontinental Exchange, parent of the New York Stock Exchange, committed up to $2 billion to Polymarket in October 2025.
In March, Nasdaq filed to offer prediction market-style contracts tied to the Nasdaq 100 Index, before partnering with Kalshi in August to provide market surveillance technology.
S&P Global completes OpenZeppelin acquisition
S&P Dow Jones Indices parent, S&P Global, separately announced Monday that it completed its acquisition of blockchain security firm OpenZeppelin, expanding its risk assessment capabilities for digital assets. The deal was first announced in September and financial terms were not disclosed.
OpenZeppelin provides smart contract security audits and development tools. Its open-source contract libraries underpin more than $38 trillion in value transferred, while its security team has conducted over 900 engagements, according to S&P Global.
OpenZeppelin will continue operating as its own business unit under founder Demian Brener, who will report to Yann Le Pallec, president of S&P Global Ratings.
S&P Global has also expanded its digital asset risk assessment work beyond smart contract security. Earlier this month, S&P Global Ratings launched a framework for evaluating crypto lending vaults across six risk categories, including blockchain security, liquidity and governance.

articles.title: SpaceX Locks Up $40 Billion for AI Chips as Musk Warns Most Neoclouds Will Die - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- SpaceX signed a binding commitment letter for about $40 billion of GPU leases from an Apollo-managed entity, with leases starting in the first half of 2027 and the master lease expected to close before the end of 2026.
- Musk said debt markets have almost entirely shut off money to companies without substantial revenue outside AI data centers, and predicted "guppy-level death and consolidation" among the 200+ neoclouds.
- Investor Chamath Palihapitiya forecast a turbulent 2027 with more idle or underused AI computing power than expected, while CoreWeave's unsecured bonds yielded about 15% in mid-October.
SpaceX said it has closed a $40 billion financing deal to buy AI chips for its data centers. Elon Musk used the announcement to warn that lenders have almost entirely cut off money to companies that depend on AI data centers for their revenue.
The financing covers GPUs, the graphics processors that train and run AI models, for SpaceX, which absorbed xAI in February. According to a regulatory filing, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, an investment firm that lends directly to companies instead of going through banks, will buy the chips and lease them to SpaceX.
Musk called it debt, but the filing describes a finance lease, a long-term rental that works like a loan. SpaceX would repay about $40 billion in principal through quarterly installments over roughly five years, plus interest at a fixed rate that has not been set. The chips arrive in batches, with leases starting in the first half of 2027.
“As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers,” Musk wrote on X. “SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.”
Pretty much.
As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers.
SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch…
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 25, 2026
Investment grade is a credit rating telling lenders a borrower is unlikely to miss payments, and Moody's rated SpaceX Baa1, an investment-grade level, in June. Starlink is SpaceX's satellite internet business, and both it and the rocket launches bring in revenue that has nothing to do with AI.
“That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation,” Musk added. “Some will make it through, but not many.”
Neoclouds are specialist companies that rent out GPU capacity to AI developers. The largest, CoreWeave, began in 2017 by mining Ethereum with graphics cards before pivoting to AI after the network retired mining in 2022.
CoreWeave's shares fell about 30% between September 30 and October 16, from $87 to $61, and the company carries roughly $50 billion in debt. Its unsecured bonds, meaning loans with no specific assets pledged as backup, yielded about 15% in mid-October, so investors demanded roughly 15% a year to lend to it.
The weakness is that chips lose value fast while the loans last for years. CoreWeave booked nearly $1.4 billion in depreciation and amortization, the accounting charge for hardware wearing out, in the second quarter against about $2.6 billion in revenue.
Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, told the firm's markets conference on October 20 that GPUs resemble airline seats as both cost almost nothing to add once they exist, so prices can collapse when supply outruns demand.
Venture capitalist and entrepreneur Chamath Palihapitiya expects more AI computing power to sit idle in 2027 than forecasts assume. “There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027,” he wrote on X. “Hyperscalers will (obviously) react by focusing on their own internal compute needs over any third party.”
Hyperscalers are the cloud giants such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Palihapitiya said the stranded hardware is bought and paid for but earns less than it costs to finance, a problem he said holds across the industry with one exception he did not name.
“2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets,” Palihapitiya wrote. “It will also be a consolidation year for a few.”
SpaceX said it expects to finalize the master finance lease before the end of 2026, and the interest rate on the roughly $40 billion in leases has yet to be determined.

articles.title: PHP Flaw Shows AI ‘Vulnerability Apocalypse’ on Schedule: Immunefi CEO
articles.text:
PHP flaw shows AI ‘vulnerability apocalypse’ is on schedule: Immunefi CEO
Mitchell Amador warned internet users that websites could remain compromised for weeks, particularly smaller websites slower to adopt the emergency upgrades.
Internet users are still vulnerable to cyber exploits stemming from the PHP vulnerability, particularly through smaller websites that could take weeks to adopt the upgrade shipped last Wednesday, according to bug bounty platform Immunefi CEO Mitchell Amador.
“This is the vulnerability apocalypse” running on schedule, where finding vulnerabilities became cheap, but fixing them remains expensive, Amador told Cointelegraph.
“For the next few weeks, treat any site you log into as if it could already be compromised,” said Amador, warning users to avoid reusing passwords and to exercise caution when connecting their cryptocurrency wallets to websites. He also urged users to revoke unrecognized token approvals.
The comments come nearly a week after the PHP Foundation acknowledged that it delayed fixing a critical security flaw first identified in 2024, due to a shortage of resources. PHP developers released emergency patches for two critical vulnerabilities on the same day, but websites still need to independently upgrade.
In an interview published by Cointelegraph in June, Amador warned that the proliferation of frontier AI models changed the cybersecurity playing field in favor of attackers, causing a “vulnerability apocalypse” that led to the resurgence in decentralized finance (DeFi) hacks.
Percentage of programs with a confirmed critical vulnerability by time live. 
Source: Immunefi
Immunefi is the world’s largest bug bounty platform that paid out $140 million in bounties across 650 protocols to date, according to its homepage.
Related: Cysic dangles a 10% bounty, hacker pours loot into Tornado Cash
PHP flaw drew millions of exploit attempts within hours
According to Cloudflare’s CEO Matthew Prince, the network saw millions of exploit attempts in the 24 hours after the PHP vulnerabilities were publicly revealed and thousands of attempts even before their disclosure, he wrote a Thursday X post.
About one in five websites worldwide routes traffic through Cloudflare, according to the internet infrastructure company, which helps websites load faster and protect users from cyber threats.
Research service W3Techs estimates that PHP powers about 69% of websites with a known server-side programming language. The vulnerabilities may allow attackers to spread malware or inject malicious scripts into websites around the world.
The FBI’s Cyber Division also warned that the vulnerabilities may allow malicious actors to “remotely execute code in PHP core, potentially compromising sensitive data and networks,” according to a Wednesday X post.

articles.title: Bitcoin Wallet Fixes Critical Flaw That Redirected Funds to Attackers - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin wallet Electrum released version 4.8.3 on October 24 with a patch for a high-severity exploit that let malicious servers inject fake transactions and trick users into paying attacker addresses.
- At least one user confirmed losing funds on October 18 after fee-bumping a server-manipulated transaction.
- The fix verifies signatures on wallet-owned inputs before displaying unconfirmed transactions, but incoming transactions from external senders remain unverified.
Bitcoin wallet Electrum patched a high-severity vulnerability this weekend that allowed rogue servers to manipulate pending Bitcoin transactions and redirect funds to attacker-controlled addresses. The flaw affects all versions before 4.8.3, which is now available.
At least one user has confirmed losing money to the exploit.
Electrum is one of the oldest Bitcoin software wallets around. The attack exploits the wallet’s trust model for unconfirmed transactions. When a user broadcasts a payment through a compromised server, the server can suppress the real transaction and inject a fake conflicting one—showing an attacker’s output address and zero fee, making the payment look stuck.
Because Electrum doesn’t verify signatures on unconfirmed transactions from the server, the spoofed transaction appears in the wallet’s history as legitimate.
When the user fee-bumps what looks like a stalled payment, they sign and broadcast a completely new valid transaction—one whose output address belongs to the attacker. The real payment was never sent; the fee-bump is the first transaction that actually hits the network, and it pays the attacker.
Electrum developer SomberNight, who published the advisory, noted that attackers can grind the fake transaction’s output address to match the last four characters of the user’s intended destination. Anyone spot-checking only the tail of a long Bitcoin address would see an apparent match.
The advisory states that “some servers are performing this attack in the wild,” backed by two user reports. A user identified as dannydeezy first flagged the suspicious server behavior on October 11; the manipulated transaction never propagated past the local server, so no funds were lost. A second user, Raju-K12, reported a confirmed loss on October 18 after fee-bumping a manipulated transaction.
The patch in 4.8.3 closes the main attack surface by verifying cryptographic signatures on wallet-owned inputs before adding any unconfirmed transaction to local history. A server can no longer inject a fake transaction touching the user’s own addresses without providing valid signatures—which the attacker cannot forge. The fix was tagged in the repository on October 23 and binaries were published the following day.
Incoming transactions from external senders—where none of the inputs belong to the user’s wallet—are still accepted without signature verification. SomberNight acknowledged this gap in the advisory, noting it would require additional work to close.
This isn’t Electrum’s first rodeo and it has dealt with malicious attacks in the past. A 2018 campaign used rogue servers to push fake update notifications, and by 2020 it had drained an estimated $25 million from Electrum users. Electrum’s open server model—anyone can run a node—is what makes this class of attack possible.
Users who connect exclusively to a server they run themselves are not affected. Anyone who cannot update immediately should manually verify output addresses and amounts before signing any transaction; Electrum 4.8.3 is available at electrum.org alongside the project’s Github.

articles.title: India’s CoinDCX Confirms $16 Million Loss Days After CEO Called It a ‘False Alarm’ - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- CoinDCX confirmed it lost 15.99 million USDT (~$16 million) after an internal process failed to sweep customer deposits out of wallets it retired following a 2025 hack.
- The admission reversed CEO Sumit Gupta’s earlier claim that breach reports were a “false alarm.”
- It brings CoinDCX’s losses across two incidents to nearly $60 million, following the roughly $44 million hack last year.
Indian crypto exchange CoinDCX has admitted it lost about $16 million in an attack on its wallet infrastructure, reversing its co-founder’s earlier insistence that reports of a breach were a “false alarm.”
In a blog post, the Mumbai-based exchange said 15.99 million USDT was drained and that it has absorbed the loss itself, stressing that customer funds remain safe.
The money moved on the Tron network on Oct. 21, and the company traced the incident to a failure in an internal process meant to sweep customer deposits out of wallets it had retired after a far larger hack last year.
The disclosure caps an awkward few days for the exchange. When blockchain researchers and the Arkham tracker first flagged roughly $16 million in suspicious outflows, CEO Sumit Gupta pushed back on X, writing that CoinDCX’s wallets were “not breached” and that the flagged addresses had been compromised back in July 2025, making the activity look like “a false alarm.”
On-chain investigator ZachXBT disputed that account, noting the wallet in question had still been sweeping user deposits into CoinDCX’s current hot wallet as recently as April and May, and he urged customers to withdraw their assets.
Withdraw all funds from CoinDCX if you value your assets.
Its co-founders are clowns running a circus.
They publicly and privately denied a theft of its assets occurred meaning they straight up lied or are negligently incompetent.
Later they disclosed the $16M theft and… pic.twitter.com/uEmtogPonq
— ZachXBT (@zachxbt) October 22, 2026
The loss compounds a tumultuous stretch for one of India’s largest exchanges. CoinDCX suffered a roughly $44 million hack in July 2025 that it blamed on a server breach, prompting a bounty hunt for the stolen funds and, later, the arrest of an employee over the incident.
Together, the two episodes bring the exchange’s losses to nearly $60 million.
The retired wallets at the center of the new loss were themselves a legacy of that earlier breach, addresses the exchange had stopped using but which kept receiving residual deposits. The failure of an automated transfer system to clear them out left the funds exposed.
CoinDCX has weathered other turbulence this year. The exchange faced fraud and impersonation-scam allegations that drew a police probe, while its founder denied reports of acquisition talks with Coinbase following the 2025 hack. Coinbase has separately moved to expand across South Asia and the Middle East.
The exchange said it would share further details as its investigation continues, and reiterated that user balances are unaffected.

articles.title: 3 payment rules control Aave’s native Bitcoin market, but only WBTC settles them
articles.text:
Quick Take
- LlamaRisk’s pre-listing review says Babylon’s proposed Aave integration retains WBTC payment dependencies even when keepers bypass Hub funding.
- Zero application fees and no borrower surplus still leave WBTC repayment obligations when the borrower’s debt is denominated in WBTC.
- Published addresses checked Oct. 25 still identify Sepolia testnet.
Babylon Labs’ proposed native Bitcoin lending market on Aave V4 would still need Wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) for its direct-liquidation fallback whenever application fees or borrower compensation are due.
An operator with the vault’s Bitcoin redemption rights could bypass Aave’s shared lending pool yet still be unable to complete a liquidation if those WBTC payments cannot move.
The distinction comes from risk assessor LlamaRisk’s Oct. 23 pre-listing assessment. The direct route can avoid the funding constraint of running out of WBTC lending capacity by having an authorized keeper finance the liquidation itself. Required payment failures can affect both routes.
If the borrower owes WBTC, the keeper must transfer WBTC to repay the loan even when the application fee and borrower-surplus payment are zero.
The assessment said the integration contracts had not been deployed on Ethereum mainnet. Babylon’s contract directory, checked Oct. 25, identifies its published addresses as Sepolia testnet deployments.
Two routes, three payment requirements
A borrower’s native BTC would remain in a Bitcoin vault, and Aave would recognize that collateral through a restricted internal ERC-20 accounting record, which users cannot trade as a wrapped Bitcoin token.
Through the proposed Liquidation Liquidity Provider (LLP) route, an outside liquidator would repay the borrower’s debt and receive an immediate WBTC payout.
The settlement component, BTCVaultSwap (the Swap Spoke), would place the seized vault in escrow and draw the payout from Aave’s shared liquidity pool (the Hub). The underlying BTC would remain on Bitcoin.
An authorized keeper acting as an arbitrageur would then be expected to buy the escrowed vault and handle redemption on Bitcoin. The process depends on a willing eligible buyer completing that purchase.
The Babylon proposal also describes a direct route for keepers with the vault’s committed Bitcoin redemption rights. Such a keeper would fund debt repayment and take the seized vault into redemption without the Swap Spoke’s new Hub-funded payout or its escrow step.
When the Hub WBTC allowance runs out, a keeper able to supply the required payment assets can avoid that funding constraint. However, the pool of available participants would narrow to operators equipped and authorized to claim the underlying Bitcoin.
Babylon’s liquidation operator guide says it collects debt repayment and two additional charges: the application liquidation fee and any fairness payment owed to the borrower. For direct liquidation, both additional charges are denominated in WBTC and funded by the caller.
The debt repayment uses the token of the borrower’s selected debt reserve. The adapter pulls the repayment input and refunds whatever Aave’s lending contract does not consume. The repayment input is separate from the caller’s limit on additional WBTC payments.
The keeper therefore needs assets for the debt, the fee, and any surplus payment. Its own inventory supplies funding outside the Hub, subject to each required token transfer working.
The assessment describes the Babylon application fee as 0.5% of liquidation bonus profit. The assessed design separately forces the Babylon lending Spoke’s own liquidation fee to zero while retaining the application fee at the adapter.
For the direct route to avoid the stated WBTC fee and surplus obligations in LlamaRisk’s transfer-failure scenario, the application liquidation fee must be zero and no fairness payment can be due. Those conditions address only those two payments.
A WBTC loan still needs WBTC repayment even in that exception. For a loan in another asset, repayment uses that asset, while the keeper still needs transferable debt tokens, redemption rights, and functioning liquidation contracts.
Setting the application fee to zero would itself require a time-locked Babylon application-parameter change. LlamaRisk places liquidationFeeBps changes behind the application timelock, separately from immediate emergency pause and freeze controls.
The fee-specific delay remains unspecified in the assessment, so an individual keeper has to use the effective fee setting, including any WBTC charge still due when it acts.
Whole vaults can create a WBTC surplus
The fairness payment follows from the way the collateral is held, while partial-position liquidation can seize some of a borrower’s vaults while leaving others in place. Each seized Bitcoin vault is indivisible.
Under the model described in the Oct. 23 assessment, the governance proposal and the operator guide, each liquidation call targets the first whole vault in the borrower’s ordered list. If the liquidator must liquidate multiple vaults, it checks the position’s health again.
If the borrower’s entire debt is cleared before the selected vault’s value is consumed, the liquidator still receives the entire vault. It must compensate the borrower for the remaining WBTC value at the liquidation-bonus discount.
Better sizing of the first vault can reduce the surplus a liquidator must fund while leaving other vaults in the position. Whether a fairness payment arises depends on the debt and collateral valuation at execution.
Partial-position liquidation describes how many vaults are taken, so a borrower-surplus payment can arise even on a direct call that charges no application fee.
Liquidation on Ethereum must also be distinguished from receiving spendable Bitcoin. Direct liquidation initiates an authorized redemption, but the Bitcoin proof-and-challenge process still takes multiple days. On the direct route, the keeper finances that multi-day wait itself.
Babylon’s integration documentation describes removing vaults subject to the remaining position staying healthy. The assessment additionally requires no remaining debt to withdraw every vault. Borrower withdrawals remain subject to those conditions even when a keeper can liquidate.
LlamaRisk recommends an initial 100 WBTC Core Hub credit line for BTCVaultSwap, separately from the proposed 300 BTC collateral launch cap.
The assessment envisages an initial rollout with 10 allowlisted borrowers and 50 vaults. That would be a limited launch alongside permissioned Bitcoin redemption operators.
The lending line would determine how much funding is available for the LLP route. Beyond that line, the direct fallback would rely on keepers repaying the debt and meeting any WBTC fee or borrower-surplus payment.
Final fee settings, debt assets, and vault composition would determine how far that fallback extends.

articles.title: Crypto Today: Robinhood’s Prediction Market, Musk AI warning
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Bernstein analysts said Robinhood’s prediction market earnings could leapfrog crypto, Elon Musk warned that more than 200 AI cloud providers face failure or consolidation as financing tightens and China set a 2030 target for completing its national blockchain network.
HOOD’s prediction markets to exceed crypto by 2028: Bernstein
Bernstein analysts expect prediction markets to become one of the incremental earnings drivers for trading platform Robinhood Markets (HOOD), potentially surpassing its crypto-derived revenue.
Prediction markets could drive up to $1.7 billion in business for Robinhood by 2028, surpassing the projected $1.6 billion in crypto-based revenues for that year, according to a Bernstein analysts’ forecast shared with Cointelegraph on Monday.
The analysts expects Robinhood’s prediction market revenue to increase to $1.7 billion in 2028 from about $650 million this year, accounting for roughly 18% of Robinhood’s projected $9.4 billion in total 2028 revenue.
The forecast comes a day ahead of Robinhood’s third-quarter 2026 report and shows that prediction markets are becoming a growing revenue source for the retail-focused trading platform.
Bernstein expects Robinhood’s Q3 revenue to increase 13% quarter-over-quarter to around $1.5 billion, driven by growing equity notional volumes, options volumes, event contract volumes, along with a recovery in crypto trading volume.
Musk warns over 200 AI neoclouds face ‘guppy-level death’
Elon Musk warns that over 200 specialist AI cloud providers could fail or consolidate as lenders tighten up their purse strings.
Musk said Sunday on X that lenders had largely stopped providing financing to companies without substantial revenue streams outside AI data centers. He said SpaceX had secured $40 billion in debt financing for GPUs because of its investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and rocket businesses.
“That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many,” he said.
Musk’s warning follows an October forecast from research firm Gartner that more than 80% of neocloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030, as the industry struggles to generate sufficient returns on massive AI infrastructure investments.
The warnings could also have implications for Bitcoin miners that have pivoted into AI infrastructure. For example, IREN has expanded into AI cloud services, renting computing power to customers, while Core Scientific provides data center hosting for neocloud customers such as CoreWeave.
China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout
China has set a 2030 target for largely completing a national blockchain network under a five-year digital development plan published Friday.
The 15th Five-Year Plan for National Informatization, which sets priorities calls for deeper blockchain use in trade and finance in the Yangtze River Delta, and deployment at scale in manufacturing and agriculture in the Chengdu–Chongqing region in southwestern China.
Friday’s plan was issued by the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission, a senior body within the ruling Communist Party that coordinates digital development policy.
The document makes the completion target explicit for a project already included in China’s national development plan released in March. A joint policy from the Communist Party’s central leadership and State Council published on Oct. 9 called for its construction.

articles.title: Crypto traders value Anthropic at $1.9 trillion as investor warns its IPO could mark the top of the AI bubble
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq IPO as crypto traders valued the Claude developer near $1.9 trillion ahead of its anticipated November debut.
- Moonrock Capital's Simon Dedic warned the listing could mark the AI bubble's peak while creating one of the largest private-market wealth events.
- The potential windfall could redirect billions into crypto and other markets, but staggered insider lockups complicates that.
Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq IPO Monday, reporting a quarterly operating profit as crypto markets valued it near $2 trillion.
The Claude developer submitted its S-1 registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Oct. 26, seeking a listing under the ticker ANT.
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the offering, which could become one of the largest in US history. Anthropic has not yet disclosed its proposed share price or offering size, though market expectations point to a November debut.
Crypto traders price Claude developer near $2 trillion
Crypto trading platform Liquid reported that Anthropic's implied valuation fell roughly 2% to $1.88 trillion after the announcement.
Meanwhile, Better Markets quoted an indicative pre-IPO share price of $2,967.92, corresponding to an estimated $1.43 trillion valuation under its pricing methodology.
The enormous valuations have divided investors over what Anthropic's public debut could mean for the wider technology sector.
Simon Dedic, founder of Moonrock Capital, said he expects the company to begin trading by mid-November, adding that the listing could mark the “top of the AI bubble” or become one of the largest wealth-creation events in private-market history.
Dedic argued that an offering of this magnitude could release substantial capital accumulated by early investors and employees, potentially redirecting investment toward startups and other markets.
His assessment raises a broader question about how much of the wealth created during the AI investment boom might eventually flow into other asset classes, including crypto.
However, Anthropic has not confirmed its trading date or offering valuation, while the timing of shareholder sales will depend on restrictions attached to existing holdings.
Anthropic's profitability gains face massive infrastructure obligations
The company's financial disclosures provide a clearer basis for evaluating the valuations circulating across these markets.
Anthropic generated $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, up from about $1.16 billion a year earlier, reflecting growth of about 1,300%.
Social Capital, citing the IPO filing, highlighted an even sharper acceleration in quarterly revenue, which climbed from $376 million in the first quarter of 2025 to $11.6 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
That approximately 31-fold increase over five quarters was accompanied by significant improvements in operating efficiency.
During the first quarter of 2025, Anthropic spent approximately $2.51 on computing and infrastructure for every dollar of revenue. By the second quarter of 2026, that figure had declined to about 48 cents.
The improvement helped the company record $974 million in operating profit during the June quarter, reversing a $1.67 billion operating loss in the preceding three months.
However, the company reported a $66.3 billion net loss for the quarter, largely reflecting noncash financing adjustments, including $59.6 billion from the revaluation of convertible notes as Anthropic's valuation increased.
Those accounting effects also contributed to its $80.7 billion first-half net loss, which included $72.4 billion in fair-value adjustments to convertible notes, derivatives and related financing instruments.
Venture capitalist Nic Carter described the financial results as “robust and improving,” arguing that the headline loss obscured improvements in Anthropic's underlying operations.
Nevertheless, he questioned whether a valuation approaching $1.5 trillion could be justified by approximately 22 times annualized third-quarter revenue.
Meanwhile, Milk Road AI analyst Melvin argued that the company's improving profitability and approximately $131.7 billion in cash and short-term investments challenge assumptions that frontier AI developers must continually raise external capital to maintain their operations.
However, Anthropic's infrastructure commitments introduce a substantial financial vulnerability.
The company has agreements with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and other computing providers involving hundreds of billions of dollars in potential expenditure over several years.
Its arrangements with SpaceX alone could reach $120.5 billion through 2029, although the agreements contain cancellation provisions after initial noncancelable periods.
The financial exposure is particularly significant because approximately 80% of Anthropic's first-half revenue came from consumption-based services, allowing customers to reduce spending faster than the company can unwind many of its infrastructure commitments.
Anthropic warned that weaker demand could leave it unable to meet minimum payment obligations, potentially triggering defaults under commercial agreements and accelerated repayment requirements under related financing arrangements.
The company has expanded its revolving credit commitments to $15 billion and faces a minimum quarterly liquidity requirement of $5 billion beginning at the end of 2026.
Meanwhile, the IPO could create another significant market event after the initial listing.
Dedic questioned what thousands of newly wealthy employees and early investors might do with their proceeds once restrictions on selling their shares expire, suggesting some of the resulting liquidity could flow into new investments.
Anthropic's prospectus outlines an unusual staggered lock-up structure that allows certain shareholders to sell limited portions of their holdings from the first trading day, with additional releases scheduled afterward.
Some employees may sell shares immediately, while other investors face restrictions lasting as long as 180 days. The company's co-founders and certain major shareholders face longer restrictions, up to 365 days, with specified early releases.
The structure could spread shareholder selling across several months rather than concentrate it around a single lock-up expiration.
However, the filing has not yet established the final offering size and share count, leaving the dollar value of stock that could enter public markets at each stage undetermined.

articles.title: Brazil’s Stock Market Crashes After Lula’s Upset Victory - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Brazil’s stock market lost more than $200 billion in value at Monday’s open, and the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) fell as much as 26% after Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro.
- Polymarket and Kalshi priced Bolsonaro at roughly 80% before the vote; Lula won 51.79% to 48.21%.
- The dollar jumped as much as 12% against the real, B3 triggered its first circuit breaker since the pandemic, and Bolsonaro said he will seek to annul the election.
Brazil’s stock market lost more than $200 billion in value at the open on Monday after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff, a result that prediction markets had priced at roughly a one in five chance.
The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF, ticker EWZ, a basket of Brazilian stocks that trades in New York like a single share, fell as much as 26% from Friday’s close of about $42.60, touching $31.40 before trimming the loss to about 23% at $32.84 by 10:38 a.m. ET.
That is memecoin-sized volatility for a fund built around Brazil’s biggest companies, and it leaves EWZ roughly where it started 2026 after a 34% gain through Friday.
The dollar rose as much as 12% against the real on Friday, while the Ibovespa, Brazil’s benchmark stock index, fell as much as 17% to about 170,000 points. For a dollar-based investor, those moves at their worst combine to a loss of about 26%, in line with the ETF’s low.
B3, the São Paulo exchange, halted trading for 30 minutes after the Ibovespa fell 10% from Friday’s close, its first circuit breaker since the COVID-19 pandemic. A circuit breaker is an automatic pause meant to slow panic selling, but the index kept sliding after trading resumed.
Investors had been positioning for the opposite result since Bolsonaro unexpectedly finished first in the Oct. 4 first round, with 47.03% of valid votes to Lula’s 45.16%. The Ibovespa jumped 7.85% the next day and EWZ gained more than 10% on bets that Bolsonaro would tighten public finances and open the way to lower interest rates. Monday’s drop erased that rally and, at its lows, left the Ibovespa about 11% below its Oct. 2 close.
But Lula didn’t just beat Bolsonaro, he also beat prediction markets.
Polymarket gave Bolsonaro an 82% chance of winning the day before the vote, and Kalshi had him near 80% on Sunday morning. Both platforms are prediction markets, where a contract that pays $1 if a candidate wins trades at 80 cents when traders see an 80% chance.
Polling pointed to a coin flip rather than a favorite, with the latest Datafolha survey tied at 50% each among valid votes and CNT/MDA showing Bolsonaro ahead 50.5% to 49.5% in mid-October. Lula won 51.79% to 48.21%, a margin of about 4.4 million votes, according to Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court.
Bolsonaro said on Sunday night that he does not recognize the result and will ask the courts to annul the election, after pledging in August to respect the outcome. He objected to Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin’s decision to extend voting until 7 p.m. at the request of Lula’s campaign, which he said changed the rules midgame. His own campaign had separately asked for extra voting time in parts of three states.
“It is impossible to recognize the result of the elections in the context in which these things happened,” Bolsonaro said in Portuguese outside his campaign headquarters in Brasília. “We will use our legal team, we will ask for the annulment of these elections.”
