articles.title: August updates block critical private key leak in crypto wallet Vultisig
articles.text:
Quick Take
- ChainSecurity disclosed a historical Vultisig ECDSA flaw requiring one compromised signer and many malicious signing messages.
- August Android and iOS changes stopped malicious-party retries and appeared in repository releases, without establishing complete remediation.
- The published changes leave protection across restarted sessions unverified.
Vultisig, a crypto wallet that uses shared signing, mishandled a critical stop signal in its ECDSA signing implementation, as security researchers at ChainSecurity found.
The researchers’ Oct. 21 disclosure describes how continuing after the error could let one already-compromised signer recover the full private key.
Both the Android and iOS maintainers described code that retried after the library identified a malicious participant, then added handling to stop those retries and warn the user. The changes appear in subsequent repository release notes.
Requiring several devices offers protection only if the software preserves that requirement when one participant starts misbehaving.
A multi-party computation wallet (MPC wallet) distributes signing authority among key shares. Enough shares cooperate to produce a standard blockchain signature without assembling the full private key during normal operation.
In a two-device arrangement requiring both participants, compromising one should leave the attacker dependent on the other device’s approval.
The disclosed flaw involved ECDSA signing and required that initial compromise. An attacker could then send many malicious signing messages and observe whether the other signer returned an error.
Those responses revealed bits of a reusable internal protocol seed, eventually enabling recovery of the other share and the full key, according to ChainSecurity.
That seed is an internal setup secret, and the library assumed further signing would stop after the critical error until the seed was rotated. The application displayed a generic error and did not enforce that response.
The security consequence is that a failed signing attempt can matter even when it produces no usable transaction signature.
If continuing the exchange reveals more secret information, rejecting the transaction alone does not preserve the promised separation between signers. The application must respond to the protocol failure itself.
What the August changes demonstrate
The Android change (#5658) and iOS change (#5235) were both merged on Aug. 21, two months before public disclosure.
Their descriptions say the old code compared signing failures with the library’s success result without separately handling malicious-party ban errors. The signing routines could retry up to three times, while the user received a generic failure message.
That retry count does not establish how many messages would recover a key, or how many sessions an attacker would need.
The Android code changes and iOS changes recognize the DKLS signing library’s malicious-party error codes 100–109 during session setup, message processing, and signature completion.
Both map the flagged participant to a device identifier, carry a dedicated error past automatic retries, and display a localized warning against using that device again. On Android, the exception also bypasses relay recovery.
Together, those changes show that the apps distinguish a cryptographic verdict about a participant from an ordinary signing failure.
Retry behavior appropriate for a temporary failure can become dangerous when the library is telling the caller to stop interacting with a malicious signer.
The GitHub notes for iOS v1.45.71, dated Aug. 21, list #5235. The Android v1.0.118 release, dated August 25, lists #5658.
Wallet counts and audit scope need context
Vultisig’s vault descriptions distinguish who controls the signers. Fast Vault uses one user device with VultiServer holding the second share and co-signing. Secure Vault uses two or more user-held devices without VultiServer.
A provider-assisted wallet and a wallet spread across a user’s own devices can both use distributed signing, but their operational dependencies differ. Two participants in a signing exchange also need not mean the vault has only two shares in total.
The reviewed disclosure and application materials do not provide a full affected-version and vault-configuration matrix.
Vultisig’s security documentation says Trail of Bits audited the Silence Laboratories DKLS23 library in 2024. It says mobile and desktop application audit reports will be linked when published.
At disclosure, ChainSecurity said it had not reviewed Vultisig’s fixes or audited other parts of the protocol, so the fixes remained outside that assessment.
Useful remediation details would connect affected configurations to shipped versions and explain enforcement after both automatic and user-initiated restarts. A review covering those behaviors would address the application-level failure described here.
The protection holders are promised that enforcement depends on the application enforcing the library’s stop condition throughout signing, including when users start again after a failure.

articles.title: Tom Lee's Bitmine Keeps Buying Ethereum But Pivots to Record Share Buybacks - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitmine added 10,452 ETH to reach 6,051,933 ETH, extending its weekly buying streak and nearing its 5% “Alchemy of 5%” goal.
- The week’s bigger move was a share buyback: Bitmine repurchased 2.04 million shares, lifting its 2026 total to 22.9 million shares for ~$399.6 million, which chairman Tom Lee called the largest ever by a crypto treasury firm.
- It mirrors Strategy, which paused Bitcoin buying this week to spend $204.9 million on STRC buybacks—both giants favoring their shares over fresh crypto.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak intact, adding 10,452 ETH worth roughly $24 million, but the bigger move this week was a turn toward buying back its own stock, which the company says is now the largest equity repurchase program any crypto treasury firm has run.
The NYSE-listed firm said Monday it repurchased 2.04 million of its own shares over the past week at an average price of $22.48, bringing its 2026 total to 22.9 million shares bought back for about $399.6 million.
Chairman Tom Lee framed the buybacks as a value play, saying the company intends to repurchase stock “accretively” when management views the shares as undervalued.
The ETH purchase lifts Bitmine’s holdings to 6,051,933 ETH, worth roughly $14.3 billion at a reference price of $2,356 per coin. That’s 4.95% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving the firm, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it brands the “Alchemy of 5%.”
Lee has said Bitmine is nearly finished stacking and will stop buying once it hits that threshold. (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
Lee again cast recent crypto weakness as a buying opportunity rather than a warning sign, arguing the pullback stemmed from the same risk-off forces behind a broader AI selloff. He noted ETH had fallen 13% from its recent peak while U.S. semiconductor stocks dropped 20% over the same stretch, which he said was further evidence “a crypto bull market is underway.”
Counting cash, other tokens and what it calls “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $15 billion as of Oct. 25, including 215 Bitcoin, $514 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $76 million position in Eightco Holdings.
Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, trailing only Michael Saylor’s Strategy.
Strategy leaned the same way this week, pausing its Bitcoin buying for the first time since mid-September to spend $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock, underscoring how both treasury giants pivoted toward shoring up their shares over fresh crypto purchases.
Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of roughly $318 million.

articles.title: Aviva Investors Launches Tokenized Share Class of Sterling Fund on XRPL
articles.text:
Aviva Investors launches tokenized share class of $29B Sterling fund on XRP Ledger
The move marks Aviva’s second fund to list tokenized shares, part of a broader collaboration to bring more tokenized funds to the XRP Ledger.
Aviva Investors, the asset management arm of UK-based insurer Aviva, launched a tokenized share class of its Sterling (GBP) Liquidity Fund on the XRP Ledger (XRPL).
The development adds a tokenized share class of the company’s largest fund of approximately 22 billion British pounds ($29.4 billion) in assets under management on XRPL and allows investment in the fund in tokenized format, Ripple and Aviva revealed in a joint announcement on Monday.
It is the asset manager’s second tokenized fund, after Aviva expanded its USD Liquidity Fund to the XRPL network earlier in July.
Aviva said this makes it one of Europe’s largest asset management providers of tokenized money market funds, with about 86 million pounds invested across its two tokenized share class offerings.
Aviva made an 50-million-pound investment in the Sterling Liquidity Fund’s new tokenized share class, according to the announcement. The expansion is part of a broader collaboration between Aviva and Ripple, seeking to bring more tokenized funds to the XRP Ledger.
The XRP Ledger ranks as the ninth-largest blockchain network for tokenized assets, with $642 million in total distributed real-world asset value and about 2,900 unique holders, according to RWA.xyz data.
Related: Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan

articles.title: Ripple connects XRP Ledger to a £22 billion investment giant while chasing the next wave of corporate money
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ripple unveiled 24/7 corporate treasury services as Aviva launched another tokenized fund share class on the XRP Ledger.
- The developments extend Ripple's reach into corporate cash management and tokenized investments, two potentially lucrative financial markets.
- Ripple has yet to establish how its new treasury products will drive XRP usage, leaving the token's direct economic benefits unresolved.
Ripple expanded its institutional reach Monday as Aviva added another tokenized fund share class to the XRP Ledger (XRPL).
The British asset manager invested £50 million ($66 million) in a blockchain-based share class of its Sterling Liquidity Fund, bringing its combined investments across two XRP Ledger offerings to more than £86 million ($116 million).
The announcement coincided with Ripple's expansion into round-the-clock corporate cash management, extending its presence across two areas of institutional finance that could increase activity within its digital asset ecosystem.
The developments also raise a question about XRP's role in Ripple's growing financial infrastructure business, particularly how increased institutional adoption of the Ledger translates into demand for its native cryptocurrency.
Aviva deepens XRPL commitment with £22 billion fund
Aviva's latest offering introduces a tokenized share class to its largest investment fund, which manages approximately £22 billion ($29 billion).
The £50 million investment represents roughly 0.23% of the existing fund's assets, while the broader portfolio continues to operate through conventional financial infrastructure.
The Ireland-domiciled fund invests in high-grade sterling-denominated short-term debt instruments and offers daily liquidity. Its tokenized version uses a digital twin structure, representing ownership on the XRP Ledger while preserving the underlying fund's existing investment arrangements.
The launch follows Aviva's first tokenized money market fund offering in July, when the asset manager introduced an XRP Ledger-based share class for its US Dollar Liquidity Fund.
Mark Versey, CEO of Aviva Investors, said the second launch lays the groundwork for further expansion. Versey said:
“We believe tokenised funds can increase efficiency and ultimately lead to improved client outcomes.”
He added that the company intends to explore additional opportunities with Ripple.
The latest issuance uses the XRP Ledger's Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) standard, which allows financial institutions to define how digital assets can be held, transferred, and recovered.
XRPL Foundation contributor Vet pointed out three restrictions on the Aviva token: holders must be authorized, the issuer can claw back tokens under specified circumstances, and transfers between investors are disabled.
These controls allow Aviva to maintain oversight of ownership and compliance while using blockchain infrastructure for issuance and redemption.
BNY Mellon remains custodian of the underlying fund assets, while Komainu provides digital asset custody support and Licuido supplies tokenization infrastructure.
The structure also establishes the limits of the development's immediate impact on XRP.
Transactions on the XRP Ledger require XRP-denominated fees, while accounts and certain ledger objects must maintain XRP reserves. Increased network use could therefore generate additional transactional demand for the cryptocurrency.
However, standard transaction fees are extremely small, and Aviva's investments in tokenized fund shares do not represent equivalent purchases of XRP.
The network's ability to attract further institutional issuances, increase settlement activity and develop additional liquidity applications will determine whether these deployments create more substantial demand for the token.
Ripple targets corporate cash with 24/7 returns
Separately, Ripple introduced new capabilities for its corporate treasury platform at its Swell 2026 conference, targeting businesses seeking to manage liquidity and payments beyond traditional banking hours.
The expansion includes a product called 24/7 Returns, which allows eligible corporate clients to generate returns on qualifying digital assets, including Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, held in Ripple wallets.
The service helps companies earn returns on operating cash that would otherwise sit idle overnight, on weekends, and on public holidays, without independently managing the underlying digital asset transactions.
Ripple also introduced an orchestration layer that integrates its GSmart artificial intelligence capabilities with cash forecasting, reconciliation, liquidity management, and payment execution.
The rollout builds on Ripple's $1 billion acquisition of treasury management provider GTreasury in October 2025, which brought an established enterprise software business into its digital asset operations.
Ripple identified American Airlines, Subway, Adecco, Kingfisher, Christian Louboutin, and Trax among the businesses served by its treasury platform. However, the announcement did not establish that these companies are participating in the new returns program or using XRP and RLUSD.
The commercial opportunity is substantial, although existing adoption data suggests corporate treasury departments remain cautious about digital assets.
The Association for Financial Professionals' 2026 Liquidity Survey found that 46% of organizations increased their US cash balances, while 86% of respondents would consider real-time money market funds if they complied with their investment policies.
Yet just 1% of surveyed organizations were already using or piloting stablecoins or tokenized products, with another 9% actively exploring them.
Ripple's expanded offering could give corporate clients another route into digital assets, but the implications for XRP depend partly on which settlement networks and assets those businesses ultimately use.
RLUSD operates across multiple blockchains, and Ripple's payment infrastructure can settle transactions in stablecoins or conventional currencies without necessarily using XRP as an intermediary.
Ripple has also not yet disclosed the returns available through its new treasury product, the mechanisms generating those returns, or whether participating companies will route transactions through the XRP Ledger.

articles.title: Bitcoin Faces Second Red October With $80,000 Support in Doubt
articles.text:
BTC price risks $80K loss into FOMC, earnings: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Bitcoin bulls fought for $80,000 support over the weekend ahead of a heavy week of US tech earnings and inflation data.
Bitcoin (BTC) begins the last week of October fighting to hold $80,000 support ahead of a busy week of US macro data and earnings reports.
Key points:
- Markets see the Fed holding interest rates in their current 3.75-4% range at its meeting on Wednesday as Brent crude cools to $110 per barrel.
- South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index resumes downside ahead of a major round of US corporate earnings results.
- Bitcoin is on track to end October down 4%, copying 2025 performance, as $80,000 support appears weak.
Markets see Fed rate-hike pause with oil still above $100
The US Federal Reserve is in focus for macro analysts this week as it will decide the next move on the federal funds rate on Wednesday. Markets will be watching the rate decision by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), as well as language used by Fed chair Kevin Warsh at the accompanying press conference.
Markets have little doubt over what officials will decide, seeing over 90% odds that rates will stay in their current 3.75-4% range. FedWatch data shows consensus favoring a 0.25% hike at the December FOMC meeting.
Fed target-rate probabilities (screenshot). Source: CME Group
Commenting, economist Robin Brooks argued that such expectations were a gift to Warsh, who would not need to fight external demands to change course.
“After very contentious Fed meetings earlier in 2026, this week’s meeting gets zero interest in markets, which price only 12% odds of a hike. That’s nothing versus how markets tried to push Warsh into hiking back in July. A temporary reprieve for Warsh,” he summarized.
In separate analysis last week, Brooks saw a rate pause as all but inevitable, even amid rising oil prices and growing concerns over military escalation in the Middle East. Brent crude reached $117 per barrel on Friday, its highest level since March 19, before dropping to around $110 on Monday. Even a rise to $125, however, would not force the Fed to change course, he continued.
“The debt crisis in France would escalate sharply, anxiety around all the AI and data center debt would increase and the S&P 500 would tumble. That just isn’t a setting where the Fed is itching to hike,” Brooks wrote.
“If anything, financial conditions would be tightening sharply, so the last thing you’d want to do is hike.”
CFDs on Brent crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
On Thursday, new US macro data will be released in the form of the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, known as the Fed’s “preferred” inflation gauge. Last month, PCE came in lower than expected at 3.4% year-on-year, but analysts explained that the drop was a result of changes to the way certain index elements are calculated.
KOSPI struggles as markets prepare for US tech earnings
Nerves about prospects for the AI sector continued to pressure equities on Monday ahead of the week’s first Wall Street open.
After attempting to recoup some of its losses late last week, South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index closed down 1.5% on Monday at 5,469 points. On Friday, the tech-heavy index fell as low as 5,308 points — a level not seen since late July.
KOSPI Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The low came as a result of significant tech-stock selling as foreign capital sought safety. Last week, stronger-than-expected US earnings reports ultimately failed to lift the mood, with attention instead drawn to Tesla’s reduced Q3 capital expenditure. The Nasdaq Composite Index closed at 25,955 points on Friday, its lowest daily close since Aug. 3.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Speaking to CNBC on Monday, JPMorgan Asset Management’s Raisah Rasid was unfazed by the state of the AI trade.
“It’s really about investors thinking, ‘Look, we’re not rewarding capex anymore; what we are rewarding is return on capital. I think that’s what’s happening with AI,’” she said.
Further Q3 earnings are due out this week, with Microsoft and Alphabet both reporting after the market close on Wednesday, while Amazon and Intel follow on Thursday. In total, around 20% of S&P 500 companies will report during the week, while Thursday also sees the release of US Q3 GDP numbers.
Bitcoin “Uptober” sentiment meets 4% month-to-date losses
Bitcoin is on track to end October down 4% if the monthly candle closes near current levels around $80,000.
Related: Bitcoin ETFs break 2-week outflow streak with $301M comeback
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Data from CoinGlass shows that despite average October upside for BTC/USD totaling 26.1% since 2010, earning the nickname ‘Uptober’, both this year and last have bucked the trend. After falling 3.9% in October 2025, Bitcoin went on to lose another 17.5% in November, once more going against historical patterns that have seen average November returns of 35%.
BTC/USD monthly returns. Source: CoinGlass
Almost $150 million of long positions were liquidated over two hours on Saturday as Bitcoin fell to $79,145. The $80,000 level failed to offer support on lower time frames despite its status as a psychological boundary. CoinGlass shows a $73 million wall of bids keeping price above $79,300, with asks centered around $81,000.
BTC liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Market participants are increasingly cautious about a rebound under current macro conditions. Benjamin Cowen, founder of crypto analytics platform Into the Cryptoverse, described Bitcoin’s trips to $87,000 in late September and early October as a “fakeout.”
BTC/USD should continue to see weakness through the end of the year, he told X followers on Monday, citing historical precedent and calling for downside pressure around US midterm election years.
As Cointelegraph reported, the resistance zone around $87,000 contains important price points: the 2026 yearly open at $87,490 and 20-month moving average at $87,165.

articles.title: 'Privacy Horror’: Researcher Uncovers Extent of Samsung Smart TV User Tracking - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- X user log4 says he reverse engineered his Samsung TV’s firmware and found a file listing functions including an always-on microphone, automatic content recognition, and targeted ads.
- Cybersecurity experts say AI is making reverse engineering accessible to anyone, meaning more hidden functionality in everyday devices is likely to surface.
- They added that data collection may be one reason TV prices have stayed low for decades.
A researcher found that their Samsung smart TV was tracking them through several functionalities, including an "always on” microphone—and experts warn that similar tools could exist on other "everyday devices."
X user log4j claims to have reverse engineered his Samsung smart TV's firmware and discovered what they call a "privacy horror." One file called 'security-policy.xml’ featured functions including an always-on microphone, automatic content recognition, geo-positioning, network mapping, a targeted ads service, and user profile building, while Samsung TVs without a built-in microphone will look for one on connected devices such as a soundbar or Bluetooth speaker.
But a community note on the post points out that Samsung openly advertises some of these features. Its Pet Care and Family Care tools on Vision AI TVs listen for sounds like barking or crying and alert owners through the SmartThings app.
i own a relatively new (2025) samsung tv.
i kept getting weirdly targeted ads.
i tried reversing the firmware but it was aes encrypted and no keys unless tear it apart and do uart/jtag magic.
zero days it is. root shell on new samsung TVs!
discovered PRIVACY HORROR. write up? pic.twitter.com/EsxxCy1b6a
— log4j (@log4j) October 21, 2026
James Bore, a cybersecurity and technology consultant, told Decrypt that this isn't a new finding but just adding awareness to something that most people weren't aware of.
"The amount of monitoring that smart devices, from TVs to voice assistants to cars, do isn't secret as such, just not something promoted," Bore said. "If you read privacy policies and [End-User License Agreements], it's all in there in almost every case, but most people don't read those."
Jake Moore, Global Cybersecurity Advisor at cybersecurity firm ESET, told Decrypt that this could be the start of a wave of similar findings, as a trend of AI-powered reverse engineering has swept the internet.
"AI-assisted reverse engineering may make it easier and faster for researchers to uncover and explain how devices collect, process, and share data," Bore agreed, "but the underlying collection itself is generally not new or unknown."
Decrypt has reached out to Samsung for comment and will update this article should they respond.
Bore added that smart TVs are monitoring user behavior to advertise to you better and persuade you to spend money. He added that this is "far from unique” to smart TVs.
Moore noted that this might be why TVs haven't seen a noticeable price increase in recent years.
"TVs haven’t really increased in price like some products over the last two decades and that may be because customer data collection is keeping those costs down," Moore said. "Smart TVs are doing far more behind the scenes than most people realise, as many can monitor what we are watching and collect our data to build profiles for targeted advertising."
Last week, smart TV owners started using AI coding agents like Claude Code to strip ads and tracking software out of their sets. One open-source project, Cleanyourtv, now lists tested setups for 107 TV models from 37 brands, though it only fully works on Android-based TVs—not Samsung’s Tizen operating system. However, as one Decrypt writer discovered, vibe-coded solutions can end up backfiring.
Both cybersecurity experts say that the public shouldn't be uniquely concerned about the functionalities revealed on Samsung TVs. Bore said that we should be more worried about how "blasé” we've become about accepting companies "constantly profiling us to manipulate us into spending more money on things we don't need."
"The concern is how much of our data is being collected and who it’s being shared with," Moore said. "It is possible to go through TV settings to minimise the amount of data access points are being used and analysed, but saying that, privacy shouldn’t be something you have to hunt through dozens of settings to find."
Those more anxious about security claim that this form of invasive data collection is enough for them to change their behavior.
Muneeb Ali, the co-founder of Stacks, a prominent Bitcoin layer-2 network, said that he doesn't handle private crypto keys in rooms with devices.
"We were paranoid that a hacked device could record or listen in," he tweeted. "Didn’t realize the TVs were literally 1st party programmed for full-on spying. Only the paranoid survive."

articles.title: Strategy makes record $205 million STRC buyback as Strive spends $511 million on Bitcoin
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Strive bought a record $511 million in Bitcoin last week, while Strategy purchased zero BTC and spent $205 million repurchasing STRC shares.
- Strive's holdings reached 43,000 BTC, leaving it just 1,000 BTC behind Metaplanet as Strategy's cumulative STRC buybacks exceeded $2 billion.
- Strategy faces a crucial Oct. 28 dividend vote, while Strive's new $1 billion financing program could accelerate its pursuit of second place.
Bitcoin treasury firms Strategy and Strive made record purchases last week, but directed their capital toward different assets.
While Michael Saylor's Strategy intensified its preferred-stock buybacks, Strive accelerated its Bitcoin accumulation, highlighting diverging priorities in how the companies deploy capital.
Strategy's STRC purchases exceed $2 billion
Strategy's Bitcoin buying streak ended after five consecutive weeks as the company stepped up efforts to support its STRC high-yield preferred stock.
The Saylor-led firm acquired no Bitcoin between Oct. 19 and Oct. 25, its first weekly pause since mid-September. It also raised no fresh capital through its at-the-market equity program, leaving its holdings unchanged at 848,517 BTC, purchased for approximately $64.02 billion.
Instead, the company spent a record $204.9 million to retire 2.07 million shares of its STRC preferred stock, extending a buyback campaign that has now spent more than $2 billion since July.
Bitcoin analyst Ragnar estimated that Strategy accounted for 28% of STRC trading volume in the latest week, showing how much the company's own purchases have contributed to demand for the security.
The scale of the purchases is particularly notable because STRC has recovered much of the ground lost during Bitcoin's June selloff, when the security briefly traded near $71, well below its $100 stated value.
Strategy initially sought to exploit that discount, buying back shares at prices that reduced its outstanding preferred capital and future dividend obligations. The firm publicly maintained that it would become less aggressive as the security approached $100.
However, the opposite has happened in dollar terms. Strategy executed its initial $25 million repurchase at an average price of $86.52 per share, compared with approximately $99.06 in its latest transaction. Weekly spending has continued to rise despite the shrinking discount.
The increased commitment has also drawn heavily on cash that could otherwise finance additional Bitcoin purchases. Strategy's unrestricted USD Cash balance fell to $242.4 million from $1.6 billion over the latest reporting week, reflecting an 84.8% decline.
The company left its separate $4.83 billion reserve earmarked for preferred dividends and debt interest untouched. It also retains $956.8 million in repurchase capacity after expanding its preferred-stock buyback authorization to $3 billion.
Market observers argue that Strategy's next move could reduce the need for further market intervention in STRC.
The company is seeking shareholder approval on Wednesday, Oct. 28, to introduce daily dividend payments for its preferred securities, replacing STRC's existing twice-monthly schedule.
The proposed change would allow investors to receive and reinvest income more often while potentially reducing price fluctuations tied to dividend payment dates. Strategy hopes the arrangement will help keep STRC trading near $100 without increasing its current 12% annual dividend rate.
Ragnar suggested the firm's management may want to assess whether daily dividends attract enough investor interest before considering another increase in the payout rate.
If shareholders approve the proposal, the first daily STRC dividend payment is scheduled for Nov. 2, giving Strategy an opportunity to test whether a change in payment frequency can sustain demand as its remaining repurchase authorization declines.
Strive's record Bitcoin purchase puts Metaplanet's second-place ranking within reach
Strive is taking the opposite approach to preferred-stock financing, raising fresh capital through high-yield securities as it accelerates its Bitcoin accumulation campaign.
The company acquired a record 6,182 BTC for approximately $511.4 million between Oct. 17 and Oct. 23, lifting its holdings to 43,000 BTC and bringing it closer to overtaking Japan's Metaplanet as the world's second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin holder.
The purchase leaves Strive just 1,000 BTC behind Metaplanet's 44,000 BTC and 514 coins short of Tether-backed Twenty One Capital, which holds 43,514 BTC.
The narrowing gap brings Chief Executive Matt Cole closer to his ambition of becoming the second-largest corporate Bitcoin holder before the end of 2026.
Strive has financed its rapid expansion through a series of capital raises, most recently completing a $630 million offering of its 15% Series A Perpetual SATS Preferred Stock on Oct. 20.
Strive sold seven million shares at $90 apiece, providing fresh capital while committing to annual cumulative dividends of $15 per share. The initial issuance carries approximately $105 million in annualized dividend obligations, with the company setting aside a reserve equivalent to 18 months of payments.
The fundraising campaign is continuing. Strive disclosed a new $1 billion at-the-market program on Monday, allowing it to sell additional SATS shares over time to finance Bitcoin acquisitions, other investments, and general corporate expenses.
Its balance sheet also showed considerable liquidity despite the latest acquisition. Cash and cash equivalents increased to $504.4 million as of Oct. 23 from $317.5 million a week earlier.
Strive also retained 505,000 shares of Strategy's STRC preferred stock, valued at approximately $50.2 million. The position was unchanged during the same week Strategy spent a record amount buying back that security.
However, the preferred-stock financing introduces recurring costs that could grow alongside Strive's Bitcoin holdings. Its prospectus says future cash dividends on SATS are expected to be funded primarily through additional capital raising, making continued investor demand important to sustaining the strategy.
The new offering gives Strive additional fundraising capacity as it approaches Metaplanet's holdings, although the authorization does not guarantee that the entire $1 billion will be raised. The timing and size of future sales will depend on market conditions and demand for SATS shares.

articles.title: Anthropic Makes IPO Filing Public, Plans Nasdaq Listing Under ‘ANT’ - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anthropic has filed to list its Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the underwriters.
- The company reported first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier, and a net loss of $80.7 billion.
- A trust will elect a majority of Anthropic's board, while an entity owned by its seven co-founders will hold 50.1% of shareholder voting power.
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude family of AI models, has filed for an initial public offering, the company announced on Monday.
The company plans to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT," according to its S-1 registration statement. The number of shares and the price range have not yet been set. Both Anthropic and existing shareholders will sell shares, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named first among 24 underwriters.
Anthropic has filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC related to its proposed IPO.
Read more: https://t.co/zuRMrxXzNx
Legal disclaimer: A registration statement relating to these securities has been filed with the SEC but has not yet become effective. These securities…
— Anthropic (@AnthropicAI) October 26, 2026
The public filing follows a confidential draft submitted to the SEC in June. Details of that draft reported by Reuters last month included backers' hopes for a valuation above $2 trillion. In May, Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation.
Anthropic reported revenue of $16.29 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared with $1.16 billion in the same period a year earlier. Full-year revenue was $4.59 billion in 2025, up from $386 million in 2024 and $41 million in 2023.
The company recorded a net loss of $80.7 billion for the first half of 2026. Most of that came from a $72.4 billion charge for changes in the fair value of convertible notes and other instruments, which the filing says was primarily driven by an increase in its valuation. Its operating loss for the period was $693 million.
As of June 30, 2026, Anthropic had raised $141.1 billion in total and held $112.4 billion in cash and cash equivalents, plus $19.3 billion in short-term investments, according to the filing. As of September 30, it had more than 1,900 customers generating at least $1 million in revenue over the previous 12 months, and about 250 generating at least $10 million.
Anthropic's governance structure
Anthropic is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which requires its directors to balance shareholders' financial interests with those affected by its conduct and its stated purpose: "the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
Under the proposed structure, the Long-Term Benefit Trust, a body of five financially disinterested trustees, will elect a majority of the board through a special class of stock. Immediately before the offering, Anthropic will issue a single Class F share to an entity owned by its seven co-founders, carrying 50.1% of the voting power on most shareholder matters. The filing says that makes Anthropic a "controlled company" under Nasdaq rules.
Holders of Class A shares will get one vote per share. The filing warns that the structure "may effectively eliminate the ability of holders of our Class A common stock to influence important decisions, including a change in control."
Anthropic has also contributed about 847 million non-voting shares, representing 5% of its fully diluted shares as of June 30, to a wholly owned subsidiary dedicated to its public benefit purpose. Its co-founders have each pledged to give 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropic causes, according to the filing.
The company announced the fund earlier this month, drawing criticism from investor and former White House AI czar David Sacks. "Whether it serves the public good remains to be seen," he tweeted.
Disclosure: This article was drafted with the assistance of Claude, an AI model developed by Anthropic.

articles.title: Securitize Tokenized Stock Market Cap Halves as Circle Leads $3.3B Market
articles.text:
Securitize’s tokenized stock value halves as Circle widens lead
SECZ’s onchain market cap fell to $208.6 million as Circle-linked tokens reached a combined $383.6 million across several issuers in the $3.3 billion tokenized equities market.
The value of tokenized shares of Securitize (SECZ) have lost more than half their value in less than a month as the gap with market leader Circle (CRCL) widens.
The market capitalization of SECZ tokens fell from a high of $430.4 million on Sept. 28 to $208.6 million by Sunday, according to Token Terminal. The NYSE-traded shares closed Friday down 2.1% at $7.80 apiece, with a market cap of $1.27 billion.
Tokens tracking Circle’s shares have gained about 20% in market value since Sept. 28 to reach $383.6 million, reclaiming the top spot in the $3.3 billion tokenized stock market.
Tokenized stock market capitalization by underlying stock, excluding ETFs. Source: Token Terminal
The decline in tokenized SECZ coincided with a sell-off in Securitize’s underlying shares on the NYSE, which erased gains that followed the Oct. 8 launch of its stock trading platform on Solana. Citi downgraded SECZ from Buy to Neutral on Oct. 13 amid concerns about tokenization revenue.
Securitize helps asset managers including BlackRock issue securities on blockchains. The company brought its own common shares onchain alongside its July 2 NYSE listing, becoming the largest tokenized equity at the time.
SECZ remains the largest individual tokenized stock as Circle’s total is spread across products from several issuers. Binance’s CRCLb on BNB Chain leads those offerings at $154.1 million.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Gain $301M Despite Late-Week Sell-Off
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs break 2-week outflow streak with $301M comeback
US spot Bitcoin ETFs finished the week with $301 million in net inflows after a strong three-day start gave way to heavy withdrawals.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) attracted around $301 million in net inflows last week, snapping a two-week outflow streak despite heavy withdrawals late in the week.
The funds lost about $228 million the previous week and $680 million the week before. October’s net outflows stood at about $314 million, according to Farside Investors data.
Bitcoin ETFs drew $1.08 billion between Monday and Wednesday as Bitcoin (BTC) climbed to a weekly high of $84,777 on Wednesday, according to CoinGecko. Investors then withdrew about $774 million on Thursday and Friday as BTC retreated toward $80,000.
ETF investors have tended to sell into Bitcoin declines, according to research published Thursday by market maker DWF Labs. The company found net outflows during seven of eight Bitcoin sell-offs of at least 15% since US spot Bitcoin ETFs launched in January 2024.
“ETF investors aren’t the dip buyers people think they are,” DWF said.
At the time of publication, Bitcoin traded at $80,025, down around 3.3% over the past seven days. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to a “Neutral” reading of 50, down from “Greed” at 59 a week earlier.
US spot Ether ETFs recorded a fourth consecutive week of net outflows, shedding about $221 million last week, according to Farside Investors data.

articles.title: Treasury dealers’ net bill holdings hit a two-year high as October 30 funding pressure nears
articles.text:
Quick Take
- FHLBNY reports dealers’ net Treasury-bill holdings at a two-year high as money funds redirect some cash into short repo.
- SOFR reached 3.9% for October 22, while FHLBNY flags Canadian bank year-end on October 30 as a forthcoming pressure.
- Coinbase reports rebuilding Bitcoin leverage, while Treasury-to-crypto spillover still needs evidence linking dealers to borrowers.
Treasury dealers’ net holdings of bills, short-term U.S. government debt, have reached a two-year high, according to the Federal Home Loan Bank of New York’s October 23 update. Financing those inventories puts dealer capacity in focus ahead of October 30, even while overnight dollar funding looks calm.
FHLBNY attributes wider bill spreads partly to heavy issuance and money market funds shortening their portfolios amid uncertainty about Federal Reserve policy. Some cash has shifted from bill buying into overnight and short-term repurchase agreements, or repo. That allocation can support overnight lending even as dealers hold substantial bill inventories.
The distinction is between cash being available and intermediaries having room to pass it on. A 2024 Federal Reserve staff study explains that moving repo cash from money funds to leveraged borrowers expands dealer balance sheets. Its authors hypothesize that tighter constraints increase the compensation dealers demand.
Overnight conditions have remained calm. The latest New York Fed SOFR observations available on October 25 put the Treasury-backed borrowing benchmark at 3.9% for October 22, up from 3.88% on October 21. FHLBNY said SOFR stayed at or below the Fed’s 3.9% interest rate on reserve balances during the report’s week.
FHLBNY flags Canadian bank year-end on October 30 and cash leaving repo to pay mortgage-backed-security holders as forthcoming pressures. It says SOFR may test 3.9% more steadily. Calmer Thursday bill auctions than the previous week provide a counterweight to those risks.
Bitcoin’s financing gives a separate reading
Bitcoin’s positioning data show rebuilding leverage. Coinbase Institutional’s October 23 research reported perpetual funding rising from 0.1% annualized on October 13 to 7.2% one week later. Its Prime Trading commentary separately interpreted rebuilding Bitcoin and Ether funding as momentum longs adding exposure. These derivatives payments measure the cost of maintaining leveraged positions, rather than a comparable repo borrowing rate.
For borrowing context, Coinbase’s financing table dated October 22 listed indicative centralized-finance overnight rates of 4.25%–12.5% and a Bitcoin borrowing range of 1.25%–4.75%. Without matched borrower and collateral terms or an earlier comparable quote, those ranges cannot establish a new tightening in credit.
Futures basis, the premium over spot prices, needs similar care. The 2023 BIS paper Crypto carry finds that interest-rate differentials explain little of its variation, emphasizing leveraged investor demand and the relative scarcity of arbitrage capital. Basis therefore needs to be read alongside borrowing conditions and positioning.
A Treasury-to-Bitcoin transmission case would strengthen if repo pressure persisted while comparable crypto borrowing or rollover terms worsened and market depth thinned. Stable crypto financing would weaken that explanation. Even simultaneous deterioration would leave causation to establish: evidence that constrained intermediaries actually reduced financing available to Bitcoin markets remains the missing link.

articles.title: Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buying, Spends $205M Buying Back STRC - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strategy bought no Bitcoin last week, its first pause since mid-September, and sold no shares through its at-the-market offering program, according to an SEC filing.
- The company spent $204.9 million of its USD Cash buying back 2,068,459 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock, up from $193.1 million the week before.
- Strategy still holds 848,517 BTC, while its USD Cash balance fell to $242.4 million from $447.3 million a week earlier.
Strategy did not buy any Bitcoin last week, breaking a run of weekly purchases that began in mid-September, as it spent $204.9 million buying back its STRC preferred stock instead, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm also sold no shares through its at-the-market offering program between October 19 and 25, according to an SEC filing. It holds 848,517 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.02 billion at an average of $75,446 per coin.
Strategy has repurchased $205M of $STRC. As of 10/25/26, we hold 848,517 $BTC and $5.1B of USD Assets. $MSTRhttps://t.co/VQ9soVDIii
— Strategy (@Strategy) October 26, 2026
The pause follows a string of smaller Bitcoin purchases. Strategy bought 267 BTC for $22.1 million the previous week, after spending $21.5 million on 250 BTC the week before that and $29 million in the week it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.
The STRC buyback, covering 2,068,459 shares, was the largest of those weeks, up from $193.1 million the week before and $192.4 million the week prior. Strategy paid for it entirely from USD Cash, the pool of money it keeps for general purposes including buying Bitcoin, which fell to $242.4 million from $447.3 million a week earlier.
Its separate USD Reserve, which is meant to cover preferred dividends and interest on its debt, held steady at $4.83 billion. After the latest buyback, $956.8 million remains available under the company's $3 billion program for repurchasing its preferred stock, which it raised from $2 billion a week ago. A separate program to buy back MSTR common stock has $1 billion left.
Strategy and the MSCI rules
The pause comes as Strategy faces possible removal from MSCI's widely tracked equity indexes. MSCI finalized a rule on October 15 that treats "non-operating companies," those whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset, as ineligible for its Global Investable Market Indexes from the close of November 30. The index provider will publish the list of affected companies on November 11.
Removal would force funds that track the indexes to sell the affected shares. Strategy chairman Michael Saylor had urged MSCI to drop what he called a "discriminatory" rule.

articles.title: Circle gives its Bitcoin-backed token one balance across Ethereum and Arc
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Circle added cirBTC to Gateway, giving holders one deposited balance usable on Ethereum and Arc.
- Circle’s advertised sub-500ms access starts after deposit finality; the separate API-independent withdrawal route takes seven days.
- Gateway integration is permissionless, while minting and redeeming cirBTC for native Bitcoin through Circle Mint require qualified-business access.
Circle added its Bitcoin-backed token, cirBTC, to Gateway on Oct. 23, letting holders use one deposited balance across the Ethereum and Arc blockchains. Gateway treats deposits across supported networks as a single spendable balance per asset, reducing the need to keep funds ready on both chains, according to Circle’s announcement.
The expansion also adds the EURC stablecoin alongside USDC. Circle’s asset-specific documentation lists cirBTC on Ethereum and Arc mainnet. EURC is supported on those networks plus Avalanche, Base, Solana and World Chain.
Gateway keeps a separate balance for each asset. A cirBTC transfer burns the token on the source network and mints cirBTC on the destination; it neither converts the balance into USDC nor transfers native Bitcoin. For an exchange or wallet serving both chains, Circle says the shared inventory can be deployed where a withdrawal or payment needs to land.
Fast access follows deposit finality
Circle advertises cross-chain access in under 500 milliseconds once the deposit has finalized and the balance is established. That estimate excludes the initial funding wait and is not guaranteed. Its confirmation table lists an average of roughly 13 to 19 minutes for an Ethereum deposit before Gateway updates the balance or issues an attestation.
A separate seven-day withdrawal option lets holders reclaim funds directly from the Gateway Wallet contract without relying on Circle’s API. Circle’s asset documentation explicitly extends that withdrawal delay to cirBTC. It is a fallback exit, rather than the ordinary transfer time between Ethereum and Arc.
CryptoSlate’s August 2025 Gateway report also describes API-independent recovery after seven days.
Circle says cirBTC is backed one-for-one by native Bitcoin held at a regulated entity in its corporate group, with the BTC segregated from corporate assets for holders.
Gateway integration is described as permissionless, with no sign-up required. Access to cirBTC through Circle Mint, however, is offered to qualified businesses. Withdrawing cirBTC from Gateway leaves the holder with the token; redeeming it for native Bitcoin uses a separate Mint process in which Circle burns cirBTC and releases BTC to a Bitcoin address.
Costs also depend on the operation. Circle’s announcement says Gateway fees for cirBTC and EURC are waived on Arc at launch and quotes a one-basis-point rate outside Arc. Those rates are not an all-in transfer cost: Circle’s fee documentation lists gas and optional forwarding charges too. cirBTC transfer costs are paid in cirBTC.

articles.title: Musk Warns of Mass AI Neocloud Failures Amid Funding Crunch
articles.text:
Musk warns over 200 AI neoclouds face ‘guppy-level death’
The warning comes as Gartner forecasts that more than 80% of specialist cloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030.
Elon Musk warns that over 200 specialist AI cloud providers could fail or consolidate as lenders tighten up their purse strings.
Musk said Sunday on X that lenders had largely stopped providing financing to companies without substantial revenue streams outside AI data centers. He said SpaceX had secured $40 billion in debt financing for GPUs because of its investment-grade status and revenue from its Starlink satellite internet and rocket businesses.
“That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many,” he said.
A neocloud is a specialist cloud company that rents out computing power for AI, usually through data centers packed with powerful GPUs.
Musk’s warning follows an October forecast from research firm Gartner that more than 80% of neocloud providers will cease operating independently by 2030, as the industry struggles to generate sufficient returns on massive AI infrastructure investments.
The warnings could also have implications for Bitcoin miners that have pivoted into AI infrastructure. For example, IREN has expanded into AI cloud services, renting computing power to customers, while Core Scientific provides data center hosting for neocloud customers such as CoreWeave.
Related: Bitcoin hashrate hits seven-month high as AI shift fails to ease mining competition
In its forecast, Gartner said AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on infrastructure in 2026 and another $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030, but said there is insufficient revenue to deliver profitable returns on all those investments.
The pressure could be particularly acute for neoclouds, which must earn enough from AI computing services to sustain their operations. Larger cloud companies have more diversified revenue streams that could support AI investment for years, Gartner said.
Even strong market growth may not be enough. Gartner forecasts spending on AI-optimized infrastructure-as-a-service will rise from $66 billion in 2027 to $174 billion in 2030, but said most providers could struggle to recover their investment before the current generation of AI chips is replaced.
SpaceX sees sharp jump in AI revenue
Musk’s comments came days after SpaceX reported that its “Super Intelligence” business generated $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 830% from a year earlier and accounting for more than half of the company’s $14.6 billion in quarterly sales.
The company attributed the growth to new cloud services agreements, its acquisition of Cursor and increased adoption of its Grok AI model.

articles.title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80,000 Ahead of Fed Decision, Midterms - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin briefly fell below $80,000 over the past day, touching about $79,330, before recovering to trade at $80,264, down 2.7% on the week, per CoinGecko.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw more than $773 million in net outflows on Thursday and Friday, leaving October on course for a net loss.
- Analysts warned of further volatility ahead of the Federal Reserve's decision on Wednesday and the U.S. midterm elections on November 3.
Bitcoin slipped below $80,000 over the past 24 hours, as a sell-off in technology stocks and nervousness ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision weighed on risk assets.
The leading cryptocurrency fell as low as $79,332 before recovering to $80,240, down 2.5% over the past week, according to CoinGecko data. It remains about 36% below its all-time high of $126,080.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $635.5 million in net outflows on Thursday, wiping out most of the gains from a three-day run of inflows, followed by a further $137.9 million on Friday, according to SoSoValue. Even so, the funds ended the week up about $301 million, snapping a two-week losing streak, though they remain down about $314 million for October.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, said the drop was "primarily driven by a broader correction in global risk assets," with growing skepticism toward AI-related technology stocks a major factor.
"Investors are not necessarily questioning the long-term prospects of artificial intelligence, but rather whether current elevated valuations can be justified by future earnings and cash flows," Sun told Decrypt. Outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs and the unwinding of leveraged positions "further amplified the downward pressure," he said.
Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com, said Bitcoin had come under pressure alongside tech stocks. "Persistent inflation, elevated Treasury yields and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening have reduced enthusiasm for speculative assets," she told Decrypt.
Bitcoin's key levels
Stephen Wundke, strategy and revenue director at quantitative investment firm Algoz, said $80,000 was a psychologically important mark for many investors, but warned that a break below it could be misleading, given low trading volumes over weekends.
More worrying, he said, was a broader decline in trading volumes as investors pull out of altcoins and park funds in stablecoins. Bitcoin needed to hold the $82,000 level from which it launched rallies in August and September to support the bull case, and staying below it "could see a broader pullback in the coming weeks while the macro uncertainty remains," he said.
"The bull case for Bitcoin is not dead but it is keeping its head below the parapet whilst so many stray bullets are flying across the globe," Wundke added.
Sun said that if Bitcoin falls further, he sees $75,000 as a key support level to watch, and expects volatility to stay elevated.
Hathorn said the Fed's decision on Wednesday and major technology earnings "could prove just as important for Bitcoin as developments within the cryptocurrency market itself." A more hawkish Fed could strengthen the dollar and weigh on risk assets, she said, while "Bitcoin's recovery may remain fragile unless stronger institutional demand accompanies any improvement in broader market sentiment."

articles.title: Hong Kong Names Solana Company Strategic Enterprise
articles.text:
Hong Kong names Nasdaq-listed Solana Company a strategic enterprise
The Nasdaq-listed firm said it plans to establish Solana validator operations in Hong Kong.
Hong Kong has named Nasdaq-listed Solana Company (HSDT) a strategic enterprise under a government program aimed at attracting businesses that support the city’s economic development.
Solana Company said Thursday that it was among the seventh batch of businesses selected by Hong Kong’s Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES) and the only blockchain infrastructure company onboarded by the office in 2026.
Hong Kong’s government confirmed the addition of 18 enterprises to the program last week, bringing its total to 142.
A Solana Company spokesperson told Cointelegraph that the designation gives it a single point of contact across government agencies and regulators, expedited pathways for recruiting overseas talent and introductions to local institutional partners.
Solana Company operates staking and validator infrastructure and advises financial institutions on blockchain adoption. It also holds Solana (SOL) as part of its digital asset treasury strategy.
The company said it plans to establish validator operations in Hong Kong under Pacific Backbone, an initiative to build a low-latency blockchain infrastructure network across the Asia-Pacific region.

articles.title: Bitcoin faces an inflation warning beneath steady US consumer sentiment
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Michigan’s October 23 study finds long-run inflation expectations and uncertainty above comparable 2019 and 2024 ranges.
- Final inflation expectations were 4.7% for the year ahead and 3.5% longer term, matching preliminary October readings.
- Fed participants judged medium- and longer-term inflation expectations consistent with their 2% objective in September, before Michigan’s October study.
A University of Michigan study published Oct. 23 finds that Americans’ long-run inflation expectations remain above comparable 2019 and 2024 readings. That persistence could complicate easier financing conditions for Bitcoin even as the headline consumer sentiment index barely moves.
The concern is that repeated price shocks can leave consumers expecting inflation to persist. If those expectations change spending behavior, bringing inflation down could become harder, narrowing the room for US monetary policy to ease.
Michigan’s final October survey put sentiment at 48, versus 48.1 in September. Year-ahead inflation expectations were 4.7%, up from 4.6%; long-run expectations reached 3.5%, up from 3.4%.
Both inflation readings matched the preliminary figures already cited in CryptoSlate’s Oct. 22 and Oct. 23 advance coverage. Each rose from September and held steady between the preliminary and final releases.
The new study provides the historical comparison. Using a consistent web-interview series, it finds median long-run expectations above the monthly ranges seen in 2019 and 2024. Recent readings also show elevated expectations among consumers anticipating the largest price increases, alongside greater uncertainty.
Sample sizes differ across years, but survey director Joanne Hsu says the findings also hold against historical official phone interviews.
Hsu describes the 2025 tariff escalation and the energy shock associated with the 2026 Iran conflict as successive influences on expectations. Consumers who expect further price increases may bring purchases forward. Across households, that spending could reinforce inflation, she warns.
Hsu presents precautionary spending as a risk whose current contribution remains unmeasured. She says entrenched expectations remain avoidable.
How the risk could reach Bitcoin
For Bitcoin, the potential connection runs through policy and investors’ willingness to take risk. The Fed’s policy framework says anchored inflation expectations help inflation return to 2% and support moderate long-term interest rates. Persistently elevated inflation could therefore constrain monetary easing.
There is a counterweight. At their September 15–16 meeting, Fed participants judged medium- and longer-term expectations consistent with the 2% objective, according to the meeting minutes. Some nevertheless worried that prolonged above-target inflation could affect expectations and wage- and price-setting. Those judgments predate Michigan’s October study.
A 2023 IMF working paper found that US monetary tightening depresses a shared component of crypto prices by reducing investors’ willingness to take risk, resembling its effect on equities. That historical result supports a possible route from stubborn inflation to weaker crypto demand.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s Bear Market Is Over, Galaxy Research Says: 'Now Is an Attractive Time to Buy' - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Galaxy’s Alex Thorn argues Bitcoin bottomed in June and is now in an accumulation phase, calling it “an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin.”
- Bitcoin has closed five straight weeks above its 50-week average, and its market value never fell below its realized value, a first for any bear market.
- Thorn cites $40 trillion in federal debt and 5% Treasury yields as fuel for Bitcoin. Galaxy and Thorn disclose holding Bitcoin.
Galaxy Digital’s head of research thinks the worst is over for Bitcoin.
In a report published Monday, Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, argued that Bitcoin’s bear market ended in June and that the asset is now in an accumulation phase. “Our conclusion is simple: we believe now is an attractive time to buy and hold bitcoin,” he wrote.
The call comes as Bitcoin struggles for direction. It traded at around $80,000 on Thursday, 36% below its October 2025 high but 39% above its June 30 low. On Sunday, Bitcoin briefly slipped below $80,000 to about $79,700, according to CoinGecko.
Thorn’s case starts with the charts. Bitcoin spent 44 weeks below its 50-week moving average before reclaiming it in September, and the week ended Oct. 18 marked its fifth straight weekly close above that line. Since 2011, Bitcoin has reclaimed the average after a stretch of 20 weeks or more four times. In each case, the price never closed more than 8.4% below the reclaim level over the following year and eventually regained its prior all-time high.
The halving cycle, the roughly four-year event when rewards for Bitcoin miners are cut in half thereby reducing new supply, points the same way. The three previous cycles bottomed between 777 and 912 days after a halving, and Thursday was day 916. The latest downturn was also the shallowest on record: a 53% drop, compared with declines of 77% to 93% in past cycles.
Onchain data appears to back that up. For the first time in any bear market, Bitcoin’s market value never fell below its realized value, the average price at which every coin last moved. The ratio between the two bottomed at 1.10, compared with lows of 0.56, 0.69 and 0.75 in prior cycles.
Short-term holders, whose coins carried the recovery from $58,525, have an average cost of $74,811 and sit about 9% in profit. Yet the spent-output profit ratio, which tracks whether coins are being sold at a gain, sits at 1.009, suggesting few are cashing out.
Selling pressure is fading, too. Long-dormant coins, unmoved for five years or more, have been sold at about 34,000 BTC a month this year, half the 2024 pace. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have added 87,000 BTC since the June low after holdings fell just 11% from peak to trough while the price dropped 53%, the report found.
Thorn also argued that the macro case has strengthened. Federal debt has reached $40.44 trillion, fiscal 2026 ended with a $1.99 trillion deficit, and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.31% this month, its highest since 2007. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 sits less than 1% below a record, while Bitcoin would need to rise 53% to reclaim its high.
“A bet against stocks and hard assets is a bet on fiat, the one position that makes no sense today,” Thorn wrote.
The bullish call lands in a choppy market. Spot Bitcoin ETFs swung from a $1 billion three-day inflow streak to two days of heavy outflows this week, leaving October flows in the red.
Last week’s hotter-than-expected inflation data revived bets on another Federal Reserve rate hike, and Bitcoin briefly dipped below $80,000. Higher interest rates lift Treasury yields, the return investors earn for lending to the U.S. government. A bond paying around 5% with almost no risk makes Bitcoin a harder sell, while higher rates make borrowing pricier and strengthen the dollar.
Thorn’s tripwire is a weekly close below the 50-week average, currently $76,540, that isn’t regained within a month. He also noted that Bitcoin “has proven its ability to run to at least $125k, and we see no reason why it can’t retake that level.”
Galaxy and Thorn both disclose that they hold Bitcoin.

articles.title: Robinhood Chain's Trading Boom: How Pons Put Stock Tokens to Work
articles.text:
Key Takeways
- Pons has made Stock Tokens useful inside third-party markets. Creators can price a new coin against a Stock Token; trades build the reserve, and successful launches carry the pair into a Uniswap pool.
- The scale is already significant. Bitquery counted 207,893 V2 launches, $736 million in bonding-curve turnover, and at least $2.14 billion after graduation over 32 days.
- Reserve choice is the distinctive feature. Some 73,896 launches used tokenized stocks, commodities, or wrapped bitcoin as reserves, generating $232 million of curve turnover. That total is broader than Stock Tokens alone.
- A working use case is different from a durable market. The next signals are retained liquidity, returning users, useful applications beyond launch week, and outcomes for traders and creators.
A memecoin launch might seem like an unlikely place to find a new use for tokenized stocks. On Robinhood Chain, that’s exactly what’s happening. Pons lets creators launch tokens against assets linked to Nvidia and other stocks. Those assets become part of how the new market trades, collects reserves, and eventually moves to Uniswap.
Here's how it works. A creator chooses a reserve asset, and buyers trade against it on a bonding curve. Once the reserve reaches its target, liquidity moves into a Uniswap pool. Robinhood’s Stock Tokens provide economic exposure through tokenized debt securities, without shareholder rights. Pairing a memecoin with one doesn’t turn the memecoin into a share of the company.
The interesting part is what developers can do with those assets once they’re onchain. Pons puts them to work in markets built outside Robinhood. In a little over two months, it became one of the chain’s busiest applications. That gives us a working use case and the next question: what keeps people using it after the launch rush?
1. Robinhood Chain: A Growing Market for Builders
Robinhood brought an established consumer business into its onchain expansion. In its mainnet announcement, the company said it served nearly 28 million customers across 38 countries. Stock Tokens were available through Robinhood Wallet in more than 120 countries, subject to local restrictions. The Arbitrum-based chain opened to independent builders with Uniswap and Pleiades among its launch partners.
Activity grew across the wider network. In its second-quarter earnings call, Robinhood reported more than $12 billion in DEX volume after the mainnet launch. At a September investor conference, CEO Vlad Tenev said about 200 Stock Tokens were live, and trading across the chain had recently reached billions of dollars a day. And that set the context for a range of projects, including Pons, building markets and applications around tokenized assets.
2. The Growth Story: From Challenger to Heavyweight
Pons began operating on Jul 14, 2026. In CoinGecko’s late-July market snapshot, Pons accounted for 37.2% of all tokens launched on Robinhood Chain from July 13 to July 27, after Noxa paused new launches.
The bigger surge followed a new V2 deployment on Aug 3, 2026.
Bitquery reconstructed V2’s first 32 days through Sep 3, 2026. The totals were substantial: 207,893 launches, $736 million traded on bonding curves, and at least $2.14 billion traded after tokens graduated to Uniswap. Growth accelerated late in the study period. Bitquery reports that daily curve volume rose about 55-fold over 11 days, while daily launches increased roughly 17-fold.
That growth also showed up in revenue. According to CoinGecko, Pons overtook Pump.fun in daily protocol revenue on Sep 2, 2026, generating $1.1 million. Stonkfun achieved its own daily lead four days later with $1.5 million, underscoring how quickly new launchpads were entering the competition.
By Sep 28, 2026, Pons was still recording substantial trading activity. A DefiLlama snapshot showed $2.45 billion traded on V2 bonding curves over the preceding 30 days, including $231 million in the preceding week. These figures exclude trading after graduation to Uniswap. They show activity extended beyond the initial surge, while leaving the longer-term growth pace open.
3. The Reserve Choice: Why Stock Tokens Matter
The reserve choice is what makes Pons interesting. Pons lets creators price a new token against ETH, a dollar stablecoin, or a tokenized asset. If the token graduates, its reserve becomes one side of the Uniswap pool. Someone arriving to trade a memecoin can therefore end up trading against a Stock Token without setting out to buy stock exposure.
The choice caught on. In Bitquery’s first 32 days of V2 data, 73,896 of 207,893 launches used a reserve other than ETH or the dollar stablecoin. They generated $232 million of the $736 million traded on Pons’ curves—nearly one dollar in three. That category includes tokenized stocks, commodities, and wrapped bitcoin; Nvidia was its most popular reserve, followed by a SpaceX tracker, Trump Media, and SPY.
Figure 1. Alternative reserves accounted for nearly a third of Pons V2 curve volume, with tokenized stocks included alongside commodities and wrapped bitcoin.
Two graduates show where a stock-linked launch can lead. Orbio.so (ORBIO) launched against Nvidia’s Stock Token and graduated to Uniswap. CoinGecko recorded its market cap rising from $13.6 million on September 15 to $87.5 million on September 28. Orbio says it converts half of token trading fees into AI inference credits for holders, while its dashboard reported roughly 547,000 gateway requests served by September 30.
Longbow (BOW) launched against the SPY Stock Token, which is linked to an S&P 500 ETF. Its team reported 57 lending markets and more than 1,000 users in its first 30 days. A September 30 DefiLlama snapshot showed $4.37 million locked in its markets and about $857,000 in active loans. Longbow’s lending activity gives the stock-linked launch a story beyond the token’s trading.
4. Pons' New Application Economy
Beyond launch counts, Pons is already generating meaningful application-level economics. Bitquery measured $11.8 million in fees charged during the 32-day cohort. About $9.7 million went to holders of launch fee rights across 103,904 recipients. That fee flow is a tangible result for a young launchpad, even though individual recipients earned very different amounts.
The model can create activity at several layers. Pons collects application-level fees while a graduated market can generate Uniswap swap fees for liquidity providers and gas fees on Robinhood Chain. These streams accrue to different participants, so curve volume and secondary turnover should be understood as market activity rather than a single revenue figure. The broader point is that Pons brings new markets, liquidity, and transactions into the chain’s economy.
The PONS token is a separate part of the ecosystem. Bitquery found that it predates the audited V2 launches and is neither listed in the V2 creation registry nor referenced by its factory, router, or fee contracts. Whether V2 activity funds any PONS buybacks or burns, and by what mechanism, remains to be clarified.
5. The Next Chapter: Building Durable Markets
Most launches never reach the open-market stage. Bitquery counted 3,228 tokens that filled their reserves and graduated to Uniswap, or 1.55% of 207,893 created. Half of those graduations happened within four minutes, a sign of intense competition at launch. The graduates went on to generate at least $2.14 billion in trading—roughly three times the volume on Pons’ curves. The handoff into Uniswap is working at scale. The public cohort does not show whether stock-reserve launches graduated or retained liquidity at a different rate.
Figure 2. Most V2 launches did not reach Uniswap; the graduates generated substantial secondary trading.
The first month produced a large field of experiments and a much smaller group of markets with substantial secondary activity. In Bitquery’s cash-flow measure, 66.8% of 314,736 trading addresses withdrew less reserve value than they deposited, with unsold tokens valued at zero. Among 2,339 graduates with sufficient trading history, the median price at the study cutoff was 85% below its first-hour level. These snapshots do not measure final returns. They show why discovery, retained liquidity, and participant outcomes matter as Pons develops.
The commercial opportunity is in repeat use. A Stock Token can be the asset traders need to enter a new market, the reserve accumulated by its curve, and the asset paired with the token after graduation. That puts Robinhood’s assets in circulation through third-party activity. It also gives Pons more ways to differentiate a launch. Whether this becomes recurring demand will depend on the markets that remain useful once new-token excitement fades.
The useful follow-up is a like-for-like view of stock-reserve pairs after seven and 30 days: which still trade, how much liquidity remains, and whether people return. Comparing those patterns with ETH and stablecoin launches would show whether the reserve choice changes the life of a market. Returns after costs and the value of unsold holdings would help answer a separate question about participant benefits.
Pons has turned Robinhood’s Stock Tokens into building blocks for independent crypto markets. Its flexible reserve menu lets creators choose how a token launches, gives traders a new way to use stock-linked assets, and carries successful pairs into Uniswap. That is a concrete achievement for both Pons and Robinhood Chain. The next chapter is to turn this early momentum into recurring markets with retained liquidity and better outcomes for participants. The first cohort proves the use case; durable adoption is the opportunity still ahead.

articles.title: Keystone Breach Exposes Hardware Wallet Buyers’ Addresses
articles.text:
Keystone says website breach exposed hardware wallet buyers’ addresses
A security researcher warned that the leaked shipping details could expose crypto holders to targeted scams and physical attacks.
Crypto hardware wallet maker Keystone has disclosed a website security breach that exposed customer information to attackers, raising concerns about targeted scams and physical attacks.
Keystone said Saturday that it detected suspicious activity earlier in the week and confirmed Friday, after reviewing API activity with Shopify, that an unauthorized third party had accessed customer shipping information. This included names, contact details, shipping addresses and other order details, such as items bought.
“We’ve blocked access, fixed the vulnerability, opened an investigation, and are emailing affected customers,” said the company.
Keystone warned that the exposed information could be used for targeted phishing attacks. However, security researcher Taylor Monahan also raised concerns that leaking shipping addresses could expose customers to physical attacks and kidnappings.
Blockchain security firm CertiK recorded 52 verified wrench attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 33% from 39 during the same period last year. Such crimes, commonly called “wrench attacks,” involve using physical threats or violence to force cryptocurrency holders to surrender their assets.
“Again, we’re truly sorry to everyone affected,” Keystone said. The company did not disclose how many customers were impacted.
Keystone questioned over promise to delete customer data
The breach has also raised questions about Keystone’s handling of older customer information.
In a 2023 blog post, Keystone said it had reduced its customer data retention period to 180 days following security incidents affecting other hardware wallet manufacturers.
However, some customers said they received breach notifications despite purchasing their devices more than two years ago, raising questions about what information Keystone retained and whether the notifications indicate that older order records were not deleted as promised.
Related: Italy investigates government email breach linked to Revolut data leak
An X user going by “OG DEGEN” said they received a call from a scammer claiming they were law enforcement investigating a fraud case. The user suspected the caller obtained their information through a Keystone order placed in 2024, based on the personal information the caller referred to.
“I think their plan was to convince me that my private keys had been exposed and then send me a phishing link to supposedly reset them,” they wrote on X.
Another X user, trintaetres, also said they received the email notification despite buying the device over two years ago.
Cointelegraph contacted Keystone to ask how customer information from purchases made more than 180 days earlier could have been exposed despite its previously announced retention policy, and how many customers were affected. The company did not respond by publication time.
