articles.title: What happens when your PC's CMOS battery dies? - Engadget
articles.text:
What happens when your PC's CMOS battery dies?
You might not even have known about this little battery, but you'll notice the effects when it stops working.
Look closely at a desktop computer's motherboard, and you'll notice a small disc-shaped battery that was installed from the factory. This coin-sized battery powers your computer's real-time clock and helps preserve basic hardware-related settings when the machine is turned off.
Like any cell, the CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor) battery has a limited lifespan and eventually requires replacement. The good news is that the process is fairly easy and inexpensive. In most cases, you can go many years without needing to replace a CMOS battery since they only drain when your PC isn't connected to power.
What does a CMOS battery do and why do computers need it?
You can think of a CMOS battery as a backup power supply for a computer's motherboard, allowing it to keep track of the date and time even when it's unplugged. Motherboards also store boot-related BIOS or UEFI settings on a small memory chip that receives power from the CMOS battery.
Most desktop computers use a standard CR2032 coin cell, which is the same kind that powers Apple's AirTags. Some may use a CR2025 coin, but this is less common. Since the battery only needs to power a real-time clock and memory chip, it can usually last several years, or even up to a decade.
A telltale sign of the CMOS battery failing is if your computer can no longer accurately keep track of the time and date between power cycles, especially after unplugging it from the wall. It may reset to a default value (like January 1, 2000 or January 1, 1970) on every boot. An incorrect date-time combination can result in websites not loading, as modern HTTPS connections rely on security certificates with narrow validity periods. This will also add confusion from inaccurate "last updated" dates on your own files.
That said, many modern operating systems now fetch the correct date and time from an online server upon boot, so you may not notice a failing CMOS battery until it's completely dead. When that happens, your computer's BIOS or UEFI will throw up a warning on boot and revert to its factory settings every time it starts up. That means system-level options like the boot order and fan configurations are set to default every time.
You can ignore this temporarily, as it doesn't affect your apps or files. But replacing the battery is inexpensive and straightforward. To preserve your motherboard's settings between sessions with a dead battery, use sleep mode instead of rebooting your computer, and avoid unplugging it from the wall.
Many laptops use their main battery instead of a dedicated CMOS cell to maintain the internal clock, so you're much more likely to run into this problem on a desktop PC. That's a benefit since most modern laptops don't offer easily user-replaceable components anyway.
How to replace your PC's CMOS battery
If you suspect your CMOS battery needs a replacement, all you need is a new coin cell battery and a few minutes. Most computer cases are toolless these days, so you likely won't need a screwdriver. However, I keep a flathead screwdriver on hand for the task as it makes prying the existing coin cell battery out of the motherboard easier.
To find out which battery you need, power off your PC, take the side panel off your computer case and locate the CMOS battery on your motherboard. You're looking for a silver-colored coin-shaped cell. If you have a graphics card or other bulky hardware installed, you may have to temporarily remove that from your case if the battery is located behind it.
The CMOS battery is typically held down by a clip or latch. This is where you can use a flathead screwdriver or any flat object to gently release it and dislodge the cell. Install the new battery, put the side panel back on and you're done. If you have a mini PC or a non-standard motherboard, I recommend reading your computer's manual before starting the process.
With the CMOS battery replaced, don't forget to enter your computer's BIOS or UEFI settings and adjust settings to the way you had them before. An important one for gamers or anyone using heavy software is re-enabling Intel XMP or AMD EXPO to ensure your RAM performs as well as it should. Likewise, you may want to tweak your motherboard's built-in CPU overclocking features, although be warned that increased performance comes at the expense of added power draw and heat.

articles.title: iPhone Duo now supports Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2
articles.text:
Apple has just released iOS 27.2, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The software update also includes an “Edge Light” feature for the iPhone Duo that’s intended to illuminate your face during video calls.
iPhone Duo now supports Apple Pencil with iOS 27.2
The latest iOS update also adds dual-camera use in group FaceTime calls.
Apple previously said the iPhone Duo would add support for the Apple Pencil “later this year.” The company’s first foldable comes with revamped iOS 27 controls designed to work across the device’s 7.6-inch inner display and 5.4-inch outer screen. Many major apps, like Netflix, Prime Video, and Microsoft Outlook, already support the Duo’s extra screen real estate, but some still need some work.
The iOS 27.2 update also allows Siri AI to take suggested actions in Messages, while adding support for Siri AI in more languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Apple is rolling out support for Google’s SynthID AI watermark in Photos and Image Playground, too, according to 9to5Mac.
Other smaller but notable updates include user profiles on the Apple TV app on iPhone. The Apple Podcasts app is also replacing its “Up Next” queue with a list of “New Episodes,” along with a “Continue Playing” section just beneath it. You’ll also see the new Apple Music logo. And group calls on FaceTime now support dual capture so you can show both what’s visible from your selfie cam and your back cameras.
Apple also released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, watchOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2.

articles.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen3.8 tried to upload a file to Beijing
articles.text:
An Alibaba Qwen model tried to upload a file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing during a security test, Cohere says. Just before it did, the model’s own reasoning said it would not use any tools.
The Canadian AI company published the findings on Monday in a blog post. Cohere’s sandbox blocked the attempt, and no external communication succeeded, the company said.
What the model did
Cohere ran Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Alibaba’s August preview of its Qwen4 architecture, through a Microsoft benchmark for AI agents that do a security analyst’s job. The task was to write a rule that detects malicious file downloads.
Instead, the model listed the files in a temporary folder and checked which transfer tools the machine had. It read the DNS settings. Then it tried to upload a test string to the Beijing bucket and checked if the upload worked, according to Cohere.
“Our sandbox had no route out, so the request died at the container wall. On a developer’s laptop or in a CI runner with normal network access, it would have reached the foreign server before anyone noticed,” Cohere wrote.
The behaviour is rare, Cohere said. It happened in fewer than one call in 100,000 across its tests. A clean re-run of the same prompt produced a correct detection rule. Still, a service handling 10 million agent turns a week could see up to 100 such calls, the company said.
Other habits
To find the trigger, Cohere fed the model the start of its own command and sampled hundreds of completions. In 23% to 36% of them, the model reached for 169.254.169.254. Cloud servers on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure fetch their temporary access keys from that address. Cohere reads that as an attempted credential grab, though it says its sandbox had nothing live to return.
Then Cohere added the flag that saves a download to disk. The model wrote a web address in 92% of completions, up from 4%. Hosts on Cohere’s watchlist rose from 0.5% to 23%, led by an Alibaba file proxy.
In a separate offline test, the model tried to create a RAM disk without administrator rights. When the container refused, it used a Linux trick to make itself root inside a private namespace, Cohere said.
Developers had spotted parts of this before. In August, a Hacker News report described a Qwen3.8 model producing signed Alibaba Cloud storage links nobody asked for. In September, an agent project logged eleven fetches of addresses on one Alibaba host.
A training leftover or a backdoor
Cohere says it cannot tell whether the behaviour is deliberate. It may be a leftover from training, such as unscrubbed agent logs from Alibaba’s training sandboxes. Or it may be a deliberate mechanism to “call home”. Nick Frosst, a Cohere co-founder, said the same on X.
Our research team found that Qwen models may attempt to contact servers in China without prompting.
Whether this reflects an unintended post-training artifact or learned behavior remains unclear.
Either way, its important consideration when deploying.
Nick Frosst (@nickfrosst) October 26, 2026
Cohere sells its own AI models to businesses and governments, and it also releases open-weight models. Chinese models accounted for 41% of downloads on Hugging Face in the year to March 2026, Cohere said, citing the platform’s spring report. The US has already told civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek from their systems. Alibaba’s chairman, Joe Tsai, has called open source Europe’s route to independence in AI.
Cohere advises security teams to block agents from reaching the internet by default and to treat model weights they did not build like unsigned software. A model’s reasoning trace is not a security boundary, it says.

articles.title: Hôm nay diễn ra Diễn đàn Kinh tế mùa thu năm 2026
articles.text:
Với thông điệp “Sự hội tụ của các cực tăng trưởng mới toàn cầu” và chủ đề “Tinh thần hợp tác trong kỷ nguyên mới”, Diễn đàn Kinh tế mùa thu 2026 (AEF) hướng tới thúc đẩy đối thoại chính sách, kết nối nguồn lực và mở rộng hợp tác quốc tế trong bối cảnh kinh tế thế giới đang tái cấu trúc.
Diễn đàn do Thủ tướng Chính phủ chỉ đạo, UBND TPHCM chủ trì, Trung tâm Cách mạng Công nghiệp lần thứ 4 tại TPHCM (HCMC C4IR) phối hợp với các sở, ngành và đối tác trong nước, quốc tế tổ chức.
Theo ban tổ chức, AEF 2026 diễn ra trong 4 ngày, từ ngày 26/10 đến ngày 29/10, với sự tham gia của hơn 2.700 đại biểu đăng ký tham dự và 214 diễn giả đến từ 27 quốc gia, vùng lãnh thổ.
Sự kiện gồm nhiều chuỗi sự kiện khác nhau, trong đó có các điểm nhấn như sau:
Ngày 26/10, điểm nhấn là Chương trình CEO500, tập trung vào sự hội tụ của dòng vốn đầu tư trực tiếp nước ngoài (FDI), công nghệ và tài chính toàn cầu, kết nối lãnh đạo doanh nghiệp và tìm kiếm cơ hội hợp tác, tăng trưởng mới.
Đặc biệt, hai ngày trọng tâm là ngày 27 và 28/10 sẽ chính thức đồng thương hiệu với Diễn đàn Kinh tế Thế giới (WEF) – dấu mốc lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử các kỳ AEF.
Trong đó, ngày 27/10 sẽ diễn ra các phiên thảo luận chuyên đề về chuỗi giá trị toàn cầu, trung tâm tài chính quốc tế, logistics xanh, kinh tế tuần hoàn, kinh tế số, trí tuệ nhân tạo, công nghệ lượng tử và các lĩnh vực mới; cùng không gian trình diễn công nghệ Rising Star Arena.
Ngày 28/10 sẽ diễn ra Phiên toàn thể cấp cao với sự hiện diện của Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng cùng sự tham dự của lãnh đạo, đại diện 8 quốc gia, Liên hợp quốc, Liên minh châu Âu (EU). Ngay sau đó, Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng sẽ có Phiên đối thoại 60 phút trực tiếp trên sân khấu với giám đốc điều hành WEF.
Phiên đối thoại với chủ đề "Định vị Việt Nam trong tương lai toàn cầu" nhằm làm nổi bật thông điệp Việt Nam chuyển từ một đối tác chủ động tham gia sang một bên đồng kiến tạo các cơ hội tăng trưởng và hợp tác mới.
Cuối cùng, trong ngày 29/10 diễn ra các hoạt động kết nối doanh nghiệp song phương Việt Nam - Anh, Việt Nam - Trung Quốc, Bắc Âu - Việt Nam và Việt Nam - Israel, cùng các chuyến tham quan khu công nghiệp và trải nghiệm văn hóa.
Song song với các điểm nhấn trên, từ ngày 26/10 đến ngày 29/10, các hoạt động kết nối và trình diễn công nghệ cũng diễn ra xuyên suốt, gồm khu vực Rising Star Arena, họp mặt thường niên Mạng lưới C4IR toàn cầu và các hội thảo xúc tiến đầu tư, công nghệ với đối tác quốc tế, trong đó có Trung Quốc, Ấn Độ, Israel và các nước Bắc Âu.
Theo ban tổ chức, AEF 2026 được thiết kế xuyên suốt qua 4 trụ cột chiến lược là vai trò của các siêu đô thị; công nghệ đột phá và hệ sinh thái đổi mới sáng tạo; các mô hình hợp tác mới; và vai trò tiên phong của khu vực tư nhân. Từ 4 trụ cột nền tảng này, các hoạt động được thiết kế gắn kết chặt chẽ theo dòng thời gian nhằm tạo nên một mạch nội dung thống nhất.

articles.title: Elvis Presley's estate is suing Anthropic over copyright infringement - Engadget
articles.text:
Elvis Presley's estate is suing Anthropic over copyright infringement
Stakeholders said Anthropic trained its models on 250-plus Elvis songs and demanded $41 million in compensation.
A new lawsuit over a modern issue, AI copyright infringement, is reaching back into the past. The owners of Elvis Presley's music just sued Anthropic for $41 million, claiming the AI company trained its models on 274 Elvis songs without permission, The New York Times reported. That amount for a single artist who died nearly 50 years ago shows how expensive alleged musical plagiarism can be for AI companies.
Stakeholders in Elvis Presley's back catalog include Authentic Brands Group, Raleigh Music Publishing, multiple trusts and at least one individual. They accuse Anthropic of bypassing DRM protections and removing or altering copyright management information from 247 songs. Those include hits like Don't Be Cruel, Can't Help Falling in Love and A Little Less Conversation, according to the lawsuit filed on October 23rd.
"The Elvis Plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the Defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before," lead attorney Richard Busch wrote. "The Elvis Plaintiffs' iconic collective catalog contains some of the most influential and enduring musical compositions in human history." The complaint notes that Elvis sold over a billion records and that his works "are some of the most valuable in the world."
Like OpenAI and other AI companies, Anthropic is facing multiple lawsuits for training their models on copyrighted music and other materials. Sony and Warner recently sued Anthropic for "blatant violation" of copyright law involving thousands of works. Prior to that, Universal Music and Concord Music Group filed a similar claim against Anthropic for illegally downloading and training on 20,000 copyrighted songs. Each lawsuit is claiming damages in the billions of dollars.
The Elvis suit, though, is notable because it centers on a single musician who died decades before AI was a thing (though some have tried to recreate him as a robot). Anthropic has previously claimed that training its AI models on copyrighted music constitutes "fair use." In a short statement to Engadget, Anthropic said that "we disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully."

articles.title: Apple confirms iPhone Duo inner screen fault and offers replacements
articles.text:
Apple has acknowledged a fault with the inner screen of some iPhone Duos. It says affected owners can get a replacement through AppleCare.
Apple gave the same statement to several outlets on Monday, including CNBC, where Kif Leswing and MacKenzie Sigalos reported it. It follows reports of cracking screens from owners over the weekend.
“We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement,” Apple said.
Apple also told Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman that most Duo units are not susceptible to the fault, he wrote on X. Affected phones show the defect soon after first use, Apple told him.
The statement does not say what causes the fault or how many phones it hits. Out of warranty, an inner-screen repair costs $999, according to Apple’s support site. The Duo itself starts at $1,999.
A problem at the hinge
Owners describe bright lines spreading across the inner screen from the hinge. Some said their screens broke within hours. One owner said it failed before finishing setup, in a post on Reddit.
iFixit, which took a Duo apart over the weekend, suspects the hinge. Its chief executive, Kyle Wiens, set out the problem in a post on X.
“The hinge is actually dozens of parts, with ludicrous precision. A manufacturing variance or grain of sand can kill the fragile display panel it protects,” Wiens wrote.
Apple points to apps
Apple also said early buyers like the phone and that developers are updating their apps for it.
“The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor,” Apple said.
Apple also released iOS 27.2 on Monday. It adds Apple Pencil support to the Duo, as Emma Roth reported for The Verge.
The Duo went on sale in stores on Friday, after preorders sold out within minutes on 16 October.

articles.title: The NBA’s response to gambling scandals is to add more gambling partnerships
articles.text:
From the bright minds that brought you FTX Arena and NBA Top Shot NFT maketplace (where sales last month dropped to $762,781, which is a 99.66 percent decrease compared to the February 2021 peak of $226,350,843), the NBA announced Monday that it has new “preferred” prediction market deals for Kalshi and Polymarket, as well as a memorandum of understanding with the US CFTC about how to manage the relationships. It also announced an expansion of its DraftKings deal to include prediction markets, and says that more expansions will be announced with others soon.
The NBA’s response to gambling scandals is to add more gambling partnerships
The NBA announced a new integrity framework, along with prediction market deals for Polymarket, Kalshi, and DraftKings.
The NBA is already facing scandals after Jontay Porter pleaded guilty to conspiracy over a gambling and manipulation scheme in 2024, Malik Beasley is reportedly in negotiations over a plea deal on similar charges, while former player Terry Rozier and coach Chauncey Billups are under indictment on charges of allegedly rigging prop bets and participating in rigged poker games, respectively.
NBA Head of Media Distribution & Partnerships Scott Kaufman-Ross proclaims that “Protecting the integrity of the game is our top priority,” as it establishes its integrity framework for the Kalshi and Polymarket deal. Under the new arrangements, prediction markets will be able to use official league data and IP, while promising limitations on “permissible markets” and information-sharing on suspicious trades and investigations.
That last bit will probably be important, as prediction markets have already drawn insider trading activity for everything from US military activity in Venezuela to Trump’s teleprompter. Currently, New York attorney general Letitia James is just one of many state AGs suing Kalshi and the others as senators investigate reports pointing out how DraftKings and others use AI to target the gamblers who are more likely to lose, while restricting bets from those who win.

articles.title: iFixit's teardown of the iPhone Duo shows potential causes for cracked screens - Engadget
articles.text:
iFixit's teardown of the iPhone Duo shows potential causes for cracked screens
The Duo is the most repairable folding phone yet, but opening it up isn't for the faint of heart.
iFixit's latest teardown of the iPhone Duo has arrived, and it's especially interesting because of the device's complex folding display. The DIY repair group spotted some interesting details about the hinge design that may explain screen cracks some buyers are seeing. It also said that the Duo is the most repairable folding device yet, but opening it up wouldn't be for the faint of heart.
To make the screen fold smoothly while minimizing the appearance of a crease, Apple took a twofold approach (sorry). The first part involved creating a smooth curve for the screen inside the hinge by using multiple curved guides that extend when the display is folded and retract when it's open. A center support bar running along the hinge also drops to accommodate the fold.
Secondly, Apple hid the crease by using oval pixels aligned a specific way and effectively "blurring" the fold point with a nano-texture coating. iFixit showed this effect precisely by putting the screen under a powerful microscope.
The retractable curved guides and support bar may point to the potential cause for screen cracks. To figure this out, iFixit built a 3D hinge model from "teardown footage, patents and CT scans, then compared it with the reported damage locations." In one of its simulations, it found that the center bar failed to drop far enough, creating a stress point when the screens fold comes down on it.
The company also found that, despite the iPhone Duo's IP68 dust resistance rating, fine particles can make their way into the hinge mechanism (just like they can on other folding phones). That can cause the hinge to "crunch" and damage the screen, causing the "green line" damage pattern across the display seen by some users. The reason, says iFixit, is that while the internal mechanism is dust resistant, the hinge mechanism apparently is not — so you may want to avoid taking your Duo to the beach.
Other parts of the Duo are more solid and easily repairable. iFixit was able to remove the outer screen and batteries, and said that the smaller components were "fairly accessible." The inner display and hinge accounted for the largest deduction and iFixit noted that "many are opting for AppleCare+ coverage for this reason... the early reports of screen failures make clear that display replacement is more than a distant possibility." With all that, iFixit gave the iPhone Duo a provisional 5/10 repair score, pending availability of replacement parts.

articles.title: iPhone Duo bị đẩy giá lên 80 triệu đồng
articles.text:
Theo giá công bố tại TopZone, iPhone Duo bản 256GB có giá 64,99 triệu đồng. Các phiên bản 512GB, 1TB và 2TB lần lượt được niêm yết ở mức 71,49 triệu đồng, 84,49 triệu đồng và 103,99 triệu đồng.
iPhone Duo bắt đầu có hàng tại Việt Nam từ ngày 23/10/2026. Tuy nhiên, tại thời điểm ghi nhận, một số hệ thống bán lẻ như TopZone, FPT Shop và CellphoneS hiện không còn suất đặt mua iPhone Duo trên website. Tình trạng khan hàng khiến người mua khó tiếp cận sản phẩm theo giá niêm yết, đồng thời tạo điều kiện cho thị trường mua bán sang tay đẩy giá lên cao.
Trên các hội nhóm Facebook, iPhone Duo được rao bán với giá cao hơn đáng kể so với giá niêm yết chính hãng. Bản 256GB có giá 74-80 triệu đồng, chênh khoảng 9-15 triệu đồng so với giá bán tại hệ thống phân phối chính hãng.
Các phiên bản 512GB và 1TB được rao bán với giá 88-105 triệu đồng, cao hơn giá chính hãng khoảng 16-20 triệu đồng.
Đáng chú ý, bản 2TB màu Trời Đêm (Night Sky) có giá rao bán lên tới 125-135 triệu đồng, chênh 20-31 triệu đồng so với giá niêm yết 103,99 triệu đồng.
Nguyên nhân chính khiến iPhone Duo bị đội giá là nguồn cung đợt đầu hạn chế so với nhu cầu thị trường. Theo thông tin được ghi nhận, Việt Nam chỉ được cung ứng khoảng 5.000 chiếc trong đợt mở bán đầu tiên.
Một số người mua muốn nhận máy ngay thay vì chờ đợt hàng tiếp theo, tạo điều kiện cho người có sẵn thiết bị hoặc suất mua sớm chào bán với giá cao hơn.
Trên các hội nhóm, người bán chào hàng xách tay từ Singapore và Thái Lan. Một số người chuyển nhượng suất đặt cọc hoặc lịch hẹn nhận máy sớm tại các hệ thống như TopZone, FPT Shop và CellphoneS.
Ngoài ra, máy có sẵn cũng được rao bán với mức giá cao hơn niêm yết. Hình thức này hướng đến khách muốn nhận hàng ngay mà không phải chờ các đợt hàng tiếp theo, dự kiến vào tháng 1-2/2027.
Một số tin đăng cũng chào bán máy nguyên seal, chưa kích hoạt. Có người rao iPhone Duo với giá 79 triệu đồng; người khác đưa ra mức giá tương tự cho cùng phiên bản.
Với bản 512GB màu trắng, một tài khoản đăng lịch hàng dự kiến về vào các ngày 23/10, 28/11 và 5/12, đồng thời yêu cầu trả thêm 8 triệu đồng đối với máy đợt đầu và 5 triệu đồng đối với máy đợt sau.
Ông Đỗ Thành Nam, kỹ sư công nghệ thông tin, khuyến cáo người mua iPhone Duo qua các hội nhóm Facebook cần thận trọng với nguy cơ lừa đảo đặt cọc. Một số tài khoản có thể sử dụng hình ảnh máy hoặc hóa đơn lấy từ Internet để tạo lòng tin, sau đó yêu cầu người mua chuyển tiền giữ hàng hoặc nhận chuyển nhượng suất mua.
Để hạn chế rủi ro, người mua nên xác minh danh tính và lịch sử giao dịch của người bán, kiểm tra hóa đơn và thông tin đơn hàng, đồng thời ưu tiên giao dịch trực tiếp và chỉ thanh toán sau khi đã xác nhận được sản phẩm. Không nên chuyển khoản chỉ dựa trên ảnh chụp hóa đơn hoặc lời hứa giao máy.
Với iPhone Duo xách tay, người mua cũng cần tìm hiểu kỹ chính sách bảo hành. Các thiết bị không phải phiên bản phân phối chính hãng tại Việt Nam có thể phát sinh chi phí khi cần gửi bảo hành ở nước ngoài. Việc sửa chữa các bộ phận như màn hình gập hoặc bản lề cũng có thể gặp khó khăn nếu thiếu linh kiện phù hợp.
Mức chênh lệch 10-30 triệu đồng so với giá niêm yết khiến chi phí sở hữu iPhone Duo tăng đáng kể. Nếu không có nhu cầu sử dụng ngay, người mua có thể chờ các đợt hàng tiếp theo từ đại lý chính hãng để hạn chế rủi ro và tránh phải trả thêm tiền mua máy.

articles.title: Lykyn Turns Growing Mushrooms Into a Spectator Sport
articles.text:
If your online algorithm detects your having even the slightest interest in growing mushrooms, you will, at some point, probably see an ad for the Lykyn. It looks like something out of a science fiction movie—a clear box with theatrical lighting, fog, and a giant mushroom displayed like an otherworldly specimen.
After trying the Lykyn myself for a month, I can confirm that it really does look like that in real life, and as someone who has tried many different mushroom-growing methods, I was impressed by how well the Lykyn worked as a legitimate fruiting chamber. The thing you’ll have to decide for yourself is whether it’s worth $300 to showcase a process that lasts only a week or two.
Some Assembly, Some Fog
Even though the company is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, Lykyn manufactures all fruiting chambers in Turkey and ships them straight from Istanbul for free. I worried about a delay, but my unit arrived in just 11 days, with none of the duty fees or other customs weirdness that seem to plague many overseas shipments these days. The speed was even more impressive given that I had the custom wood handle engraving add-on ($15), which puts your own text on the handle instead of “Lykyn.” (Mine had my name.)
The 13 x 13 x 15-inch unit, available in white or black plastic, arrives mostly disassembled—you will need to peel the protective film off both sides of each acrylic panel, slide them into plastic tracks on the base, add the corner posts, and fill the unit with distilled water. One panel doubles as a sliding door, and installing it was fiddly on my unit; I had to open and close it a few times to loosen it, and even now it still takes two hands to wrench it open. The Lykyn must be connected to 2.5-GHz Wi-Fi and a power source with its 5-volt USB-C cable (there is no provided brick), and the light—a little LED pad that sits on top—plugs into the base.
The only troubleshooting I had to do was with the ultrasonic humidifier, which emits an occasional cloud of fog (and is audible, but no louder than a typical humidifier), with extra humidity being pulled out by a fan. Despite my following directions, the mister produced no mist, and I kept getting notifications from the Lykyn app that the unit was out of water, despite the reservoir being visibly full. I eventually had to push the preinstalled wick farther down into its slot and “prime” the membrane on top with a little bit of water. (I later verified the Lykyn app’s humidity reading against my own hygrometer; the readings were similar within a couple of percentage points.) Other than refilling the water reservoir, the Lykyn needs no maintenance.
Brief but Spectacular Blooms
The Lykyn is a “smart” fruiting chamber, which means the humidity, airflow, and light schedules are controlled by settings for your specific species in the easy-to-use Lykyn app. There are also options to control these variables manually. (Note also that though the app shows the temperature, the Lykyn is not able to heat or cool.) While you can use any brand of fruiting block in the Lykyn up to 6 pounds, I tested my unit with the brand’s own 5-pound shiitake and pink oyster blocks, which came separately—no fruiting block is included with your Lykyn purchase. There are also no instructions on or with the blocks themselves, so be sure to check online for how yours needs to be prepared—some, like the shiitake, need to be taken totally out of their packaging, while others simply need an X cut into the side of the bag.
Having the block in versus out of the bag had a dramatic effect on the overall aesthetic of the Lykyn, which sat front and center in my dining room during the test. The bare shiitake block looked like a moon rock or quirky scientific specimen under the colorful lighting (which is customizable, but the default indicates the mushroom's “emotions," from green for “happy and thriving” to red for “stressed and worried”), while the black-bagged oyster mushroom block looked like … well, a black plastic bag. With the precisely controlled lighting and humidity, both mushroom blocks fruited within several days, compared with several weeks with other methods I’ve tried. This is especially impressive for shiitake, which are notoriously fussy in their requirements.

articles.title: Marissa Mayer defends using her Dazzle AI to describe her daughter
articles.text:
Marissa Mayer has defended using her startup’s AI assistant to describe her own daughter, after a New York Times profile drew a wave of criticism online.
The former Yahoo chief executive told Alexandra Alter of The New York Times that her daughter’s teacher had asked for three bullet points on what made the girl special. Mayer asked Dazzle, her company’s AI assistant, instead.
“It came back and was like, your daughter is empathetic, creative and an animal lover,” Mayer told the Times.
Users on X criticised her for handing the question to an AI, as Caitlin Hornik reported for The Independent.
Mayer’s reply
Mayer answered in a post on X on Monday. She thanked the Times for the piece and said she wanted to give more context.
Thank you to @nytimes for yesterday’s piece on Dazzle (@itsdazzleai) and for recognizing our team’s hard work. While it’s still early days, the user engagement and response so far have been terrific.
I wanted to share more context behind one anecdote in the article: my daughter Marielle’s birthday slide.
To be clear, I didn’t use Dazzle because I was overwhelmed by making a slide. I used it because summing up your child in a few bullets feels laughably limiting. And, since our team had just gotten an early prototype running, I wanted to see what deeper threads it might find.
So, when Marielle and her twin sister Sylvana’s 4th-grade teachers emailed asking for a slide celebrating each girl for their December 10th birthday, I pasted the email into Dazzle to test its limits. I fully expected it to struggle, since most facial recognition can’t even tell my identical twins apart.
Instead, Dazzle blew me away. Not only did it distinguish Marielle from Sylvana, it surfaced forgotten kindergarten projects (like the “snake denomizer” and the “sandcat playground”) and connected them to who Marielle is today. I combined Dazzle’s insights with a few of my own and showed the slide to @zackbogue. He was floored and asked how I remembered those details. I fessed up that the Dazzle prototype had found them, and we both marveled at what AI can unlock from our camera rolls.
(Pictures attached of Dazzle’s response, plus the slide I made with its insights and my own.)
The foundational paper on transformers is titled “Attention Is All You Need.” What makes photos + AI so powerful is that our camera rolls are a decades-long record of what we pay attention to. By analyzing that visual history, an AI agent can connect dots we didn’t even realize we were documenting.
A birthday slide isn’t a common case, but here are a few that have stunned Dazzle users recently:
– Personalized learning: Dazzle offered custom spelling lists and grammar concepts based on photos of a child’s schoolwork.
– Home inventory: Given a book club reading list, Dazzle found a book the user already had and noted two others by the same authors, entirely from the backgrounds of their photos.
– Design intuition: Dazzle noticed a new sofa in a user’s living room photo and recommended artwork to hang above it.
– Wardrobe suggestions: For an esoteric costume party, Dazzle recommended what the user already had in their closet and could wear, based on the clothes in their past pictures.
We take 5 billion photos a day, often wondering if we’ll ever look at them again. Now, AI can turn those snapshots into deep, personal context.
marissamayer (@marissamayer) October 26, 2026
She said her daughters’ teachers had asked for a slide celebrating each girl for their birthday. Her team had just got an early prototype running, and she wanted to test its limits.
Dazzle told her identical twins apart and found forgotten kindergarten projects in her photos, she wrote. She added that she combined its suggestions with a few of her own.
What Dazzle does
Dazzle launched in late September. It reads the photos in a user’s camera roll to answer questions, carry out tasks and make suggestions. It competes with personal AI agents such as Meta’s Muse, which has 10 million users. Mayer’s startup has 10 engineers, according to the Times.
Mayer told the Times she thinks Dazzle could appeal in particular to women.
“Women, this is my own bias, tend to take more photos and are more visual, and so being able to work with A.I. in a visual medium is fun,” she said.
She also said Dazzle works just as well for men. Some power users spend hours a day with it, she said. Alter asked whether it was depressing to imagine AI planning birthdays, gifts and family holidays.
“I haven’t really thought that through,” Mayer said.
From Google to Dazzle
Mayer joined Google as its 20th hire in 1999 and led search there for a decade. She ran Yahoo from 2012 to 2017. Her startup scrapped its first apps, Sunshine Contacts and Shine. The idea for Dazzle came from Shine, she told the Times.
Asked about the small number of women leading AI companies, Mayer named Fei-Fei Li, who sold World Labs to AMD. She said gender balance in tech “will come in time”.

articles.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
articles.text:
The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it’s updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site.
The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
Previous reporting by The Verge found that Meta’s Muse could be used to effectively block other shoppers from purchasing items for hours.
The change comes days after The Verge reported that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal’s item reserve system. On the retailer’s website, an item goes “on hold” and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it’s placed in a user’s shopping cart. Using Meta’s Muse, The Verge was able to instruct the AI agent to continuously re-add The RealReal listings in a shopping cart as soon as the 20-minute hold had expired, effectively blocking other shoppers from purchasing products for hours or longer.
After publication, chief technology officer Luke Friang said in an email that the company had addressed the Muse use case flagged by The Verge’s story. The RealReal’s bot defense configuration now makes it much more difficult for all agents to log in, add items to cart, and check out, Friang said. Agents will still be able to surface listings from The RealReal and direct Muse users to product pages, Friang said, adding that the company will continue to strengthen protections as AI-powered online shopping evolves.
Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Technology companies are selling agents as personalized assistants for billions of people — always-on, compliant entities that will schedule meetings, throw parties, and purchase things for human users. So far, agents and shopping seem to go hand in hand; Meta said in its Q3 earnings call this month that it was the most common use case for Muse so far, and that purchases were over $200 on average. Muse has been a hit for Meta and could signal a turning point for AI agents: The company said 10 million people in the US had downloaded the app in 40 days.
But robots shopping for things instead of humans has the potential to upend the balance of the web as we know it. For one, if humans stop visiting websites directly and instead access the web through chatbots, businesses become one step removed from their customers. Retailers — most notably Amazon — have recognized that reality could disrupt their bottom line, especially advertising revenue, and have blocked agents from shopping on their sites.
An influx of AI agents accessing consumer platforms could also break or complicate even the most unexpected things shoppers take for granted, like the reserve system of a used clothing website. There is, of course, a realistic limit to how long a person is willing to spend adding and re-adding designer clothing to their shopping cart if they’re indecisive. An agent in contrast does not care. It is perhaps precisely the type of busywork a fashion-forward person might pay an actual personal assistant to do on their behalf. Now, a capability like this is at the fingertips of millions of consumers, and they are just beginning to learn how to take advantage of it. Retailers, too, are playing catch-up.

articles.title: Can you run regular Ethernet cables outside? - Engadget
articles.text:
Can you run regular Ethernet cables outside?
Just because you can do something doesn't mean you should.
Cable category terms like Cat5e and Cat6 have that industrial twang, so, understandably, some may assume they're tough enough for outdoor use. And they can do more than just improve home internet, which is especially helpful for security cameras on your porch or in your yard. Sure, you can use standard Ethernet cables outdoors, but you can also run outside in a lightning storm with a ten-foot metal pole above your head — just because you can do something doesn't mean you should. Standard indoor cables have a flexible PVC jacket, which is susceptible to sunlight. Over time it will fade and crack, exposing the internal components and ultimately degrading the connection.
Outside temperatures and rain accelerate the problem. The copper in an Ethernet cable won't have proper protection from lightning strikes and other elements. Use a cable specifically rated for outdoor exposure, such as a direct-burial-rated cable made for an in-ground run across the yard. Direct-burial cables are specifically designed for this, and it will be written clearly on the cable jacket. Whatever the cable rating, it's best practice to install surge protection on either end of the cable. While it requires additional hardware, you can avoid the risks of running copper outdoors by using outdoor-rated fiber optic cables instead of Ethernet, though any equipment exposed to the elements would still be at risk.
Use the right outdoor cable
There's a difference between a direct-burial and an outdoor Ethernet cable. Outdoor cables typically use a more weather-resistant polyethylene jacket (such as LLDPE or PE) instead of the standard PVC jacket. These materials are much better at resisting UV exposure, moisture, and wild temperature swings.
If the cable needs to run underground, opt for the direct-burial cable. These cables are capable of dealing with long-term exposure to moisture and the physical pressure of the surrounding soil. Depending on the type of direct-burial cable, it might use water-blocking tape, powder, or gel to keep the wire dry even if the outer jacket is damaged.
Local ordinances may not be happy with your buried wire, so be sure to check local rules on conduit, depth, and the cable types permitted. If all you need is a short and simple exterior run to an outdoor access point, a Cat6 outdoor-rated Ethernet cable is appropriate. Always secure exterior cable runs with cable clips to avoid abrasion, and never sharply bend the cable, even if that means the run requires a bit of creativity.
How to tell if an Ethernet cable is outdoor-rated
To make sure your cable can be used outside, check the printing on it. It's not always easy to read the small print, especially if it's faded a bit, so you might have to make an extra effort for it; the color or category label means nothing where this is concerned. Terms like "CMX," "OSP," "UV-resistant," "sunlight-resistant," or simply "outdoor" are what to look for. Outdoor cables will also often list their jacket material, such as PE, HDPE, or LLDPE. The National Electrical Code (NEC) requires communications cables installed in buildings to be listed and marked, and UL's guidance notes that cable evaluated for outdoor use is marked "outdoor" or "outdoor use," so the rating shouldn't be hard to confirm. Plus, the documentation that comes with them will state that they're approved for direct burial or wet locations.
Just note that an outdoor-rated cable doesn't mean its inherent toughness makes it an excellent indoor application. Some exterior cables may not meet the requirements for indoor fire safety hazards, and that includes situations where only a small section of the outdoor cable is run inside. An unlisted outdoor cable generally can't run more than 50 feet inside before it needs to terminate and transition to an indoor-rated cable, and shorter is better. Your best bet is to always read the cable's markings and any associated literature. If you're still unsure, check the local codes, especially for a permanent installation.

articles.title: Giá xăng dầu hôm nay 26/10: Thế giới hạ nhiệt, trong nước chờ tuần mới
articles.text:
Giá dầu thế giới hôm nay
Mở cửa phiên giao dịch đầu tuần này (26/10), giá dầu thế giới có xu hướng đi xuống, sau khi tăng nhanh ở tuần trước.
Dữ liệu từ Oilprice cho hay, vào lúc 6h36' ngày 26/10 (giờ Việt Nam), giá dầu Brent được niêm yết ở mức 115,8 USD/thùng, giảm 0,77% so với phiên liền trước. Còn giá dầu WTI được giao dịch ở mức 102,3 USD/thùng, hạ 0,9% so với phiên liền trước.
Trong tuần trước, giá dầu thế giới tăng mạnh. Tính chung trong cả tuần qua, giá dầu Brent tăng 6%, trong khi giá dầu WTI tăng 2,3%.
Giá dầu Brent đóng cửa tuần qua ở mức 116,7 USD/thùng, còn giá dầu WTI kết tuần trước ở mức 103,3 USD/thùng.
Dù giá dầu thế giới đi xuống khi mở cửa phiên giao dịch đầu tuần này nhưng vẫn duy trì ở mức cao trong bối cảnh giới đầu tư lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung dầu từ Trung Đông.
Trong phiên giao dịch cuối cùng của tuần trước (ngày 23/10), giá dầu thế giới đã tăng hơn 3%, đạt mức cao nhất trong gần 6 tháng, sau khi các cuộc tấn công của lực lượng Houthi nhằm vào Saudi Arabia làm dấy lên lo ngại về nguy cơ gián đoạn nguồn cung năng lượng từ Trung Đông - khu vực xuất khẩu dầu mỏ trọng yếu của thế giới.
Theo giới chức Mỹ và một số nguồn tin, lực lượng Houthi đã tiến hành nhiều hoạt động quân sự nhằm vào Saudi Arabia trong tuần trước.
Căng thẳng tiếp tục gia tăng khi truyền thông Iran đưa tin về các vụ nổ chưa rõ nguyên nhân tại khu vực Sirik ở miền nam nước này.
Lực lượng Vệ binh Cách mạng Hồi giáo Iran (IRGC) ngày 22/10 cho hay, 4 tàu liên quan đến hoạt động chuyển giao dầu bất hợp pháp ở phía Bắc Vịnh Ba Tư đã bốc cháy sau khi bị lực lượng này theo dõi.
Cùng thời điểm, cơ quan chức năng của Các Tiểu Vương quốc Ảrập Thống nhất (UAE) cũng thông báo phát hiện 1 vụ tràn dầu.
Bộ Biến đổi Khí hậu và Môi trường UAE cho biết đã phát hiện 1 vụ tràn dầu từ một tàu chở dầu ngoài khơi bờ biển Umm Al Quwain của UAE. Song cơ quan này không nêu rõ nguyên nhân gây ra vụ tràn dầu và các nhà chức trách chưa xác định được tàu chở dầu liên quan.
Ông Tamas Varga, nhà phân tích tại PVM Oil nhận định, nhiều thông tin cho rằng lượng dầu thô xuất khẩu từ Trung Đông đã vượt mức trước khi xung đột nổ ra, nhưng không đủ để bù đắp tác động từ các cuộc tấn công nhằm vào tàu thuyền tại eo biển Hormuz, cũng như các cuộc tấn công của lực lượng Houthi nhằm vào Saudi Arabia và cơ sở hạ tầng dầu mỏ của nước này.
Giá xăng dầu trong nước hôm nay
Giá bán của các mặt hàng xăng dầu phổ biến tại thị trường trong nước vào hôm nay (26/10) được áp dụng như sau:
Theo kỳ điều hành ngày 22/10, giá xăng E5RON92 giảm 1.610 đồng/lít so với kỳ trước, giá bán lẻ không cao hơn 25.361 đồng/lít.
Cùng xu hướng, giá xăng E10RON95-III hạ 1.816 đồng/lít, giá bán không cao hơn 25.213 đồng/lít.
Ngược lại, giá dầu diesel 0.05S được điều chỉnh tăng 444 đồng/lít, lên mức tối đa 29.550 đồng/lít.
Trong khi giá dầu mazut 180CST 3.5S được điều chỉnh tăng 1.238 đồng/kg, giá bán không cao hơn 23.373 đồng/kg.
Theo dữ liệu từ Bộ Công Thương, giá bán lẻ xăng dầu tại Việt Nam hiện ở mức thấp hơn so với các nước có chung đường biên giới.
Liên bộ Công Thương - Tài chính đang tiếp tục theo dõi sát diễn biến thị trường để thông báo giá xăng dầu phù hợp với diễn biến thị trường và kịp thời đề xuất Chính phủ, Thủ tướng các giải pháp bình ổn giá xăng dầu.

articles.title: The Tragedy of Having a Wikipedia Page—and Then Losing It
articles.text:
What do you need to know—need to know—about Xavier Trudeau? The eldest son of former Canadian prime minister Justin, the teenage Trudeau has recently begun performing R&B under the mononym Xav. But, with all due respect to Xav, do those facts make him a person of note? Should you expect to be able to read about him on Wikipedia? What about Evanescence guitarist Tim McCord, or 2012 Yachtmaster of the Year Rainer Holtorff?
All three have had a biography on Wikipedia; all three of those biographies were considered for deletion this year on the grounds that the subjects were not notable enough to warrant a biography at all. Every day, dozens, sometimes hundreds, of Wikipedia biographies—of child actors turned LA realtors, retired ambassadors, soccer players who have played less than 10 minutes of professional soccer—are purged from the world’s free encyclopedia.
It’s not as though Wikipedia, which hosts over 7 million articles in the English language, doesn’t have the space. But Wikipedia has only so many volunteers to monitor its contents. To this day, Wikipedia editors are discovering hoaxes that have gone undetected for decades. The time it takes to verify the release dates of Xav’s three singles is better spent—the logic goes—by asking whether the American Civil War officer Nathaniel Lyon really drank mustard during battle, as was claimed in his Wikipedia biography for 17 years. Wikipedia removed the mustard claim, not because it was proven wrong, but because there was no reliable evidence for it. “We’re not really looking for what’s true,” Britta Gustafson, who has been editing Wikipedia since 2001, told me. “We’re looking for what’s verifiable.”
Wikipedia editors do not themselves decide that a person is not notable, only that there is a lack of reliable evidence to support the claim. One person who recently lost her Wikipedia biography on notability grounds is Kimberly Small, the CEO of a Nevada nonprofit that supports survivors of sexual assault. The debate occurred in a public page on Wikipedia itself; it’s in that space that the really tricky decisions about what is and what isn’t good enough for the encyclopedia are made. One editor raised a question: “How should we judge not-for-profit executives? By the nature of their job, the focus is, as it should be, on the organization and the work the organization does, not them.” Another editor replied: “I don’t think there is anything wrong with not-for-profit executives being less often individually notable. Wikipedia coverage is not a prize.”
Is it not? “Having an article says something,” Gustafson admitted. “It implies something.” For six weeks over April and May, I reached out to hundreds of people who were about to lose their Wikipedia page, almost all of whom were learning that information from me. “If you want to write something to save the page, I would appreciate it,” a Spanish filmmaker told me. A biography on Wikipedia might not be intended as a prize, but nobody knows its value like the people who’ve had one and then lost it.
Martina Dimoska is a scientist, originally from North Macedonia, who works at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Specifically, Dimoska is an “analog astronaut”—she takes part in missions that simulate a space environment—and a “science communicator.” She posts often about her work in the can-do, aspirational register that is de rigueur on LinkedIn, where she cites her “recognition by … Forbes, Bloomberg, the United Nations … and global innovation networks.” A Facebook reel of hers, filmed during the crew announcement of NASA’s upcoming Artemis III mission, shows Dimoska alongside the text, “When you work hard so you belong in rooms where history gets proactively written.” On TikTok, she’s had paid partnerships with a makeup brand whose products are tested for effectiveness during spaceflight.
On April 29, Dimoska posted on Facebook, “Wait … I’m on Wikipedia now???” She went on: “A few years ago, building a career in space from the Balkans felt impossible. And now … somehow, that journey is part of the public record. I’m incredibly grateful that [the biography] is there … My hope is that through my journey, I will help a new generation to begin to see space as accessible, not distant.”
The next day, Dimoska’s page was nominated for deletion.
Anne Clin, who has edited Wikipedia since 2005 under the name Risker, warned me that it’s folly to celebrate becoming the subject of a Wikipedia article. “Especially if you’re what we call ‘borderline notable,’” she said.
The other taboo is editing information about yourself. You can’t do that—even if the existing facts about you are wrong—without disclosing a conflict of interest. Even then, it’s strongly discouraged. Jimmy Wales, the cofounder of Wikipedia, has been caught editing his own Wikipedia biography multiple times; that he did so is now part of his Wikipedia biography. In 2022, the novelist Emily St. John Mandel, unable to update her biography to reflect her recent divorce, sat for an interview solely to create a secondary source for that information.
Some high-profile Wikipedia editors and volunteers have bio pages about themselves. Clin is occasionally asked if she would want one. She doesn’t merely refuse; she actively sabotages the possibility. “You cannot write a proper biographical article about me, because I don’t give out enough personal information to do that,” she said. “Absolutely not. Absolutely not.”
Among the people reading Martina Dimoska’s Facebook post about her new Wikipedia page was Kiril Simeonovski, an economist in Skopje, Macedonia, and a Wikipedia editor since 2008. Simeonovski found the post self-congratulatory and the biography itself entirely promotional. He also doubted the inherent notability of an “analog astronaut,” a role that he later likened to a lab mouse.
A Wikipedia editor can tag an article for deletion, and unless satisfactory edits are made within a certain timeframe, the page will disappear. Simeonovski didn’t do this—he referred the article for debate among his fellow editors.
Arguing the case for deletion, Simeonovski described the Dimoska biography as “merely [a] chronology of overhyped personal achievements,” each meticulously deflated by Simeonovski, that did not credibly establish Dimoska as a notable individual.
More damningly, in his argument, was the timing of Dimoska’s Facebook post, coming “shortly after the article was approved.” To him, this was a smoking gun as much as anything. How could she have so promptly promoted the page if she were not somehow connected to it?
When an editor proposes a Wikipedia article for deletion, they append a caveat to the marked page: “If you created this page, please don’t take offense.” This courtesy is not extended to the subject of the article. When I reached out to these people, in the hundreds, to ask them how it felt to be considered non-notable, I was not surprised that the response rate to this question was about 1 percent. Maybe lower.
Matthew Songer, a Michigan orthopedist with three decades of experience, had his biography flagged for deletion (“Unlikely to be notable”) in April. Songer was among the 1 percent of respondees. He told me it’s not for vanity that he needs that page. He is often enlisted as an expert witness in trials, he said, because of the extra imprimatur of being on Wikipedia. The page “is a good reference for attorneys.”
Maneli Mirkhan, a French-Iranian adviser on international affairs, agreed that having a Wikipedia biography inspires confidence in her services. Her biography was called out by Wikipedia editors for reading like a résumé.
The biography of Andrew Wyant, a Phoenix-area executive who works in fitness and nutrition, was also deemed insufficiently notable, due to a lack of coverage from secondary sources. Wyant said he blamed himself for failing to “feed” his public persona through self-promotion. “What I know to be true is that I am largely responsible for the growth of the profession of personal trainers and fitness coaches by building the entire category over the last decade,” he told me. “I feel my accomplishments and impact are notable, but I don’t feel the need to promote them in media so I can have a Wikipedia page.”
Wyant’s biography was deleted. Songer’s biography was deleted. Mirkhan’s biography was deleted.
Of those, only Mirkahn’s reappeared, rewritten and with new sources, a few days later. I asked Mirkhan if she had been involved in re-creating the page. No, she said, but she wasn’t surprised. Mirkhan had been, and continues to be, sought out by the French media to comment on events in Iran, and more coverage means more demonstrations of notability. But there’s always that chicken-and-egg problem: Mirkhan thinks that what gave the media confidence in choosing her as a commentator was not just her career and her expertise. It was the fact that she was on Wikipedia.
Kiril Simeonovski did not lead with his suspicions that Martina Dimoska wrote her own Wikipedia biography. He argued, on Wikipedia’s public page for editorial debates, that the biography’s sourcing was weak, relying in part on posts from Dimoska’s LinkedIn page. It promoted Dimoska’s social media accounts, where she posted things like—and this Simeonovski found objectionable enough to cite in his argument for deletion—a picture comparing herself to NASA software engineer Margaret Hamilton. Published three separate times, it became one of her most popular posts, engendering sexist mockery and vicious defense.
To Simeonovski, self-promotion like this suggested that the case for Dimoska’s notability was regularly oversold by Dimoska herself. Though he could not prove a connection, it was difficult to imagine the Wikipedia biography as anything but an extension of that project.
That afternoon, a new Wikipedia user added comments to Simeonovski’s public arraignment, noting three existing articles about other individual analog astronauts. A fair contribution, tempered by a shot across the bow at Simeonovski: The user’s name was “Kiril’s mom.” The user was not Simeonovski’s mom, and the account was subsequently blocked. Hours later, another new user asked Simeonovski, rhetorically, “If I publish a blog post about someone and he finds it amazing and celebrates it does that mean that he/she created it?” Their username was a coded reference to the actual name of Simeonovski’s mother. They also got blocked.
Nine days later, another anonymous user—whose IP address, according to Simeonovski, placed them in Skopje, North Macedonia—said Dimoska’s biography had improved “considerably,” with new sourcing from publications like The Telegraph. The revised article, the user claimed, was superior to “85%” of Wikipedia articles about living Macedonians.
Three days later, Simeonovski dismantled each of the 32 new sources in turn. It wasn’t really the British newspaper The Telegraph that had been cited, for instance, but the Albanian news website Telegrafi. “I fail to find a single independent and reputable English-language source,” he later wrote.
The next day, the anonymous user rebutted Simeonovski point by point. They said it was “strange” that Simeonovski could not seem to find a single appropriate source for Dimoska’s biography but had found “10 sources from non-independent websites” when he wrote an article about the former governor of the National Bank of North Macedonia. The National Bank of North Macedonia, the user added to Simeonovski: Isn’t that where you work?
At one point, Simeonovski said he would report his detractor to the Wikimedia Foundation legal department.
Of Rosemary Bush, a professor at Northwestern University in Illinois, a Wikipedia editor recently wrote: “It will be many years until she qualifies as notable.” Bush herself agreed, to a point, that the Wikipedia page about her did not make a strong case, though she found the biography itself to be strange, possibly AI-generated, and not wholly representative of her career. “The world is fine without a Wikipedia page on me,” she said, but added, “I do think the comment proposing deletion is a bit rude.”
A little rudeness is unavoidable in this line of work. Sonia Jones, a Welsh singer best known for the theme song from the 1979 film Monty Python’s Life of Brian, is indeed best known for the theme song from Monty Python’s Life of Brian; therefore, Wikipedia editors decided that her Wikipedia biography should be deleted and henceforth redirect to the article about the song. Jones, when I asked her for a comment, did not agree that her achievements since 1979 do not merit documentation. “No, I do not want them to remove my page,” she said. “Why would they?”
“Canada has a national dodgeball team? Who would have thought?” wrote one editor in their case to delete the biography of Savannah Burton, the first transgender athlete to compete for Canada’s national dodgeball team. “Even though dodgeball is not considered a mainstream sport, competing at the highest level in any sport is a significant accomplishment,” Burton told me. “Given the ongoing attempts to erase transgender people, along with infringements on our rights and our ability to live normal lives, this action is not surprising.”
There is, when you look for it, a careless and cocky tone that can creep into the verdicts of Wikipedia editors who have been doing the job for a long time. “This guy is a nobody. Delete him.” “I’ve got more followers on Instagram than he does.” “All we have here are stand-up comedy, opinion columns, being a guest or collaborator on some non-notable podcasts … This is more or less every twentieth person who lives in NYC.”
Rosemary Bush’s biography was deleted. Sonia Jones’ biography was deleted. Savannah Burton’s biography was retained. “It was easy to find more sources,” wrote an editor who came to the page’s rescue. Editors’ participation in this process is not mandatory. Articles, once marked for death, can be deleted simply because nobody showed up to debate the matter. That anyone would volunteer their time to save an undeserving article from oblivion is a kindness: a good deed in a rude world.
Kiril Simeonovski never did refer the anonymous editor of Martina Dimoska’s biography to the Wikimedia Foundation’s legal team. Instead, he and his antagonist continued their debate on sourcing and semantics for days, and then weeks.
Per her Wikipedia page, Dimoska’s achievements included the command of two analog astronaut missions in Poland, but Simeonovski argued that while this information was verifiable, the missions themselves did not meet the threshold of notability and therefore neither did Dimoska. The anonymous user pointed to Dimoska’s inclusion in a Macedonian book for schoolchildren about 50 Macedonian women: “The book was subsequently recommended by the Bureau for Development of Education as optional reading material for ninth-grade students nationwide, which gives the subject recurring exposure within the educational system rather than temporary media attention.”
“You’ve apparently regressed to using children’s books to support the notability of the person we’re discussing,” said Simeonovski. “I expect [you] to continue gaslighting with multi-paragraph comments, but that won’t change the observation that the person isn’t notable [enough] for a Wikipedia article.”
“Count your words and then mine … and see who is the one gaslighting with multi-paragraph comments.”
“You seem to mix up ‘prominence’ and ‘notability.’”
“Your argument relies heavily on personal anecdotes and assumptions about how Macedonian media operates.”
Other editors with an eye on the debate pleaded for colleagues to lend their perspective. Most supported Simeonovski, but they didn’t linger long. “At this point the most visible thing about this individual seems to be [this] article,” one said, before bouncing.
As this unfolded, I asked Dimoska what she made of it. “The whole thing has become quite challenging to track,” she said, “and I’m already behind on my social media.” She denied editing the page herself or having any knowledge of the people defending it. She added: “Watching strangers debate your life, work, and credibility in such an intense way is definitely a strange experience to process.”
On April 25, a user named “DavidfromArizona” took to Wikipedia to announce that his friend Sheldon Marks—“the world’s leading vasectomy reversal expert,” per Marks’ own website—wished for his Wikipedia biography to be removed.
“It is inaccurate and does not truly represent his achievements,” David wrote. “[His] ego is hurt by having such a page. He either wants a detailed page or wants this one deleted.” A request from the subject of a Wikipedia article is not grounds for deletion in itself, although it can tip the balance if there is no clear consensus. On examination, Wikipedia editors found the biography lacking in sources that demonstrated notability.
On May 6, a Wikipedia user who 17 years earlier had created a biography for Sophie Aston, a British landscape artist, said that Aston had recently asked that the page be deleted. “She has retrained as a psychotherapist and wishes to forget her career as an artist.”
Having seen how much a Wikipedia page matters to certain people, I asked Marks and Aston why they wanted theirs removed.
“A kind and enthusiastic man made my Wiki page as a surprise for me about 17 years ago,” Aston told me. “We’d been on two dates. I found it a bit embarrassing but sweet. I didn’t see him again; I wasn’t into him. The info on the page was never [very] accurate and is now very out of date.” It was “ostentatious,” she added, for Wikipedia to present her as an artist of note, not least because for the past 10 years she has been a professional psychotherapist. The biography, she said, “makes it sound like I am an important artist, and I am not—it’s inappropriate.”
The Wikipedia editors could not treat Aston’s request with undue favor, but given the chance to cast fresh eyes over the article, they found her biography lacking. “The request to delete her article is not relevant,” one wrote bluntly, “but I don’t view her artistic career as meeting [notability] guidelines regardless of the request.” Aston’s biography was deleted.
Sheldon Marks didn’t respond to me. After receiving my email, however, he fled straight to the debate unfolding on Wikipedia. “I did not request deletion of this article,” he wrote. The statements made by DavidfromArizona, whom Marks did not know, were apparently fabrications. Marks wanted to keep his page. He admitted it could be improved but maintained that he was a notable individual: “I am the author of Vasectomy Reversal: Manual of Vasovasostomy and Vasoepididymostomy (Springer, 2018), translated into Chinese by Springer Nature in 2025; the surgical instrument known as the Marks Vas Cutting Forceps is named for me; I have served as Course Coordinator for the AUA post-graduate course on vasectomy reversal; and I have been a contributor to WebMD since 2005.”
The Wikipedia editors briefly conferred, then replied that they had already voted to delete.
There’s a final twist in the biography of Martina Dimoska: She knew Kiril Simeonovski—the guy trying to get her deleted.
“I had interacted with him on social media before and had crossed paths through mutual friends,” Dimoska said. “One recent example I remember clearly is seeing his post after he was injured by a cyclist who had left the scene.” Dimoska recalled the post in detail, though she had not responded or reacted to it at the time.
Simeonovski said he didn’t remember ever speaking with Dimoska in person but admitted the possibility of “virtual interaction.” Both are active on Facebook, and though they do not follow each other, Simeonovski said they have enough mutual friends in North Macedonia that their respective algorithms often put them in each other’s path. Just as Dimoska saw Simeonovski’s post about his accident, so Simeonovski came across Dimoska’s celebration of inclusion in Wikipedia, which led him to discover Dimoska’s earlier Instagram post comparing herself to Margaret Hamilton, then to a much older Reddit thread asking if Dimoska was the smartest Macedonian woman. (“Isn’t it just all hype about that girl?” one Redditor replied.) Simeonovski didn’t comment on any of those posts. But in Wikipedia he had found an opportunity to contest her notability on surer ground.
“It was somewhat surprising to me, perhaps because I have become accustomed to professional environments where people tend to be more openly supportive of one another’s work,” Dimoska told me. “At the same time, having grown up in North Macedonia, I am aware that recognition within a small community can sometimes generate more scrutiny than one might expect.”
One month after Simeonovski nominated Dimoska’s biography for deletion, he lost. The page was kept. “Given the bludgeoning, canvassing, and sockpuppetry evident here, this is a no consensus closure without prejudice against speedy renomination,” wrote an editor in a determination. “The arguments to delete here are stronger on the merits, but sufficient reasoned opposition exists that I do not see a consensus for deletion.” Obstinacy won the day, though Dimoska’s page now carries a disclaimer that it contains “promotional content.”
Wikipedia pages, for better or worse, matter to people. To be included is a validation of a life. If it were not so desirable, then one of the very first things Kiril Simeonovski did upon joining Wikipedia in 2008 would not have been to create a page about himself. Which he did do. He “wasn’t aware about the notability policies” back then, he told me.
The page was promptly deleted. “If your achievements, etc., are verifiable and genuinely notable and thus suitable for inclusion in Wikipedia,” an editor chided Simeonovski at the time, “someone else will probably create an article about you sooner or later.” To date, nobody has.

articles.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
articles.text:
Following reports of iPhone Duos with cracked and broken inside screens, often showing a bright line running from the center to the right side, Apple says in a statement to Bloomberg and 9to5Mac that it’s aware of “an issue impacting the inner display” on a “small number of iPhone Duo units.” If your iPhone Duo is affected, Apple says to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
Apple says a ‘small number’ of iPhone Duos have shown the cracked inner screen problem and that owners should contact AppleCare.
Here is the full statement, which Apple’s Alex Kirschner shared with The Verge:
The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Kirshner says most units aren’t susceptible and that the issues appear quickly on units with the defect.
Shortly after launch, iPhone Duo users started reporting similar issues where the hinge would tighten, and opening the device caused a crack and the distinctive bright lines on the display. One user in Australia said that an Apple Store replaced their unit “on the spot.”
This weekend, iFixit published its teardown of the phone and gave its perspective on why some phones might be cracking. Where the damage has been happening, iFixit shows how the foldable screen might be pushing against a center bar.
The Verge has contacted Apple about the reports, but has not received an on-the-record response about the issues with these new phones. They’re some of the first devices to launch after new CEO John Ternus took over from Tim Cook.
Updates, October 26th: Added Apple’s statement and additional context.

articles.title: Butterfield had one hour with Benioff before Salesforce bought Slack
articles.text:
Johnny Rodgers, one of Slack’s original eight team members, has written a first-hand account of Slack’s first two years inside Salesforce. It quotes Stewart Butterfield, Slack’s co-founder and former chief executive, throughout.
Rodgers spent 11 years at Slack and left in the spring of 2023. He published the second part of his Building Slack series on the Salesforce years on Friday.
“I only got about one hour of total facetime with Marc before the deal was announced. My last meeting with him was cut short because McConaughey arrived,” Butterfield told Rodgers, referring to Matthew McConaughey, one of Salesforce’s celebrity spokespeople.
Salesforce announced the deal in December 2020 at $45 a share. That was more than double Slack’s stock price at the time, as Rodgers recounted in part one in March.
Celebrities, tickets and email
Once the deal closed in 2021, the inefficiency Butterfield found at Salesforce “baffled” him, Rodgers writes. He says Butterfield watched executives approve expensive celebrity appearances while cutting travel between offices.
Rodgers also describes VPs hiring thousands of people and then laying off thousands in later quarters. An annual trip to Hawaii for senior staff, called Laulima, cost millions, he writes. Butterfield raised these issues with Benioff and Bret Taylor, then Salesforce’s co-CEO, but “it seemed to fall on deaf ears”, according to Rodgers.
Slack staff had to file tickets instead of asking in a channel, complete regular quizzes on Salesforce’s Trailhead platform, and use email again. Rodgers writes that Slack’s CEO had once joked that he would fire anyone who sent internal email.
A sales team that didn’t use Slack
The biggest gap was in sales, Rodgers writes. Salesforce sells to one department at a time, while Slack needed buy-in from a whole leadership team.
“Salesforce got put onto Slack [the product], but weren’t really using it, especially in Sales. They didn’t understand the product. So they sold the products they understood and were easier to sell vertically. Slack didn’t fit the pattern,” said Cal Henderson, Slack’s co-founder and former chief technology officer.
Benioff praised Huddles, Slack’s first big feature under Salesforce, at a company all-hands. But it was clear inside the company that Benioff himself did not use Slack and did not really understand it, Rodgers writes.
The Davos panel
Butterfield decided to leave in the autumn of 2022. The tipping point, he told Rodgers, was a trip to Davos to represent Slack and Salesforce. He expected to meet customers. Instead, he found himself on a panel about innovation with will.i.am, another Salesforce spokesperson.
In a leaked all-hands at the time, reported by Fortune, Butterfield described the problem himself.
“The problem has been, there’s no incorporation of the Slack culture into the Salesforce culture. And unless there is some element of that, then it’s not integration in any sense. It’s just elimination,” Butterfield said.
Butterfield planned to announce his exit on 1 December 2022. A day earlier, Taylor, who had brokered the deal, announced his own departure. Nobody had told Butterfield, Rodgers writes.
Slack has stayed central to Salesforce’s plans. It has given Slackbot 30 new AI features, and Benioff wants coding inside Slack next. In September, Meta said it was dropping Google Chat for Slack.
Rodgers, who is now building a company called Supergroup, says one more Building Slack post is to come.
