articles.title: From Wall Street to Silicon Valley, Anthropic IPO poised to have massive 'trickle-down effect'
articles.text:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic, which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet, which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon, Broadcom and Google, while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom, which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
Market reset?
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX, which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
Downside risks
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark.
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.
WATCH: Seems like Anthropic will beat OpenAI to IPO, says FirstMark's Rick Heitzmann

articles.title: Israeli election draws tens of thousands of citizens flying back to vote
articles.text:
An extremely tight race into Israel's election Tuesday, has some citizens flying back into the country to cast their votes.
Israel doesn't allow votes from abroad, except from those serving in the country's diplomatic missions. As many as 80,000 Israelis living outside the country are expected to come back to vote in Tuesday's election, according to estimates from one group helping to organize citizens living outside the country. Israel has about 7.3 million eligible voters, according to the Washington-based International Foundation for Electoral Systems.
"While not a large block, the 80,000 that may return home to participate could make a big difference in the final count of a very tight election," said Yael Shomer, a professor of political science at Tel Aviv University.
In Israel's first election since 2022, Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud party, who has served as Prime Minister for 18 years over three separate periods, is facing top challenger Gadi Eisenkot, the former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces, who heads the Yashar party. Both would likely need backing from potential coalition partners in order to win.
Polls are extremely tight heading into Tuesday's election. Issues like security, already a major decider for Israelis, have gotten even more contentious with the Iran war in full swing. The exemption of some ultra-Orthodox men from conscription is also causing a great divide in Israeli society, while Prime Minister Netanyahu is still working on a controversial plan that would give the governing coalition more control over the judiciary.
"All elections in Israel are energetic, but because this one will have such a meaningful impact on the future of the country it has been especially hard fought," Shomer said. "This election is really about how we see our future, voter turnout will be very high."
Voter turnout in 2022 was just above 70% according to Israel's Central Elections Committee. Pollsters believe it could reach as high as 87% this time. Among foreign service workers serving in embassies and consulates outside of Israel, voter turnout was 90%. According to The Central Elections Committee, that number is usually closer to 70%.
In order to help those living abroad come back to cast votes, an organization called Fly & Vote was set up by the America-Israel Democracy Coalition, a U.S.-based group which was originally created in 2023 to stop the effort by Likud to reform the judicial system.
While organizations and political parties are prohibited from paying for any kind of transportation for people inside or outside of Israel, Aid Coalition has found other ways to facilitate the voting.
Fly & Vote, which has been funded by private donations, chartered a flight for Israelis living in Portugal and bought blocks of tickets for flights from the New York area. Anyone on the flights had to pay for their own seats.
"Israelis who don't live here still have a stake in what we do, and we want to help them," said Ora Peled-Nakash, the group's co-founder. "We don't take a political position though and we don't tell anyone how to vote, we just help them cast their ballot."
Travelers will also have plenty of commercial options.
For decades El Al was the only Israeli airline to fly routes from the U.S. to Israel. Arkia started offering flights last year and Israir earlier this year. Legacy U.S. carriers United and Delta are also flying to Israel again after suspending flights due to the war with Iran. Germany's Lufthansa flies to Israel from Europe and British Airways is scheduled to re-start flights this week.
What's more, the price is in line with what it would be during normal times, Peled-Nakash said. There were still a few seats left on El Al flights from JFK or Newark airports ranging from $1,300 to $2,500 as of Sunday, according to research from CNBC.
After years of political instability that saw five elections between 2019 and 2022, Tueday's election result could help shape Israel's political, security and economic direction for years to come. But it also shows how politically divided the country has become.

articles.title: BlackBerry reinvented: CEO sees big opportunities AI-powered robots
articles.text:
BlackBerry CEO John Giamatteo sees artificial intelligence-powered robots as a major growth opportunity for the former smartphone king.
Once one of the world's biggest mobile phone makers, Canada-based BlackBerry has reinvented itself.
The company's QNX operating system, which provides underlying software for features ranging from braking systems to some semi-autonomous driving functions, is now embedded in more than 275 million vehicles worldwide. But the company is increasingly looking beyond the automotive industry to capitalize on the emerging market for physical AI.
"While the products we sell today can't be held in the palm of your hand, they're pervasive around you," Giamatteo told CNBC's Jim Cramer on Monday. "275 million cars, robots, governments, medical instrumentation, supply chain. That's the new BlackBerry, and that's what's driving all of our growth."
Robotics has already emerged as one of the fastest-growing businesses within QNX, according to Giamatteo. Unlike generative AI, which produces text and images, physical AI allows robots and other machines to interact with the real world. BlackBerry sees an opportunity to provide the underlying software that helps those machines operate safely and reliably, building on its experience in the automotive industry.
That opportunity is contributing to BlackBerry's growing backlog. The company recently announced that its QNX royalty backlog surpassed $1.2 billion, increasing by more than $250 million over two quarters. Giamatteo identified three drivers behind that growth: automakers' transition to more advanced computing systems, expanded software offerings, and emerging demand for physical AI applications.
Investors have taken notice of the turnaround. BlackBerry shares have surged 142% in 2026, following years of struggles for a company whose formerly ubiquitous handhelds with physical keyboards ruled the smartphone world before Apple's iPhone and other devices that were fully touchscreen. Back then called Research in Motion, the stock saw its market cap peak at nearly $85 billion in 2008, a year after the first iPhone. BlackBerry's current market cap is about $5.4 billion.
Giamatteo also highlighted BlackBerry's partnership with Nvidia, which began in the automotive sector. Nvidia has now "standardized on QNX as the platform of choice" for its Halos Safety Stack, Giamatteo said. "That has opened up so many doors, an incredible pipeline of opportunity, and these are things like AMRs (automated mobile robots), autonomous forklifts, skateboards that are driving pallets to the docking station."

articles.title: Jim Cramer warns this overlooked danger could threaten the market rally
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer warned Monday that a wave of massive initial public offerings and capital raises could threaten the bull market.
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, filed its IPO prospectus Monday, moving one of Wall Street's most anticipated public debuts a step closer. Investors have long awaited public offerings from AI leaders Anthropic and OpenAI, but Cramer said that their potentially massive fundraising needs could strain an already crowded market. With $148 billion raised through IPOs so far this year, he fears the influx of new shares could outstrip investor demand and derail the rally.
"Politics can weaken the bull, higher rates can choke it, but if you want to slay the darn thing, use the IPO lance and stab it again and again," the "Mad Money" host said. "It just gets weaker and weaker until it is weak enough to be slaughtered with the ease of a bad quarter, a rate hike and a run on the margin bank."
Cramer emphasized that his concerns aren't about the viability of AI itself. Unlike the speculative internet startups that collapsed during the dot-com bust in 2000, many of today's leading technology companies have established businesses and genuine demand for their products.
"This time around the companies are real. They tend to make big money. We trusted them before this moment. We will trust them after," he said.
But Cramer sees one troubling similarity between the two periods: the enormous amount of capital being raised. During the dot-com boom, a flood of stock offerings eventually exhausted investors' buying power, contributing to the market's collapse. Supply outpaced investor demand.
He fears a similar dynamic could emerge as companies including Meta, Alphabet, SpaceX and Oracle tap capital markets. Cramer warned that these massive fundraising efforts could absorb investor dollars that might otherwise flow into the S&P 500 and other stocks, putting pressure on the broader market even as corporate fundamentals remain strong. Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of Meta and Alphabet.
"I think both the debt and the equity markets are running out of money," he said.
That means the market could run out of the money companies need to finance their ambitions before investors see the payoff. "I am not calling a top," he said. "I am just saying that I do not like what I see."

articles.title: Stock futures are little changed after Wall Street starts the week on a winning note: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures were little changed on Monday night following a winning session on Wall Street, with traders looking ahead to a slew of corporate earnings while the Federal Reserve gets set to begin its two-day policy meeting.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slipped 8 points, or less than 0.1%, while S&P 500 futures were marginally lower. Nasdaq-100 futures added 0.1%.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.7% while the Topix gained 0.4%. South Korea's Kospi advanced 3.8% and the tech-focused, small-cap Kosdaq gained 2.9%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.32% lower.
Wall Street kicked off the week on a solid note. The Dow climbed 146.42 points, or 0.3%. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.8% as tech shares outperformed. The artificial intelligence trade got a boost after Anthropic filed to go public at the Nasdaq. This would mark another major tech IPO for 2026, following SpaceX's blockbuster listing in June.
Tesla shares advanced more than 5%, while Nvidia climbed 2%. Microsoft and Amazon also rose on the day.
Those gains come as the artificial intelligence trade has faced pressure from investors worried companies in the space are borrowing too much cash to fund their AI build-outs.
On Tuesday, traders will pore through a deluge of third-quarter earnings reports. Coca-Cola, Robinhood and Boeing are among the companies set to post results. Tech giants Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are due out later in the week.
The Fed is also set to kick off its latest monetary policy meeting. While the central bank is expected to keep rates unchanged, traders will look for clues on whether another rate hike will take place before year-end.
"If, as expected, there is no change in rates, it will still be interesting to see what the vote is after the swings in the last two meetings," wrote Thomas Block, Washington policy strategist at Fundstrat. "While the Fed views itself above partisan politics, it would be unlikely that the Fed would move rates a week before a national election."
On the economic front, traders will be watching for durable orders, consumer confidence data and the new home sales report.

articles.title: Bessent dines at Cheesecake Factory, slams Obama over Trump joke
articles.text:
Let them eat cheesecake?
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday became the latest right-wing critic to accuse former President Barack Obama of elitism for mockingly comparing President Donald Trump's ostentatious White House renovations to the Cheesecake Factory.
But Bessent, a former hedge fund manager whose net worth has been estimated at around $600 million, put his money where his mouth is — dining at the chain restaurant and praising its food before giving the Democratic ex-president a slice of his mind.
"This is the man who built the museum [that] looks like Darth Vader's tomb," Bessent told a Fox Business reporter who asked about Obama's remark as he left the restaurant. Bessent was apparently referring to the Obama Presidential Center, a monolithic structure that opened in June.
"I had a great meal, always have a great meal, and I would just tell the Martha's Vineyard set to give it a try," Bessent said. Obama vacationed on Martha's Vineyard as president, and he and his wife Michelle now own an estate on the exclusive island.
Bessent said he ordered "what I always have: the French Dip Cheeseburger."
That's a "Charbroiled Cheeseburger Served on a Toasted Brioche Roll with Grilled Onions, Sriracha Mayo and Au Jus for Dipping," one of the "Glamburgers" on Cheesecake Factory's famously sprawling menu. The burger, which comes with french fries or a green salad, currently costs $22.95 at the restaurant's downtown Washington location.
"I recommend the Cheeseburger Spring Rolls," Bessent added in a follow-up post on X directed at Obama.
Bessent's biting comment followed those of other Trump allies who claim Obama sneered at working-class Americans when he tore into Trump over his extensive White House construction and decoration projects.
"I don't know if you've noticed, but he seems very focused on home renovations. He should be on HGTV!" Obama said of Trump during a speech at an Ohio rally for gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton and Senate candidate Sherrod Brown on Saturday.
"There's gold everywhere. What's up with the gold?" Obama went on. "He's got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory."
The crowd erupted in cheers and laughter at the remarks from Obama, who has previously poked fun at Trump's gold-heavy remodel of the White House.
Since retaking office, Trump has devoted significant amounts of time to discussing his renovations, including in the Oval Office, which now features heaps of gold leaf among many additional decorations. He has also built a White House helipad, the still-under-construction White House ballroom and an array of other projects.
Trump on Monday afternoon defended his White House redesign at length while claiming Obama had failed to address needed repairs.
"We have to explain to Obama that the White House is a symbol of America, and it has to be maintained properly," Trump said as he headed to Mississippi for a campaign rally. "Guys like Obama don't see it. You don't see dirt. He doesn't see filth. He doesn't see broken ornaments on a building."
"It has to be clean," Trump continued. "The columns can't be broken. The bricks can't be falling off from under the plaster. And for you to say it's a cheesecake factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president." 
Detractors insisted Obama's use of the Cheesecake Factory as an example of cheap, gaudy decor amounted to no less than class warfare.
"Classic Obama snobbery," Republican commentator Matt Whitlock wrote on X. "Cheesecake Factory is a great option for people who can't afford a private chef at their Martha's Vineyard estate."
GOP pundit Scott Jennings called Obama "undefeated at condescending to regular folks," while claiming the former president "has never been in a Cheesecake Factory."
That backlash quickly sparked its own backlash.
"This is actually a condescending view of working-class people," wrote Derek Guy, a popular menswear influencer, on X.
"I grew up in a working-class immigrant family and we ate at Red Lobster and The Cheesecake Factory for 'fancy nights out.' But even we understood that the White House should not look like the inside of a Red Lobster," Guy wrote. "Working-class people are not culturally illiterate just because their experiences are shaped by their limited means."
The food fight is taking place just days before the Nov. 3 midterm election, where most polls and analyst projections indicate Democrats are poised to make significant gains in Congress.
The election cycle has been defined by Americans' widespread unhappiness with high costs, which has dragged Trump's approval ratings to new lows and imperiled Republicans' majorities in the House and Senate.
The Cheesecake Factory is set to report its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday.

articles.title: DOJ charges ex-FBI Director James Comey in new case
articles.text:
Former FBI Director James Comey has been charged for the third time with federal crimes, according to a court filing unsealed Monday in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., at Comey's request.
Comey is accused in the new case with knowingly communicating information related to national defense to a person not entitled to receive it.
He is also charged with conspiring with others to violate the law against sharing such information.
The charging document, known as an information, says Comey, "through one or more co-conspirators," directed an unnamed individual "to disclose national defense information to a reporter for a national news publication."
According to a court filing by Comey, who is seeking to dismiss the new case, the information relates to the "alleged disclosure of classified information" to The New York Times on Oct. 5, 2016.
Comey's lawyers told a judge in that filing that the alleged disclosure "was investigated by two separate U.S. Attorneys over the past ten years. Both declined to prosecute."
Comey has been repeatedly targeted by the Department of Justice under the administration of President Donald Trump, who fired him as FBI director in 2017. Both men have been fierce critics of one another since then.
The DOJ filed the information against Comey on Oct. 5 and asked a judge to seal it, citing the risk that an ongoing criminal investigation would be compromised by the charges becoming public. Judge Trevor McFadden granted that request that day.
Attorneys for Comey, whom the DOJ agreed should be notified of the information, filed a motion to dismiss the case on Oct. 9, arguing that the 10-year statute of limitations to file a grand jury indictment relating to events of Oct. 5, 2016, had expired.
Comey's lawyers accused the DOJ of filing "a faulty information under seal" in an effort to put the statute of limitations on hold.
The attorneys on Monday asked McFadden to unseal the information, and the judge agreed to do so.
Comey separately is currently seeking the dismissal of an indictment obtained by the DOJ in North Carolina federal court on charges of threatening Trump's life by posting a photo of seashells on a beach on social media. He previously successfully won dismissal of another indictment accusing him of falsely testifying to Congress.
The new criminal complaint came to light hours after a federal judge in New York ruled that the Department of Justice had unlawfully fired Comey's daughter, Maurene Comey, last year as an assistant U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York.
"Well, they're back — again," James Comey said in a video message on Substack addressing the new case.
"It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice, one that we cannot become numb to," he said. "Nothing's changed with me. I'm still innocent. I'm still not afraid of these people, and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary."
"And I'm still lucky to have an amazing family and an incredible group of lawyers that will stand up in court and fight the latest and whatever comes after this," Comey said. "The next couple of years are going to be hard for all of us. It's really important that we stand straight and keep the faith in America."
In the pending indictment in North Carolina, Comey in late April was charged with threatening Trump's life by posting on Instagram a photo of seashells on a beach arranged to form the numbers "86 47."
Prosecutors claim that the number "86" — which is often used in restaurants to indicate a menu item is no longer available — was code for suggesting someone kill Trump, who is the 47th U.S. president.
Comey has denied any wrongdoing in that case and is seeking to have the indictment tossed out by a judge.
Comey was first indicted in September 2025 by a federal grand jury in Virginia on charges of making a false statement and obstruction, in connection with testimony he gave before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Sept. 30, 2020.
Comey, in that testimony, denied authorizing another person at the FBI to serve as an anonymous source in news reports regarding an investigation of Hillary Clinton and her emails when she was the Democratic presidential nominee in 2016.
That first indictment was dismissed by a judge on Nov. 24, 2025, after the judge ruled that Lindsey Halligan, a then-interim U.S. attorney who obtained the indictments, had been invalidly appointed.
On the same day the judge tossed Comey's case for that reason, the same judge dismissed an unrelated indictment obtained by Halligan against New York Attorney General Letitia James, who had been accused of bank fraud and making false statements to a financial institution in connection with a home mortgage she obtained in 2020.
James, like Comey, has been a staunch critic of Trump, and a target of the president's ire.

articles.title: Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: Whirlpool, JetBlue, Celestica & more
articles.text: Here are some of the companies making headlines in extended trading. Whirlpool — The home appliance maker dropped almost 9% after slashing its full-year revenue guidance to $14.5 billion from $15 billion. Revenue in the third quarter also fell short of estimates, coming in at $3.68 billion versus the $3.92 billion LSEG consensus estimate. The company also lost an adjusted 21 cents per share, while analysts expected a profit of 80 cents per share. JetBlue Airways – The air carrier surged 7% after the company said that it expects further margin expansion in the fourth quarter even as fuel prices are anticipated to be 85% higher than a year earlier. JetBlue reported an adjusted loss of 60 cents a share in the third quarter, compared to the 55-cent loss analysts polled by LSEG had sought. Revenue narrowly missed expectations, as well. Amkor Technology – The provider of semiconductor test services added 5% after third-quarter revenue came in at $1.99 billion. That's higher than Amkor's earlier call for $1.90 billion, but just below the FactSet consensus call for $2.04 billion. Celestica – Shares of the supply chain management company jumped 10% after Celestica hiked its full-year guidance. The company sees adjusted earnings of $11.55 per share, up from its earlier call for $11.30 per share and beating the FactSet consensus forecast for $11.16. Rambus — The semiconductor name fell 2% despite reporting sharp year-over-year earnings and revenue growth for the third quarter. Rambus earned 84 cents per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $218.3 million. That represents growth of 35% on the bottom line and 22% for the top line, respectively, year on year. Public Storage — Shares were little changed even after the storage company reported better-than-expected results for the third quarter. Public Storage also raised its full-year funds from operations forecast. Cadence Design Systems — The electronic systems design company advanced 2% after third-quarter results surpassed estimates. Cadence Design earned $2.11 per share on an adjusted basis and posted revenue of $1.63 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG sought $2.05 per share and $1.61 billion. The company also lifted its full-year revenue growth outlook.

articles.title: JetBlue posts bigger loss on fuel costs, but CEO says margins improving
articles.text:
JetBlue Airways reported a bigger loss in the third quarter compared with last year, but the New York carrier said strong travel demand is helping to offset higher fuel prices as it seeks to calm investors after shares fell to a new low Monday.
JetBlue stock soared roughly 11% in after-hours trading Monday.
JetBlue on Monday posted a net loss of $257 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, compared with a loss of $143 million a year earlier. The carrier's fuel bill rose 61% to $868 million.
"Resilient demand and strong yields drove revenue well ahead of our initial expectations, allowing us to recapture more of the increase in fuel costs than we initially expected," CEO Joanna Geraghty said in an earnings release. "That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, and Fort Lauderdale continues to deliver exceptional results even as we significantly grow capacity."
JetBlue's average fares rose more than 19% to $245.11 in the third quarter from $205.67 in the year-earlier period.
JetBlue executives are set to hold an earnings call on Tuesday at 10 a.m. ET, where they will face questions from analysts about the company's long-term health amid sustained losses. A group of the airline's senior creditors is reportedly working with restructuring adviser PJT Partners, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
The carrier said it ended the quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and that its unencumbered asset base is now $7 billion, including $2.8 billion in aircraft and engines.
JetBlue had total debt of $8.4 billion as of Sept. 30, the carrier said in its earnings filing Monday.
"Importantly, we believe we have the liquidity and financing options to create a strong bridge to at least $1 EPS and positive free cash flow in 2028," CFO Ursula Hurley said in a statement. "We remain focused on disciplined cost execution and capital management as we work toward sustained profitability and positive free cash flow."
Here is what JetBlue reported in the third quarter compared with Wall Street estimates compiled by LSEG:
- Loss per share: 60 cents adjusted vs. a loss of 55 cents expected
- Revenue: $2.81 billion vs. $2.82 billion expected
JetBlue last posted an annual profit in 2019. The airline is in the middle of a multiyear turnaround plan that includes cutting cuts and boosting revenue by investing in premium seats, like a new domestic first class section that recently went on sale.
Fuel costs have eaten into airline profits across the board. JetBlue said travel demand has remained strong despite higher fares, which are up more than 20% this year.
JetBlue has struggled not just with higher costs but also with competition from larger rivals.
It sought to acquire now-defunct carrier Spirit Airlines, but that deal was upended by a federal judge who ruled it was anticompetitive. A judge also blocked a regional partnership between JetBlue and American Airlines, which the airlines argued would help them compete better against carriers in the congested Northeast U.S. JetBlue now has a partnership with United Airlines.

articles.title: Meta, SpaceX, Anthropic stoke the AI funding frenzy. What it means for our stocks
articles.text: The AI funding window is closing, and everyone wants a seat on the train. Clearly, the rush to raise capital is on, as more and more artificial intelligence-focused companies are feeling pressure to continue building to keep up. We know the demand for everything AI — from models to agents to chips to data centers — keeps growing and growing. But Wall Street is now becoming more discerning about which companies it wants to bet on during the next phase of what is being called the fourth industrial revolution. The insatiable need for capital is the bottleneck. Unlike the initial push to spread money around to bet on would-be AI winners, there is not enough to go around at this stage. The smaller cloud companies in recent weeks have been at the forefront of this rationalization push. CoreWeave has become the face of the "do we have too many neoclouds" debate. The stock has lost 60% from its year-to-date high of nearly $139 on May 6. It hit a 52-week low of just above $51 on Monday before moving higher with the broader market. Make no mistake about it, some of the biggest companies in the world need more money, too. Club name Meta Platforms , as well as SpaceX and Anthropic, are dominating the headlines on Monday with plans to raise their share of the shrinking capital pie for the next legs of their AI ambitions. Meta announced plans to raise as much as $95 billion in three steps: first, an additional $22.5 billion worth of Class A common (what we and most investors currently own) priced at $642.62 per share; another $12.5 billion of preferred shares; and $60 billion no sooner than next year via an at-the-market offering for Class C shares. We learned about the plans to create the non-voting Class C shares last week as a vehicle to raise money in the future. Who knew the future was only a few short days away? Elon Musk said that SpaceX has closed a $40 billion debt financing deal for graphics processing units (GPUs). We previously learned that SpaceX would look to exclusively build on Nvidia hardware. Remember, while SpaceX is a rocket and satellite company, it is also a massive AI infrastructure company. Anthropic dropped its initial public offering prospectus. The frontier AI lab, whose IPO valuation could be as high as $2 trillion, filed its so-called S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The share pricing and initial raise were not disclosed. They will come later. However, it is probably safe to say it will be for tens of billions of dollars, if not $100 billion, given the level of financial commitments the company has disclosed in the filing. These three are just the latest in a mad rush for capital that has been putting a strain on the AI trade. The bulls argue that the demand means the compute is needed and the investments being made now will provide positive returns. The bears argue that there is a grave misallocation of capital underway, as the AI hype won't be met with AI profits down the line, and the compute demand everyone is predicting won't materialize. In a post on X confirming SpaceX's debt raise, Musk put those challenges in context . "As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. ... That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many." The neoclouds have a real problem. There is little doubt about that. The bigger question for us: Is that going to be a problem for everyone else? We don't think so, as Jim Cramer wrote in his Sunday column , saying he is not giving up on the AI trade, especially for the companies on the other side of Musk's "guppy" trade. We're talking about the ones that do more than AI. Last week, we argued that the key strategic advantage for the Meta Super Intelligence Lab (MSL) is that Meta Platforms, the broader company, has a wildly profitable core advertising business that gives MSL a structural advantage versus pure-play AI labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. A similar advantage can be found at the infrastructure layer, with hyperscalers Microsoft , Amazon , and Alphabet . Microsoft's other business is enterprise software found most on most personal and work computers. Amazon has e-commerce. Alphabet, like Meta, has a strong ad business. If many lower-quality neocloud players go under due to lack of funding, then it should read as a positive for the survivors long-term. (However, there is no getting around the near-term headline risk of any neocloud blowups. Investors will be selling first and asking questions later.) The reason why is that demand won't evaporate if a neocloud goes under. The companies doing business with CoreWeave, Nebius , or Iren aren't after doing business specifically with those providers, as much as they are after the gigawatts of compute they have stood up at prices and services they like. Because the industry has standardized around a few players, like Nvidia and a few custom chipmakers, tied into the larger hyperscalers that are the ones soaking up all the excess capital. It won't be an issue for the customers to move their workloads. It's a simple equation: fewer suppliers, with equal demand, amounts to more share for each supplier. Bottom line As is usually the case with choppy periods in any given industry, if trouble hits and players start getting their legs taken out from under them, it's those that have the financial durability to come out standing on the other side and reap the rewards. That brings us back to the biggest names, like Club stocks Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon, which are all set to report quarterly results this week. We expect funding to be the hot topic of conversation during their post-earnings conference calls. During Monday's Morning Meeting , Jim thought that Microsoft and Amazon would be feeling the most heat to raise funds following Meta's move Monday and Alphabet's $85 billion stock sale over the summer. UBS suggests that Amazon's 2027 capital expenditures plan could exceed $300 billion, even as the analysts raised their price target on the cloud and e-commerce giant and reiterated their buy rating. The UBS note gets at the heart of the issue and speaks to the conclusion of Jim's weekend column. Caution is warranted in the near term. We've certainly lightened up on our AI exposure in recent weeks, including an exit of Broadcom on Friday, due to funding uncertainty. Long term, however, you have to stick with the trade, pick your spots like the hyperscalers and Nvidia, and take advantage of weakness in the highest quality names, "because the revolution is real." The question, as Jim puts it: "How many will be left?" (See here for a full list of the stocks in Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust.) articles.title: Anthropic's IPO puts power in the hands of founders, giving everyday shareholders little voice
articles.text:
Prospective Anthropic investors better buckle up, because the AI company's seven co-founders are firmly in the driver's seat.
The Amodei siblings — Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei — and five others will be the "sole members" of "Founder LLC," a new entity that will hold 50.1% of the voting power of the company's outstanding shares. The structure gives them "the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of our stockholders generally for the foreseeable future," Anthropic said in its IPO prospectus on Monday.
The arrangement will also limit the power and influence of institutional and retail investors, who will have to put their trust in a small band of artificial intelligence engineers and researchers as the company marches toward a trillion-dollar-plus market cap. Anthropic has long tried to establish itself as the more safety-conscious AI lab, and it's created a structure designed to give its founders the ability to preserve that long-term mission, even as it enters the world of quarterly financial reports.
"Our governance structure is likely to have the effect of limiting the likelihood of an unsolicited merger proposal, unsolicited tender offer, or proxy contest for the removal of directors," Anthropic said in the filing. "As a result, our governance structure may make it more difficult to replace our directors and management and may have the effect of depriving our stockholders of an opportunity to sell their shares at a premium over prevailing market prices."
Anthropic's "novel capital and corporate governance structure" serves as another layer of complexity for investors to consider as they pore over the company's prospectus, which includes more than 90 pages of risk factors. Anthropic highlighted a number of political challenges, data center moratoriums and the company's effort to balance safety and commercial objectives as potential risks.
For some investors, founder control is a defining characteristic of generational tech companies.
Byron Deeter, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, told CNBC Monday that "when you have great leadership," investors are often comfortable giving early management and founders governance into the public market. Bessemer backed Anthropic at a $14 billion valuation, and Deeter said it's the biggest investment on a cost basis in the firm's 116-year history.
SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk has retained roughly 85% of the voting power at his rocket maker, while Meta co-founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg has around 60% of the voting power at the social media giant. Both executives have positioned themselves as indispensable to their companies, which can also put them at odds with their investors.
"There are some unusual elements to these things when they occur, but for category-defining, industry-defining opportunities, you want teams to be able to think long term," Deeter told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Monday. "And there are a lot of benefits to being able to do that so teams can focus on true innovation, and not be month-to-month, or even quarter-to-quarter."
Sam Altman remains a powerful figure at competitor OpenAI, especially since many of his original co-founders have departed. Unlike Amodei, Altman has no direct equity in his company and OpenAI's current structure doesn't offer a similar voting bloc like the one Anthropic created through Founder LLC.
Aside from the Amodeis, Anthropic's founding team includes Tom Brown, chief compute officer; Jack Clark, head of the Anthropic Institute; Jared Kaplan, chief science officer, Sam McCandlish, chief architect; and Christopher Olah, head of interpretability research efforts.
Anthropic's Founder LLC builds on its existing status as a public benefit corporation, which means it's required to balance the financial interest of stockholders, the best interests of those affected by its conduct and its "Company Purpose," which is to facilitate the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity."
In addition, Anthropic introduced an independent governance body called the "Long-Term Benefit Trust" in 2023, which has the authority to elect and remove the majority of the company's board of directors. The LTBT will exercise that authority using a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, which "does not otherwise have voting rights on matters submitted to stockholders generally," according to the prospectus.
The LTBT currently includes Christopher Stubbs, an experimental physicist, Ben Bernanke, the former chair of the Federal Reserve, Neil Buddy Shah, CEO of the Clinton Health Access Initiative, and Richard Fontaine, a national security expert. All the trustees are "financially disinterested" from Anthropic, according to the filing.
Anthropic is considered a "controlled company," according to Nasdaq Global Select Market corporate governance requirements, because the LTBT has the authority to elect the majority of its board. Anthropic said it plans to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol "ANT."
Anthropic's co-founders will have the authority to elect the company's remaining board members through their capacity within Founder LLC. It said Monday that it believes its co-founders are "distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission."
The company said the voting power of Founder LLC and its LTBT are "not derived from or proportionate to economic interests" in the company, and won't be diluted or otherwise reduced. The company said its capital structure will concentrate voting power within these two entities for "the foreseeable future."
"Moreover, the LTBT, Founder LLC, and our individual co-founders may have interests that differ from yours and may vote in a way with which you disagree and that may be adverse to your interests," Anthropic said.

articles.title: As AI becomes more fractured, one names stands out: AMD
articles.text:
As Anthropic rushes to takes its shares public, the AI trade is showing cracks, and they are not confined to fringe players.
We recently wrote about CoreWeave, which fell 15.5% on Oct. 14 as yields on its 2032 notes touched 15%, and its default-swap spreads nearly doubled in October. IREN is down more than 20% this year. Last Thursday, the contagion reached chipmakers, which makes sense since much of CRWV and IREN's spending is going there. AMD dropped 8.1% as Meta's financing plans and a supply warning from Lam Research exacerbated data-center fears about the pace of AI spending.
So why be bullish?
Because when you screen for factors that demonstrably generate outperformance over time, the list narrows quickly. My screen: price above the 200-day moving average; revenue growing at least as fast as the S&P 500 (5%+ per annum); EPS growing at least as fast (7%+); rating upgrades; a PEG below 3; and ROE and ROIC of at least 12%. Of the names reporting in the next two weeks, AMD is effectively the only one that makes the list. Yes, you can (and arguably should, as our staples article described) position your portfolio with slightly less tech exposure than the broad indices provide, but we can't ignore the market's biggest and most transformative sector entirely.
Especially because the growth in this case doesn't just meet my criteria; it blows past them. Consensus for Q3 calls for EPS of $1.94 on revenue of $13.06 billion, versus $1.20 and $9.25 billion a year ago. That's YoY growth of nearly 62% and 41%, respectively. The recent drawdown came from a sector selloff, not anything AMD reported, but it shows that if some names in the space get hit, even the larger players are likely to feel it. On Oct. 6, Lisa Su said AMD would substantially increase supply in 2027 because AI orders keep outrunning capacity.
So how do you balance factors we know work for a fast-growing company against a backdrop of cracks in the AI trade? Options.
The trade
Owning the stock outright means absorbing a roughly 9% to 11% implied earnings-related move (day of). Earnings are about a week out, and over the past four quarters the smallest move over a similar window was more than 9%, and the largest move, after the company reported its Q1 26 results, was 38%! Of course, that kind of volatility means options aren't cheap, and that rich premium is also a reason not to simply buy calls.
A call spread risk reversal does both jobs: it reduces risk if the cracks widen, and the short options offset the elevated volatility we would otherwise pay for. The bottom chart shows that, by sacrificing about $1,700 of upside for $5,000 in outperformance during a severe downside move, and given how jittery this trade has been lately, this is a way to stay in it with considerably less risk. $5,000 less, specifically. Of course, selling that out will tie up some cash, but less so than simply buying the stock. And selling both the out and the call reduces long call purchase by 66%

articles.title: J&J's potential 'game-changer' drug — plus, what Microsoft's mass buyouts mean
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. Stocks are broadly higher on Monday , with the AI trade rebounding from last week's sharp losses. The market is trying to rebuild confidence in the data center theme following three big news stories this morning: Meta Platforms said it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity; SpaceX announced a $40 billion debt raise to finance Nvidia GPU purchases, and Anthropic filed for an initial public offering. As investors shifted back into AI infrastructure names, they took profits in defensive sectors such as staples, healthcare, and utilities that had outperformed in last week's flight to safety and quality. Hyperscaler earnings later this week will provide key insights into spending plans among AI's biggest investors, as well as demand for AI products and services. Johnson & Johnson shares moved higher after the pharma giant announced Phase 1 results that Leerink analysts described as a potential "game-changer" for prostate cancer treatment and the company's broader oncology franchise. J & J said 12 of 16 patients with advanced prostate cancer and measurable tumors who received its investigational, once-daily oral drug JNJ-6143 achieved a complete or partial tumor response. This means 75% of those patients responded to treatment, with their tumors shrinking significantly or disappearing. JNJ-6143 works by disrupting cancer cell function and triggering cancer cell death. The results are a big deal because there is a significant unmet need in advanced prostate cancer. Leerink noted that J & J could provide new disclosures about the medication's future development plans, including earlier lines of therapy, at its Dec. 8 Enterprise Business Review event. Shares of Microsoft traded slightly higher after the company announced it is offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 eligible employees. Unlike Netflix's layoff announcement earlier this month ahead of earnings, we wouldn't view Microsoft's update as a harbinger of a slowdown in its business. Instead, the voluntary buyouts are likely a function of the company optimizing its operating structure as it invests in its AI infrastructure. It's worth mentioning that Microsoft has been spending well within its means — better than the other major hyperscalers like Amazon , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms. Microsoft is expected to generate roughly $8 billion in free cash flow in the soon-to-be-reported quarter, compared with outflows of $9.9 billion at Amazon and $2.3 billion at Alphabet, according to FactSet. Meta Platforms reported a quarterly free cash outflow of about $2 billion last week. That could help explain why Microsoft shares have outperformed Amazon, Alphabet and Meta year to date, despite their sluggish performance in the first six months of the year. We'll know more about Microsoft's revenue trajectory and spending plans when it reports earnings on Wednesday after the closing bell. Nucor , Celestica , Cadence Design Systems , and Amkor Technology report after Monday's close. Before the opening bell on Tuesday, Boeing reports. Other notable companies reporting Tuesday are Coca-Cola , United Parcel Service , Centene , HCA Healthcare , Novartis , Freeport-McMoRan , Johnson Controls , Corning , PayPal , Sherwin-Williams , Illinois Tool Works , Sofi . On the data side, we'll see durable goods orders, Conference Board Consumer Confidence, and new home sales. (See here for a full list of the stocks in Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust.) articles.title: Từ 1/11, gia đình có con nhỏ chú ý quy định mới để không bỏ lỡ quyền lợi
articles.text:
Từ 1/11, gia đình có con nhỏ chú ý quy định mới để không bỏ lỡ quyền lợi
Quy định mới cụ thể liên quan đến vấn đề gì?
Theo thông tin từ Cổng Thông tin điện tử Chính phủ, ngày 11/9/2026, Chính phủ đã ban hành Nghị định số 353/2026/NĐ-CP quy định về phổ cập giáo dục mầm non cho trẻ em từ 5 đến 6 tuổi, giáo dục bắt buộc và xóa mù chữ. Nghị định chính thức có hiệu lực từ ngày 1/11/2026, thay thế Nghị định số 20/2014/NĐ-CP về phổ cập giáo dục, xóa mù chữ.
Một trong những nội dung đáng chú ý của nghị định là quy định cụ thể về đối tượng, điều kiện thực hiện phổ cập giáo dục mầm non, đồng thời xác định các chính sách hỗ trợ dành cho trẻ trong độ tuổi này.
Theo Điều 10, đối tượng phổ cập giáo dục mầm non là trẻ em từ 5 đến 6 tuổi chưa hoàn thành chương trình giáo dục mầm non. Chương trình được thực hiện theo quy định của Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo, thông qua các cơ sở giáo dục thuộc hệ thống giáo dục quốc dân và các cơ sở giáo dục thuộc lực lượng vũ trang theo quy định pháp luật.
Đây là giai đoạn quan trọng trước khi trẻ bước vào lớp 1. Việc thực hiện phổ cập giáo dục mầm non nhằm bảo đảm trẻ được tiếp cận môi trường học tập phù hợp, hoàn thành chương trình giáo dục theo độ tuổi và có sự chuẩn bị cần thiết trước khi chuyển sang bậc tiểu học.
Đáng chú ý, bên cạnh việc quy định đối tượng phổ cập, nghị định còn đề cập đến những chính sách miễn, giảm, hỗ trợ học phí và hỗ trợ chi phí học tập mà phụ huynh cần nắm rõ.
Trẻ từ 5–6 tuổi được hưởng những quyền lợi gì?
Theo khoản 4 Điều 5 Nghị định 353/2026/NĐ-CP, trẻ em thuộc đối tượng phổ cập giáo dục mầm non từ 5–6 tuổi được hưởng chính sách miễn, giảm, hỗ trợ học phí; hỗ trợ chi phí học tập và các chính sách hỗ trợ khác theo quy định của pháp luật về giáo dục, trẻ em, người khuyết tật, chính sách dân tộc, trợ giúp xã hội và pháp luật có liên quan.
Thông tin được Báo Điện tử Chính phủ cũng nhấn mạnh, Nhà nước ưu tiên đầu tư và bảo đảm các điều kiện để thực hiện phổ cập giáo dục mầm non cho trẻ từ 5 đến 6 tuổi, tạo điều kiện để trẻ trong độ tuổi được tiếp cận giáo dục.
Đối với trẻ theo học tại các cơ sở giáo dục dân lập, tư thục thuộc hệ thống giáo dục quốc dân, Nhà nước thực hiện chính sách hỗ trợ học phí. Mức hỗ trợ cụ thể do Hội đồng nhân dân cấp tỉnh quyết định theo quy định, không vượt quá mức học phí của cơ sở giáo dục dân lập, tư thục.
Ngoài học phí, một số nhóm trẻ còn có thể được hỗ trợ chi phí học tập nếu đáp ứng điều kiện, chẳng hạn trẻ khuyết tật, trẻ mồ côi cả cha lẫn mẹ, trẻ thuộc hộ nghèo hoặc nhóm đối tượng tại địa bàn đặc biệt khó khăn theo quy định.
Một điểm khác cũng cần chú ý là sự khác biệt giữa chính sách dành cho trẻ 3–5 tuổi và trẻ 5–6 tuổi.
Theo giải đáp của Bộ Giáo dục và Đào tạo được Báo Điện tử Chính phủ đăng tải, đối tượng hưởng chính sách theo Nghị định 277/2025/NĐ-CP là trẻ 3 tuổi học chương trình mẫu giáo 3–4 tuổi và trẻ 4 tuổi học chương trình mẫu giáo 4–5 tuổi.
Trong khi đó, trẻ 5 tuổi học lớp mẫu giáo 5–6 tuổi không thuộc đối tượng áp dụng của nghị định này mà được hưởng các chính sách theo quy định tại Nghị định 105/2020/NĐ-CP và các quy định pháp luật có liên quan.
Vì vậy, phụ huynh cần xác định đúng độ tuổi, chương trình học và điều kiện của từng chính sách để bảo đảm quyền lợi cho con.
Phụ huynh cần lưu ý gì khi quy định mới có hiệu lực?
Bên cạnh những chính sách hỗ trợ, Nghị định 353/2026/NĐ-CP còn quy định trách nhiệm của gia đình, nhà trường và chính quyền địa phương trong việc thực hiện phổ cập giáo dục mầm non.
Theo Điều 8, gia đình và người giám hộ có trách nhiệm tạo điều kiện để trẻ trong độ tuổi quy định được học tập, thực hiện phổ cập giáo dục mầm non. Các cơ sở giáo dục có trách nhiệm tổ chức thực hiện công tác phổ cập theo chức năng, nhiệm vụ được giao.
Đáng chú ý, Điều 12 của nghị định cũng đặt ra những tiêu chuẩn cụ thể để công nhận địa phương đạt chuẩn phổ cập giáo dục mầm non cho trẻ từ 5–6 tuổi.
Theo đó, đối với cấp xã, tỷ lệ huy động trẻ trong độ tuổi đến lớp phải đạt ít nhất 95%, riêng xã có điều kiện kinh tế - xã hội đặc biệt khó khăn là 90%. Đồng thời, tỷ lệ trẻ hoàn thành chương trình giáo dục mầm non hằng năm phải đạt ít nhất 85%, riêng xã đặc biệt khó khăn là 80%.
Đối với cấp tỉnh, phải có ít nhất 90% số xã được công nhận đạt chuẩn phổ cập giáo dục mầm non cho trẻ từ 5–6 tuổi.
Những tỷ lệ này là tiêu chuẩn đánh giá kết quả phổ cập của địa phương, không phải điều kiện riêng để từng trẻ được miễn hay hỗ trợ học phí.
Đối với các gia đình có con đang học mẫu giáo, việc nghị định có hiệu lực từ ngày 1/11 không đồng nghĩa phụ huynh phải đăng ký nhập học lại hoặc thực hiện một thủ tục mới cho tất cả trẻ.
Tuy nhiên, phụ huynh nên chủ động cập nhật thông tin từ nhà trường, xác định đúng đối tượng và điều kiện hưởng các khoản hỗ trợ học phí, chi phí học tập, đồng thời phối hợp với cơ sở giáo dục trong việc bảo đảm trẻ đến lớp và hoàn thành chương trình theo quy định.

articles.title: Apple responds to user reports of broken iPhone Duo screens on new foldable phone
articles.text:
Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, hit store shelves on Friday to considerable lines and long wait times for pre-orders.
But some customers who were lucky enough to get the $1,999-and-up phone on its first weekend have been reporting a pretty big problem: The inner screen of the phone can break, showing horizontal bright lines emanating from the phone's hinge.
Apple on Monday said it was aware of the issue, which it said affected a "small number" of phones, and that it would replace the devices under its AppleCare warranty.
"We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units," an Apple representative told CNBC. "If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement."
Apple says on its website that an inner-screen repair will be $999 for iPhone Duos that are out-of-warranty.
Most of the reports are from anonymous customers on online forums such as Reddit and X, and there are fake images online as well. But well-respected device repair firm iFixit weighed in on Sunday, after tearing down the new device and testing its resistance to dust, and theorized the issues may have to do with Apple's hinge design.
"Many of these damage reports describe folding or unfolding the phone, hearing a crunch, and pushing past it," said iFixit technician Shahram Mokhtari in its teardown video. "Right where the damage is happening, the hinge is shaped a little differently."
"The hinge is actually dozens of parts, with ludicrous precision," iFixit CEO Kyle Wiens posted on X. "A manufacturing variance or grain of sand can kill the fragile display panel it protects."
Breaking screens have been an issue with foldable phones going back to 2019, and have been seen as one of the major roadblocks to the technology's widespread adoption. That year, Samsung released one of its first folding devices, and reviewers quickly found that its inner screen cracked during normal use.
Early reviewers praised the experience of using the iPhone Duo when unfolded, especially for multitasking or media, but said that many apps had not been updated to take full advantage of the phone's larger and wider screens.
Apple said on Monday that apps were already being updated for the new foldable device.
"The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor," an Apple representative said in a statement.

articles.title: Biểu cảm trái ngược của Mbappe và Yamal khi Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
articles.text:
Biểu cảm trái ngược của Mbappe và Yamal khi Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026
Harry Kane nhận Quả bóng vàng 2026 trong tiếng vỗ tay của các đối thủ. Mbappe chủ động chúc mừng, trong khi Yamal không giấu được sự thất vọng.
- 27-10-2026Harry Kane vượt mặt Mbappe và Yamal, giành Quả bóng Vàng 2026
- 27-10-2026Sự cố tại Quả bóng Vàng 2026 gây xôn xao: Nghi bị rò rỉ thông tin, ban tổ chức lên tiếng
- 26-10-2026Tất tần tật thông tin về Lễ trao giải Quả bóng vàng đêm nay: Yamal, Mbappé hay Harry Kane được gọi tên?
Khoảnh khắc Harry Kane được xướng tên là chủ nhân Quả bóng vàng 2026 tại London Palladium đã mang đến những hình ảnh đáng chú ý. Kylian Mbappe lập tức đứng dậy vỗ tay, chủ động tiến tới ôm chúc mừng người chiến thắng. Trong khi đó, Lamine Yamal để lộ đôi mắt đượm buồn, cho thấy sự thất vọng sau khi không thể giành danh hiệu cao quý nhất.
Phản ứng trái ngược của Mbappe và Yamal khi Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026 (Ảnh chụp màn hình).
Mbappe bước vào lễ trao giải với tư cách một trong những ứng viên hàng đầu. Tiền đạo Real Madrid vừa trải qua mùa giải cá nhân nổi bật với 58 bàn thắng trên mọi đấu trường, trong đó có 15 pha lập công tại Champions League, dẫn đầu danh sách ghi bàn ở giải đấu này. Dù vậy, khi Kane được công bố là người chiến thắng, Mbappe đón nhận kết quả với thái độ bình thản và dành sự tôn trọng cho đồng nghiệp.
Chiến thắng của Kane đến sau một mùa giải đặc biệt hiệu quả. Tiền đạo Bayern Munich ghi 73 bàn sau 65 trận, cùng 8 kiến tạo cho CLB và ĐT Anh. Trong màu áo Bayern, Kane ghi 61 bàn sau 51 trận, trong đó có 36 bàn tại Bundesliga, 10 bàn ở DFB-Pokal và 14 bàn tại Champions League.
Kane cùng Bayern giành Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal và Siêu cúp Đức. Anh cũng lần thứ ba liên tiếp trở thành Vua phá lưới Bundesliga và giành Chiếc giày vàng châu Âu. Đặc biệt, Kane ghi hat-trick trong trận chung kết DFB-Pokal, góp phần giúp Bayern đăng quang.
Ở cấp độ ĐT Anh, Kane ghi 6 bàn tại World Cup 2026, góp phần đưa đội tuyển cán đích ở vị trí thứ ba. Anh cũng nâng tổng số bàn thắng tại World Cup lên 14, trở thành cầu thủ ghi nhiều bàn nhất cho ĐT Anh ở sân chơi này.
Trong khi đó, Yamal có một mùa giải cũng rất đáng chú ý. Cầu thủ Barcelona ra sân 57 trận, ghi 25 bàn và có 20 kiến tạo. Anh cùng Barcelona giành La Liga và Siêu cúp Tây Ban Nha, đồng thời cùng ĐT Tây Ban Nha đăng quang World Cup 2026.
Yamal tiếp tục được vinh danh là Cầu thủ trẻ nam xuất sắc nhất năm, qua đó có lần thứ ba liên tiếp giành giải thưởng này. Đây là cột mốc đặc biệt đối với cầu thủ mới 19 tuổi, sau những lần được vinh danh vào các năm 2024 và 2025.
Tuy nhiên, khi Kane được xướng tên ở hạng mục Quả bóng vàng, những hình ảnh ghi lại Yamal với đôi mắt rơm rớm nhanh chóng thu hút sự chú ý. Không có phát biểu nào cho thấy Yamal phản ứng tiêu cực với kết quả, nhưng khoảnh khắc ấy cho thấy cảm xúc của một cầu thủ đã trải qua một mùa giải nổi bật nhưng phải đứng sau Kane ở cuộc đua cuối cùng.
Kane, Mbappe và Yamal tạo nên ba sắc thái khác nhau tại lễ trao giải: người chiến thắng xúc động, Mbappe chủ động chúc mừng đối thủ, còn Yamal không giấu được sự thất vọng. Dẫu vậy, kết quả đã được xác lập: Harry Kane giành Quả bóng vàng 2026, còn Lamine Yamal lần thứ ba liên tiếp được vinh danh là Cầu thủ trẻ nam xuất sắc nhất năm.

articles.title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, alleging retailer overcharged shoppers
articles.text:
The Federal Trade Commission said Monday that it filed a lawsuit along with 20 states accusing Dollar General of charging customers more than the prices it displays on shelves, price tags and in advertisements.
Shares of Dollar General dropped about 4% after the FTC announced the lawsuit.
The complaint alleges that thousands of Dollar General stores have "taken advantage of vulnerable shoppers by extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges with insufficient safeguards to prevent the practice."
It also argues that Dollar General has received "tens of thousands" of complaints from consumers about charging higher than advertised prices, but that it has not implemented policies to address the problem.
The states joining the FTC in the lawsuit are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin.
"Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last," said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection.
Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The suit comes as shoppers look for discounts while they face elevated food and gas prices. Officials across the political spectrum also aim to show their efforts to protect consumers from high costs ahead of the midterm election next week.

articles.title: Nam nghệ sĩ một ngày kiếm 65 tỷ đồng
articles.text:
Nam nghệ sĩ một ngày kiếm 65 tỷ đồng
Giả Nãi Lượng từng là nam thần màn ảnh, được các bà nội trợ yêu thích. Hiện tại, anh đổi nghề vẫn kiếm được doanh thu khủng.
- 27-10-2026Nam nghệ sĩ đình đám SN 1981 khoe dinh thự trắng 5 tầng ở Hà Nội, xây để sống với mỹ nhân phim giờ vàng
- 27-10-2026Cuộc sống tại nhà của 2 người đàn ông Việt có nghìn tỷ
Trang Tài chính Sina đưa tin nam diễn viên Giả Nãi Lượng nghỉ đóng phim suốt 7 năm, đã chuyển sang lĩnh vực thương mại điện tử. Mới đây, phiên livestream của anh kéo dài suốt 12 tiếng, đạt doanh thu 570 triệu NDT (hơn 85,3 triệu USD), đạt mức cao nhất trong suốt 3 năm qua so với chính thành tích của anh.
Lượng người xem trực tiếp tại thời điểm cao nhất đạt 7 triệu lượt, giúp anh tiếp tục giữ vị trí số một trên bảng xếp hạng livestream bán hàng của Douyin.
Theo Sina , sau khi đạt mức doanh thu bùng nổ, Giả Nãi Lượng có thể đạt mức lương thưởng lên tới 57 triệu NDT, khoảng 10% tổng doanh thu. Trừ đi các chi phí khác, anh có thể nhận về khoảng 17 triệu NDT (hơn 2,5 triệu USD) sau một ngày làm việc.
So với mức cát-xê hiện tại, chỉ một ngày Giả Nãi Lượng kiếm bằng các ngôi sao hạng A đóng phim suốt 3-4 tháng, thậm chí vượt xa thù lao của một bộ phim truyền hình trong thời kỳ anh còn tập trung vào diễn xuất.
Nhiều khán giả cho rằng Giả Nãi Lượng xứng đáng với số tiền này. "Tôi chỉ xem thôi mà còn thấy mệt mỏi, anh ấy liên tục giới thiệu hết sản phẩm này tới sản phẩm khác với sự nhiệt tình mãi không hết, kiểm soát tốt nhịp độ buổi phát sóng, hiếm khi giao việc cho trợ lý livestream thay mình. Tôi thực sự phục rồi", khán giả bày tỏ.
Buổi livestream thuộc chương trình siêu mua sắm dịp 11/11, do một công ty công nghệ ở Hàng Châu vận hành, đại diện pháp nhân của công ty này là Giả San, chị của Giả Nãi Lượng. Hiện tại, anh ít đóng phim, tập trung vào các hoạt động thương mại.
Nam diễn viên từng chia sẻ ở tuổi 42, anh gặp khó khăn trong việc phát triển sự nghiệp diễn xuất. "Tôi đang ở độ tuổi không đủ già để vào vai người cha, nhưng quá tuổi để đóng phim thần tượng. Rất lâu rồi các đạo diễn không gửi kịch bản đến cho tôi nữa", anh nói.
Anh cũng thừa nhận mình có năng khiếu diễn xuất hạn chế và không còn lựa chọn nào khác ngoài việc chuyển sang bán hàng trực tuyến. Trước đó, Giả Nãi Lượng nắm trong tay 11 công ty nhưng hiện tại chỉ còn lại 5 công ty tập trung vào kinh doanh.
Giả Nãi Lượng là một trong những ngôi sao thành công khi chuyển sang lĩnh vực thương mại điện tử. Nhưng anh cũng không ít lần vướng scandal vì rắc rối liên quan tới chất lượng sản phẩm, giá tiền chênh lệch khi bán hàng.
Các ngôi sao như Đổng Khiết, Trương Bá Chi, Lưu Đào cũng là những người thành công khi nỗ lực livestream bán hàng. Tuy nhiên, họ cũng vướng phải tranh cãi địa vị bị hạ thấp, bị coi là "ngôi sao hết thời". Chỉ khi sự nghiệp diễn xuất đi xuống, các diễn viên mới chuyển sang lĩnh vực thương mại điện tử.
Khán giả cho rằng các diễn viên có danh tiếng và địa vị cao, khi bán hàng cần phải chiều chuộng, nài nỉ người mua, vì không thể kiếm nhiều tiền nhờ diễn xuất họ mới đi livestream. Danh tiếng của họ cũng bị gắn liền với sản phẩm, dễ rơi vào tình trạng nhận chỉ trích nếu sản phẩm gửi cho khách hàng có vấn đề.
Giả Nãi Lượng từng là "nam thần của các bà nội trợ" khi đóng những bộ phim thần tượng hấp dẫn như Vẫn cứ thích em, Dương môn hổ tướng, Thời gian đẹp nhất, Đại Đường ca phi, Bác sĩ sản khoa nam ...
Anh từng kết hôn với nữ diễn viên Lý Tiểu Lộ, họ từng được coi là cặp sao đáng ngưỡng mộ của màn ảnh Hoa ngữ.
Cuối năm 2017, Lý Tiểu Lộ bị khui chuyện ngoại tình với nam rapper trẻ tuổi PGone. Giả Nãi Lượng luôn coi PGone như em trai nuôi, anh cũng yêu thương, chiều chuộng vợ. Khi vụ ngoại tình vỡ lở, lúc đầu Giả Nãi Lượng còn lên tiếng bảo vệ Lý Tiểu Lộ.
Cuối cùng, cả hai ly hôn và vẫn chung tay nuôi dạy con gái Điềm Hinh. Giả Nãi Lượng thường xuyên tham gia các hoạt động từ thiện cùng mẹ con Lý Tiểu Lộ. Ngày 24/10, anh tham gia tiệc sinh nhật con gái cùng vợ cũ.
Tiền phong
