articles.title: Alaska Senate: Peltola seeks quick dismissal of DOJ election lawsuit before midterm
articles.text:
The campaign of Alaska Senate Democratic nominee Mary Peltola asked a federal judge to fast-track a Trump administration lawsuit that could block certification of that election. Peltola's campaign wants the judge to dismiss the suit before Election Day.
A lawyer for Peltola's campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee in a court filing late Sunday said they are "seriously concerned" President Donald Trump and Attorney General Todd Blanche will use the lawsuit to "lay the groundwork for unlawful efforts to challenge a potential Peltola victory" if the complaint remains pending as of Nov. 3, the day of the election.
The advocacy groups Common Cause and the League of Women Voters, which previously sought to intervene in the DOJ's lawsuit, on Monday joined Peltola's motion seeking a quick briefing and dismissal by Alaska District Court Judge Sharon Gleason.
The Department of Justice filed the suit Thursday. Trump later that day said he ordered it.
The DOJ's suit asks a judge to bar Alaska from certifying the Senate race results if incumbent Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses by a margin that could be attributable to voters mistakenly casting their ballots for another candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan.
The DOJ, in that case, would want an investigation to determine whether enough voters were confused by the men's names to swing the vote to another candidate, presumably the former Rep. Peltola. The DOJ claims that Daniel J. Sullivan's "sole purpose" of running "is to benefit the Peltola campaign by reducing the number of votes for Senator Sullivan."
The winner of the race could determine which party holds a majority in the Senate starting in January.
Peltola's campaign and the DSCC, in their court filing, asked that a judge order the DOJ to respond to their motion to intervene in the case, and their motion to dismiss the lawsuit by 5 p.m. Alaska Time on Tuesday, and to order a reply to that response by Wednesday.
"And dismiss the case this week," the motion says.
"DOJ filed this lawsuit in the midst of the ongoing general election, less than two weeks before election day, raising issues governed exclusively by state law that were definitively resolved by the Alaska Supreme Court months ago," the filing says.
"DOJ seeks an unprecedented order precluding certification of the U.S. Senate election if the candidate the President favors loses narrowly," the filing said.
"As the proposed Motion to Dismiss reflects, DOJ's claims are utterly without legal basis," the filing said.
"The Court should not allow this lawsuit to hang like the Sword of Damocles over the ongoing election, lending false legitimacy to the President's and the Attorney General's ongoing efforts to spread false narratives about Alaska's elections as voting continues and as results begin to be tabulated next week."
The DOJ declined to comment on the new motion, but pointed to an X post by Blanche on Sunday.
"The Department of Justice does not seek to stop any ballot from being cast or to stop the certification of Alaska's election," Blanche had said. "This litigation seeks to ensure that after Alaskans cast their ballots, they are preserved in a manner so that only Alaska's governing officials have the information necessary to make a determination as to whether Alaskan voters were confused or mislead."
"The lawsuit was written by Justice Department attorneys and the Department did not coordinate with any campaign or candidate, but rather relied solely on federal law," Blanche said.
The department has not said how any investigation before certification of the election could determine whether a voter was confused about which Sullivan they were voting for. The ballot for the election notes that Sen. Sullivan — whose name is listed as Dan S. Sullivan — is an incumbent and a Republican. There are no words next to the name of the other candidate, whose name is spelled out Daniel J. Sullivan.
Peltola on Friday night told MS NOW's Nicolle Wallace that the DOJ's suit "is exactly the kind of corruption that Alaskans are sick and tired of."
"This is clearly a very desperate attempt to cling to power, using his allies in Washington, D.C., to rig the system even further," Peltola said.
Peltola's campaign on Sunday said that on Saturday night she and her family "sustained minor injuries" that required medical attention after a vehicle transporting them en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives Annual Banquet was struck by another driver.
As a result, Peltola posted events in Fairbanks and Bethel on Sunday and Monday. The campaign said that those events would be rescheduled.

articles.title: Hưng Yên tiếp tục tinh gọn bộ máy, giảm nhiều đầu mối
articles.text:
Hưng Yên tiếp tục tinh gọn bộ máy, giảm nhiều đầu mối
Sau khi sắp xếp đơn vị hành chính và triển khai mô hình chính quyền địa phương 2 cấp, tỉnh Hưng Yên tiếp tục rà soát, kiện toàn tổ chức bộ máy theo hướng tinh gọn, phân định rõ chức năng, nhiệm vụ.
- 26-10-2026Đất trúng đấu giá Hưng Yên từng 'sốt' nhất miền Bắc hơn 158 triệu đồng/m2 giờ ra sao?
- 26-10-2026Liên tục nhận cuộc gọi lạ, người đàn ông lập tức đi rút 270 triệu đồng tại Quỹ tín dụng: Công an khẩn trương xác minh
- 26-10-2026Diện mạo nút giao Vành đai 4 ở cửa ngõ Tây Nam Hà Nội
Giảm đầu mối, phân định rõ chức năng, nhiệm vụ
Sau khi tỉnh Hưng Yên mới được thành lập và mô hình chính quyền địa phương 2 cấp đi vào vận hành, công tác sắp xếp, tinh gọn tổ chức bộ máy tiếp tục được triển khai trên cơ sở yêu cầu thực tiễn. Quá trình hợp nhất tỉnh và tổ chức lại các cơ quan cấp tỉnh đã giúp giảm đáng kể số lượng đầu mối.
Cụ thể, khối cơ quan Đảng giảm 5 cơ quan và 16 phòng trực thuộc. Khối cơ quan Nhà nước giảm 13 sở, ban, ngành; 90 tổ chức gồm các phòng, ban, chi cục và 41 đơn vị sự nghiệp công lập trực thuộc các sở, ngành. Việc sắp xếp cũng đặt ra yêu cầu đổi mới phương thức vận hành, chuyển từ quản lý đơn ngành sang quản lý đa ngành, đa lĩnh vực, đồng thời khắc phục tình trạng chồng chéo chức năng, nhiệm vụ giữa các cơ quan.
Ngày 10/4/2026, UBND tỉnh ban hành Quyết định số 16/2026 về quản lý tổ chức bộ máy, vị trí việc làm, biên chế, tuyển dụng và sử dụng cán bộ, công chức, người lao động trong các cơ quan hành chính tỉnh. Đây là cơ sở để tăng cường quản lý thống nhất, gắn việc kiện toàn tổ chức với yêu cầu bố trí nhân lực và thực hiện nhiệm vụ.
Cuối tháng 9/2026, tỉnh tiếp tục tổ chức lại một số đơn vị sự nghiệp trực thuộc UBND tỉnh. Trong đó, ba ban quản lý dự án chuyên ngành gồm Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng công trình giao thông, Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng công trình dân dụng và Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng công trình nông nghiệp được thành lập trên cơ sở tổ chức lại Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 1 và Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng số 2.
Tỉnh cũng thành lập Trung tâm Phát triển quỹ đất tỉnh Hưng Yên trên cơ sở hợp nhất Trung tâm Phát triển quỹ đất số 1 và Trung tâm Phát triển quỹ đất số 2; thành lập Trung tâm Xúc tiến đầu tư, thương mại và du lịch trên cơ sở hợp nhất ba đơn vị thuộc các sở: Tài chính, Công Thương và Văn hóa, Thể thao và Du lịch.
Việc tổ chức lại các đơn vị theo lĩnh vực chuyên môn hướng tới tập trung đầu mối, phân định rõ trách nhiệm và nâng cao hiệu quả phối hợp trong quá trình thực hiện nhiệm vụ.
Đại diện Ban Quản lý dự án đầu tư xây dựng công trình giao thông cho biết, sau khi tổ chức, sắp xếp lại, chức năng và nhiệm vụ của đơn vị được phân định cụ thể hơn, hạn chế tình trạng chồng chéo. Nhờ đó, công tác triển khai nhiệm vụ thuận lợi, hiệu quả hơn, góp phần đẩy nhanh tiến độ và nâng cao chất lượng các công trình, dự án được giao quản lý.
Giảm 703 cơ sở giáo dục công lập
Giáo dục công lập là một trong những lĩnh vực có quy mô sắp xếp lớn tại Hưng Yên trong năm 2026. Đầu tháng 8/2026, các địa phương trong tỉnh triển khai sắp xếp, tổ chức lại các cơ sở giáo dục công lập. Kết quả, toàn tỉnh giảm 703 cơ sở, tương đương 60,4% tổng số cơ sở giáo dục công lập trước sắp xếp.
Việc tổ chức lại theo hướng mỗi trường phụ trách một cấp học nhằm tinh gọn đầu mối quản lý, tạo thuận lợi cho công tác điều hành và nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động giáo dục. Tuy nhiên, việc sáp nhập vẫn phải gắn với yêu cầu bảo đảm điều kiện học tập, hạn chế ảnh hưởng đến việc đi lại và sinh hoạt của học sinh.
Tại xã Ngự Thiên, trong tháng 8/2026, địa phương sắp xếp 10 trường công lập, gồm 4 trường mầm non, 2 trường tiểu học, 2 trường THCS và 2 trường liên cấp tiểu học – THCS, thành 3 trường độc lập theo từng cấp học, giảm 70% số trường.
Sau sắp xếp, các điểm trường vẫn được duy trì nhằm bảo đảm điều kiện học tập cho học sinh trên địa bàn, đồng thời tập trung nguồn lực và nâng cao hiệu quả quản trị nhà trường. Việc tổ chức lại theo mô hình trường đơn cấp giúp công tác quản lý, chăm sóc và giáo dục học sinh thuận lợi hơn so với trước đây, qua đó tạo điều kiện nâng cao chất lượng dạy và học. Sau sắp xếp, hoạt động giáo dục tại trường cơ bản ổn định.
Thực tế cho thấy, tinh gọn tổ chức bộ máy không chỉ là giảm số lượng cơ quan, đơn vị mà còn đòi hỏi nâng cao chất lượng đội ngũ, cải cách thủ tục hành chính và đổi mới phương thức quản lý. Các đơn vị sau sắp xếp cần vận hành thông suốt, phân định rõ trách nhiệm và sử dụng hiệu quả nguồn lực được giao.
Ông Đào Hồng Vận, Giám đốc Sở Nội vụ Hưng Yên, cho biết tỉnh sẽ tiếp tục rà soát chức năng, nhiệm vụ các cơ quan, đơn vị; bố trí cán bộ phù hợp vị trí việc làm, khắc phục chồng chéo, nâng cao hiệu quả hoạt động. Việc tinh gọn bộ máy phải gắn với cải cách hành chính, siết chặt kỷ luật công vụ và nâng cao chất lượng phục vụ người dân, doanh nghiệp.
Tiền phong

articles.title: Mortgage rates above 7% are the 'new normal'—here's why
articles.text:
Everyone seems to agree that mortgage rates above 7% are the new "normal."
The phrase keeps popping up lately in public comments from housing economists, including Lawrence Yun, chief economist for the National Association of Realtors, and Robert Dietz, chief economist for the National Association of Home Builders.
It's a sentiment increasingly reflected in forecasts, too, with major housing groups predicting mortgage rates will remain above 7% well into 2027. Fannie Mae forecasts mortgage rates could average 7.5% in 2027, while the Mortgage Bankers Association expects them to remain above 7%.
That means the 3% or 4% mortgage rates borrowers were used to in the years before 2022 are unlikely to return anytime soon.
"We could definitely see some movement up and down depending on data, but we're just not in the same economic environment we were in during the 2010s or the pandemic," says Jenna Stauffer, a broker and market analyst with Sotheby's International Realty.
Why mortgage rates could stay higher for longer
Mortgage rates tend to move with the 10-year Treasury yield, which serves as a benchmark because mortgages are typically paid off or refinanced well before their 30-year term. And there are reasons to think those longer-term borrowing costs could remain elevated.
One is persistently high inflation. When inflation remains elevated, investors generally demand higher yields on long-term bonds to compensate for the declining purchasing power of the money they'll eventually be repaid. Inflation, as measured by the Fed's preferred PCE price index, hasn't been below the central bank's 2% target since February 2021.
But inflation isn't the only factor. The federal government is borrowing heavily, while the artificial intelligence boom is fueling enormous private investment in data centers, power generation and other infrastructure, says Selma Hepp, chief economist at real estate data firm Cotality. Together, that increased demand for capital can put upward pressure on longer-term borrowing costs, she says.
Compared to the 2010s, "we've moved from a world with more capital than investment opportunities to one with tremendous competition for capital," Hepp says. Low inflation, abundant savings and relatively weak demand for capital helped keep mortgage rates low during that period, she says.
Demand for mortgage bonds has weakened, too, putting upward pressure on mortgage rates. Banks have become more reluctant to hold mortgage-backed securities since the 2022-23 rate spike produced steep losses on bond portfolios, says Tom Graff, chief investment officer at wealth management firm Facet. That's because bond prices generally fall when interest rates rise. The failures of Silicon Valley Bank and First Republic also prompted greater regulatory scrutiny of banks' bond holdings, he says.
During the pandemic, the Fed pushed rates in the opposite direction. The Federal Reserve bought large quantities of Treasury bonds and mortgage-backed securities to push longer-term borrowing costs lower, helping drive mortgage rates to historic lows. The Fed has since stepped away from actively buying mortgage-backed securities, says Steve Kaminski, head of residential lending at TD Bank.
With those low-rate conditions no longer in place, "mortgage rates will likely remain elevated for at least the next year," Kaminski says.
What would it take for mortgage rates to fall?
Getting mortgage rates back to around 6% would likely require lower inflation, slower economic growth or less pressure from government borrowing to help bring down the 10-year Treasury yield, Hepp says.
Kaminski similarly says getting below 7% would require lower inflation and lower Treasury yields. A weakening economy could also push rates lower as investors seek the relative safety of Treasury bonds, lowering their yields, he says.
Whether that happens is uncertain, which is why Hepp says she doesn't like calling 7% the "new normal," since there's nothing permanent about that particular number. But the low inflation, abundant capital and accommodative Fed policies that helped produce 3% and 4% mortgages are no longer in place, she says.
For would-be homebuyers, that means waiting for significantly lower mortgage rates could be a gamble.
"I don't think we should expect to return to the financial conditions that routinely produced 3% and 4% mortgages," Hepp says.

articles.title: Apple stock has become an anti-AI trade. Here’s why
articles.text: As goes Apple , so goes the tech sector. For years, that was the case, but not anymore. Traders at Goldman Sachs pointed out that the stock's correlation to the Nasdaq-100 index turned negative this year for the first time ever. Indeed, the correlation coefficient between the two sits around -0.1 on a trailing three-month basis. At one point in 2020, the Apple/Nasdaq-100 correlation stood at 0.97. In 2025, it got as high as 0.91. The sharp decoupling comes as the company has moved to adopt artificial intelligence less aggressively than other major tech companies. For example, while Alphabet and Meta Platforms have launched chatbots and personal AI agents, Apple only released iOS 27 — which includes a rebuilt Siri AI — on Sept. 14. Investors in turn have piled into other tech names. Apple has returned 111% to shareholders, while Meta and Alphabet have seen returns of 125% and 164%, respectively. However, Apple's more cautious AI approach may be helping the company of late. Shares are up 4.4% in October, while the Nasdaq-100 has dropped nearly 5% in that time amid concerns that some companies may be borrowing too much money to fund their AI build-out. On top of that, excitement around the company's iPhone Duo launch was palpable. Launch-day pickup inventory of the foldable phone sold out quickly , and some deliveries appear to be delayed as far as late January. More broadly, the decoupling could be beneficial for the Nasdaq-100, with Apple potentially serving as a safety trade amid growing AI volatility.

articles.title: Một ngân hàng giảm gần 80% lợi nhuận quý III
articles.text:
Một ngân hàng giảm gần 80% lợi nhuận quý III
Tính đến ngày 26/10, lợi nhuận trước thuế quý III của Saigonbank, KienlongBank, BAOVIET Bank và PGBank đều giảm so với cùng kỳ năm trước, riêng Saigonbank giảm gần 80%.
Lý do lợi nhuận Saigonbank giảm mạnh
Theo báo cáo tài chính quý III, Saigonbank ghi nhận lợi nhuận trước thuế đạt 17,8 tỷ đồng, giảm gần 80% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Lũy kế 9 tháng đầu năm, lợi nhuận trước thuế của ngân hàng đạt gần 66 tỷ đồng, giảm gần 75%.
Nguyên nhân khiến lợi nhuận Saigonbank sụt giảm mạnh trong quý III chủ yếu đến từ sự suy giảm của một số mảng kinh doanh, trong đó có hoạt động dịch vụ và kinh doanh ngoại hối. Bên cạnh đó, chi phí hoạt động trong kỳ tăng mạnh, khiến lợi nhuận thuần từ hoạt động kinh doanh giảm khoảng 1/3 so với cùng kỳ.
Về quy mô hoạt động, tại ngày 30/6/2026, tổng tài sản của Saigonbank đạt 35.373 tỷ đồng, gần như đi ngang so với đầu năm. Dư nợ cho vay khách hàng đạt 21.754 tỷ đồng, giảm nhẹ so với mức 21.972 tỷ đồng cuối năm 2025. Tiền gửi khách hàng cũng giảm từ 26.326 tỷ đồng xuống 25.171 tỷ đồng.
Tại BAOVIET Bank, lợi nhuận trước thuế quý III đạt 17 tỷ đồng, giảm 41% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Lũy kế 9 tháng, lợi nhuận trước thuế của ngân hàng đạt 50 tỷ đồng, giảm 14,2%.
Theo báo cáo tài chính, thu nhập lãi thuần của BAOVIET Bank tăng hơn 4%, trong khi thu nhập ngoài lãi tăng 11,3%. Một số hoạt động ghi nhận mức tăng trưởng tích cực gồm chứng khoán đầu tư, chứng khoán kinh doanh và kinh doanh ngoại hối. Nhờ đó, lợi nhuận thuần trước chi phí dự phòng rủi ro tăng gần 10,14%.
Tính đến hết tháng 9, tổng tài sản của BAOVIET Bank đạt gần 112.499 tỷ đồng, tăng nhẹ so với đầu năm. Tổng thu nhập hoạt động trong 9 tháng tăng 6,56% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tuy nhiên, những kết quả tích cực ở một số mảng kinh doanh chưa đủ bù đắp các yếu tố khiến lợi nhuận trước thuế suy giảm.
Tăng trưởng lợi nhuận 9 tháng
KienlongBank cũng ghi nhận lợi nhuận trước thuế quý III giảm 12,7% so với cùng kỳ, xuống còn 537 tỷ đồng. Lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt 429 tỷ đồng, giảm gần 13%.
Dù lợi nhuận quý III đi xuống, kết quả kinh doanh lũy kế của KienlongBank vẫn duy trì đà tăng trưởng. Trong 9 tháng năm nay, ngân hàng đạt lợi nhuận trước thuế 1.713 tỷ đồng, tăng 11,5% so với cùng kỳ năm trước và hoàn thành khoảng 66% kế hoạch năm. Lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt 1.368 tỷ đồng, tăng 11,4%.
Tính đến ngày 30/9, tổng tài sản của KienlongBank đạt 115.968 tỷ đồng, tăng 12,3% so với đầu năm. Tiền gửi khách hàng tăng 13,6%, lên 81.827 tỷ đồng, trong khi dư nợ cho vay khách hàng tăng 9,6%, đạt 78.465 tỷ đồng.
Trong khi đó, PGBank ghi nhận lợi nhuận trước thuế quý III đạt hơn 190 tỷ đồng, giảm hơn 10% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tính chung 9 tháng đầu năm, lợi nhuận trước thuế sau dự phòng đạt 630 tỷ đồng, tăng 27% so với cùng kỳ năm 2025.
Đến ngày 30/9, tổng tài sản của PGBank đạt 92.637 tỷ đồng, tăng 4,3% so với cuối năm 2025. Dư nợ cho vay khách hàng tăng 7,1%, tiền gửi khách hàng tăng 5,8% so với cuối năm trước. Đáng chú ý, tiền gửi không kỳ hạn (CASA) tăng 32%.

articles.title: Mỹ sẵn sàng tấn công Iran trong vòng 96 giờ nếu có lệnh từ Tổng thống Trump
articles.text:
Mỹ sẵn sàng tấn công Iran trong vòng 96 giờ nếu có lệnh từ Tổng thống Trump
Các lực lượng Mỹ tại Trung Đông đã sẵn sàng triển khai những chiến dịch quân sự mới - có khả năng ở quy mô lớn - nhắm vào Iran “trong vòng 96 giờ kể từ khi nhận được mệnh lệnh từ Tổng thống Donald Trump”.
- 26-10-2026Lầu Năm Góc công bố tài liệu mới về UFO: Phát hiện tam giác đen bí ẩn không thể hiểu là gì bay với tốc độ 2.900 km/h
- 26-10-2026Thái độ của Mỹ với Ukraine và Iran có thể đảo chiều nếu đảng của Tổng thống Trump thua bầu cử giữa kỳ
- 25-10-2026Vì sao thế giới rất mong cuộc gặp giữa 3 nhà lãnh đạo Nga-Mỹ-Trung Quốc?
Các nguồn tin cho biết, hiện Mỹ đã tập hợp đủ lực lượng trong khu vực để thực hiện các cuộc tấn công tiềm tàng. Theo nguồn tin này, quy mô của các chiến dịch quân sự mới từ phía Mỹ có thể vượt xa những nỗ lực trước đó - vốn chỉ tập trung vào việc tấn công các trạm radar, bệ phóng và những tài sản khác của Iran mà nước này có thể nhanh chóng khôi phục.
“Đây sẽ là một nỗ lực quy mô lớn”, một quan chức chia sẻ với CNN. Quan điểm này cũng được các quan chức Mỹ thạo tin đồng tình. Một số người cho rằng vấn đề không phải là liệu ông Trump có ra lệnh hành động hay không, mà là khi nào ông ấy sẽ làm điều đó. Họ tin rằng mệnh lệnh có thể được đưa ra bất cứ lúc nào trước cuối năm nay, dù khả năng cao nhất là sau cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ tại Mỹ.
Thách thức và mối đe dọa tiềm tàng
Sau nhiều tháng giao tranh, các lực lượng Iran hiện đã quen thuộc hơn với các chiến thuật của Mỹ. Do đó, quân đội Mỹ sẽ gặp khó khăn hơn trong việc loại bỏ tất cả các mục tiêu dự kiến. Tuy nhiên, lãnh đạo tại Bộ Tư lệnh Trung tâm Mỹ và Lầu Năm Góc đang xây dựng một danh sách mục tiêu toàn diện, bao gồm cơ sở hạ tầng năng lượng, các địa điểm quân sự và các cơ sở hạt nhân của Iran.
Các quan chức cho biết, ông Trump vẫn chưa quyết định sẽ thực hiện hành động gì sau cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ, nhưng dường như ông đang nghiêng về phương án triển khai một chiến dịch quy mô lớn. Dù vậy, các quan chức cũng lưu ý rằng trong quá khứ, ông Trump từng có lúc tỏ ý ủng hộ một hành động nào đó, nhưng rồi lại rút lui vào phút chót.
Theo hai nguồn tin khác, các đánh giá tình báo gần đây của Mỹ cho thấy Iran và lực lượng Houthi đang đề phòng khả năng xảy ra các cuộc tấn công mới từ phía Mỹ, và có thể là cả Israel.
Các nguồn tin này cho biết, nếu Mỹ và Israel tiến hành các chiến dịch quân sự mới nhắm vào Iran, Tehran cùng lực lượng Houthi nhiều khả năng sẽ lập tức đáp trả bằng cách nhắm vào nhân sự và cơ sở của Mỹ trong khu vực, thậm chí có thể là ở những nơi khác ngoài khu vực này.
Giới chức tình báo Mỹ tin rằng, Iran và lực lượng Houthi khó có khả năng thực hiện các cuộc tấn công leo thang phủ đầu nhắm vào nhân sự Mỹ hoặc Israel ở thời điểm hiện tại. Tuy nhiên, họ sẽ không ngần ngại đáp trả nếu Iran bị tấn công trước bởi các lực lượng Mỹ hoặc Israel.
Mối đe dọa trong khu vực từ Iran và lực lượng Houthi là một trong những lý do khiến Mỹ dự kiến sẽ tiếp tục âm thầm rút nhân viên khỏi các đại sứ quán tại Trung Đông trong những ngày tới.
Mặc dù Đại sứ quán Mỹ tại Riyadh (Ả-rập Xê-út) hiện là cơ sở ngoại giao duy nhất của Mỹ trong khu vực nhận lệnh sơ tán nhân viên, nhưng các cơ sở khác cũng có thể sớm nhận được chỉ thị tương tự. Những nơi không nhận lệnh sơ tán cũng sẽ phải cắt giảm quy mô nhân sự theo một hạn mức nhất định.
Ngoài ra, theo một quan chức Mỹ, các quân nhân Mỹ vốn dự kiến sẽ được triển khai đến Trung Đông trong đợt luân chuyển quân tiếp theo đã được thông báo hủy kế hoạch điều động. Điều này cho thấy nguy cơ leo thang căng thẳng trong khu vực đang cận kề.
Đô đốc Brad Cooper - Tư lệnh Bộ Chỉ huy Trung tâm Mỹ (CENTCOM) - đã đến thăm eo biển Hormuz hôm 25/10, trong bối cảnh quân đội Mỹ duy trì việc phong tỏa các cảng của Iran và hỗ trợ hoạt động vận tải biển đi qua tuyến đường thủy trọng yếu này.
Theo thông tin từ CENTCOM, Đô đốc Cooper đã “quan sát môi trường tác chiến” khi bay qua eo biển trên một chiếc trực thăng. Ông cũng gặp gỡ các quân nhân làm nhiệm vụ rà phá thủy lôi do Iran thả tại tuyến đường thủy này.
Đô đốc Cooper khẳng định: “Chúng tôi tiếp tục sát cánh cùng các đối tác vùng Vịnh và ngành vận tải biển. Chuyến thăm này nhấn mạnh cam kết mạnh mẽ của chúng tôi trong việc duy trì quyền tự do hàng hải qua eo biển Hormuz”.
Mặc dù số lượng tàu chở dầu đi qua eo biển này đã tăng lên, giá dầu vẫn ở mức cao, một phần do lo ngại về các cuộc tấn công tiềm tàng từ phía Iran. Một quan chức Mỹ thừa nhận rằng tình trạng hiện tại quanh eo biển Hormuz là “không thể duy trì” về lâu dài. Nếu không có một bước đột phá ngoại giao nào vào phút chót, đây có thể là lý do khiến ông Trump cân nhắc hành động quân sự, bất chấp những nghi vấn về việc liệu Nhà Trắng có một chiến lược toàn diện hơn để chấm dứt xung đột hay không.
Israel thúc đẩy các cuộc tấn công mới
Theo hai quan chức Mỹ và một nguồn tin an ninh Israel, Thủ tướng Israel Benjamin Netanyahu đã thúc đẩy việc thực hiện các cuộc tấn công mới nhắm vào Iran, nhưng các quan chức Mỹ đã yêu cầu ông trì hoãn cho đến khi chính quyền Mỹ sẵn sàng tiến hành các chiến dịch chung, nhiều khả năng là sau cuộc bầu cử giữa nhiệm kỳ tại Mỹ.
Một nguồn tin an ninh Israel chia sẻ với CNN: “Ông Netanyahu thực sự mong muốn và đã cố gắng thuyết phục ông Trump thực hiện một cuộc tấn công chung vào Iran trước thềm bầu cử, nhưng ông Trump không chấp thuận”.
Văn phòng Thủ tướng Israel khẳng định đây là “tin giả”.
Theo nguồn tin Israel, lý do ông Trump từ chối là vì Tổng tham mưu trưởng Lực lượng Phòng vệ Israel (IDF) - Eyal Zamir đã nói với Chủ tịch Hội đồng Tham mưu trưởng Liên quân Mỹ - Dan Caine rằng hành động này sẽ gây tổn hại đến cuộc bầu cử tại Israel và dẫn đến việc phải hoãn bầu cử.
Kênh tin tức Channel 12 của Israel đưa tin hôm 25/10, rằng đã xảy ra một cuộc đối đầu “chưa từng có” giữa ông Zamir và ông Netanyahu, chưa đầy 48 giờ trước cuộc bỏ phiếu vào ngày 27/10. Theo bản tin, ông Zamir đã nhận được chỉ thị từ giới lãnh đạo chính trị liên quan đến Iran, nhưng ông yêu cầu phải thảo luận kỹ lưỡng và có các cơ sở pháp lý trước khi thực hiện, vì lo ngại rằng hành động này có thể dẫn đến tính toán sai lầm, từ đó châm ngòi cho một cuộc xung đột tức thời. Tuy nhiên, tin đồn này đã bị Bộ trưởng Quốc phòng Israel bác bỏ.
Israel dường như đã đồng ý hoãn các cuộc tấn công mới vào Iran, một phần vì nước này cần sự hỗ trợ từ Mỹ trong lĩnh vực phòng thủ tên lửa. Iran và lực lượng Houthi nhiều khả năng sẽ đáp trả nếu bị tấn công, trong khi kho đạn dược phòng thủ của Israel đã trở nên cạn kiệt sau thời gian diễn ra xung đột.
Một nguồn tin khác am hiểu các báo cáo tình báo gần đây của Mỹ cho biết, ông Netanyahu cùng các đồng minh vẫn thiếu một mục tiêu chiến lược rõ ràng, ngoài việc cố gắng thể hiện một dạng “tiến triển” nào đó và tiếp tục làm suy yếu chính quyền Iran.
“Các kế hoạch đã sẵn sàng, chỉ chờ sự phê duyệt từ ông Trump, có thể là sau cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ”, nguồn tin chia sẻ với CNN.
Tiền phong

articles.title: Top Wall Street analysts prefer these 3 dividend stocks for stable income
articles.text:
Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.
Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.
Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
Chevron
Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.
In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.
Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.
Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.
"While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.
Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.
Kinetik Holdings
Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.
Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the company to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.
The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.
Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.
"As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.
Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.
Crescent Energy
Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production company with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent announced an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).
Heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.
"CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," said Richardson.
The 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.
Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.
The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable company, regardless of market conditions.
Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

articles.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Monday
articles.text: My top 10 things to watch Monday, Oct. 26 1. Meta Platforms is looking to raise $95 billion to fund its massive AI infrastructure buildout. The tech giant said Monday that it will initially raise $35 billion through underwritten public equity offerings, followed by an additional $60 billion through an at-the-market program. Nvidia , AMD , and Broadcom have expressed interest in becoming "cornerstone investors" in the equity offering, collectively contributing up to $5 billion, according to Meta's press release . The Club name delivered a strong quarter and guidance last week, and laid out an ambitious plan for its viral Muse AI agent. 2. Elon Musk said SpaceX got its $40 billion debt deal to pay for AI chips and shut the door on the neocloud companies. Writing on X , Musk said the debt markets have almost entirely closed to companies that need financing but don't do more than data centers. (SpaceX also has satellite internet service Starlink and rockets). "That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation," Musk wrote . "Some will make it through, but not many." Neocloud stocks, including CoreWeave , are getting hit. 3. Anthropic drops its long-awaited IPO prospectus . The frontier AI lab plans to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol ANT. No terms; that will come later, after the roadshow. Morgan Stanley and Club name Goldman Sachs are named as top underwriters. Before the filing, speculation put the valuation of the company behind Claude at as much as $2 trillion. 4. Stocks overall are looking for a higher open after a volatile week for names tied to the artificial intelligence boom. In my weekend column , I acknowledged the possibility of more pain ahead for the AI trade but gave reasons why I am not bailing on it. At the same time, we got bigger in non-AI last week. Helping the market this morning are lower oil and tame bond yields. 5. It's an incredibly busy week ahead. As if the two-day October meeting of Federal Reserve policymakers wasn't enough, 11 companies in the Club portfolio report earnings. The biggies include Amazon , Microsoft , and Alp habet, as well as Boeing and Starbucks . In all, a third of the companies in the S & P 500 report quarterly results this week. 6. FedEx is one of them. Bernstein trimmed its price target on the Club name to $377 from $397 ahead of Wednesday evening's earnings. The analysts maintained their buy rating, noting that their quarterly estimates are ahead of consensus. They also expect solid guidance. FedEx Freight reports Thursday evening — its first official earnings report as a standalone firm. 7. UBS raised its price target on Club name Amazon to $348 from $318. The analysts said the company's 2027 capex could exceed $300 billion, which would obliterate free cash flow. Last week, Meta reported negative FCF. Still, UBS kept its buy rating on Amazon ahead of earnings, citing cloud growth acceleration and faster e-commerce margin expansion. 8. Following the iPhone Duo hitting stores on Friday, there are mixed reviews from people who stood in long lines to snag one. Supply was limited for purchase. Preorder wait times are several months. Some users of Apple's first foldable phone were pleased with their purchases, while others reported screen cracks. Redditors are calling it "crackgate." 9. EQT is buying Range Resources in a $13 billion deal to create the nation's biggest natural gas producer. The combined company expects $20 billion in free cash flow in the next five years. EQT shares are down more than 6%. Range stock is up roughly 11%. This space has been ripe for consolidation: Devon completed its purchase of Coterra back in May. 10. Morgan Stanley cut its price target on buy payment company Affirm to $79 from $82 ahead of earnings early next month. Kept hold, citing "valuation and macro sensitivity." I disagree with this call. Affirm is one of a few winners here. Remember, Club name Capital One had a great call last week. articles.title: Anthropic's IPO plans: 900% revenue retention, but $80 billion in first-half losses
articles.text:
Anthropic is officially headed for the public market in what is expected to be a historic offering for a 5-year-old company that's been at the heart of the generative artificial intelligence boom.
In a Form S-1 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic said it plans to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol "ANT."
The company behind Claude confidentially filed with the SEC in June, giving the agency time to review its financials before they were made available to the public and prospective investors.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI, now its chief rival. Anthropic's Claude model and services have captivated the corporate world, as companies have opened their wallets in an effort to crack new growth opportunities and find internal efficiencies.
Expansion has accelerated in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of AI coding tool Claude Code, and powerful models including Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5. The company has been racing to maintain an edge over competitors like OpenAI and Google, and faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government in recent months.
Anthropic's offering, if it doesn't get derailed, will land just a few months after Elon Musk'sSpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion. It's been a volatile stretch for SpaceX shares, which finished last week slightly below where they opened in June.
As it prepares to hit the market, Anthropic has to contend with severe jitters on Wall Street as concerns grow over whether spending on AI services will justify the trillions of dollars in expected infrastructure costs. So-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius have been hammered of late, losing over 30% of their value in October as credit risk is rising across the data center space.
When it comes to getting customers to pay more, Anthropic is currently in a class of its own.
The company's net revenue retention, or NRR, stood at around 900% as of Sept. 30, according to the prospectus. That means existing customers are increasing their spending by ninefold from one year to the next.
"Our customers' journey using Claude often begins with a single use case before expanding across departments, applications, and workflows," Anthropic said. "As our models become more capable, customers often deepen our partnerships — they find more ways to embed Claude into their workflows, increasing the scope of what Claude can accomplish within their enterprises."
For the median public cloud software company as of January, the number was 108%, according to data from Altimeter Capital partner Jamin Ball.
Anthropic said new models that it's released have lowered the costs of specific tasks, resulting in customers increasing their adoption.
"Anthropic net revenue retention is NINE HUNDRED PERCENT," Austin Allred, founder of Gauntlet AI, wrote on X. "What a ridiculous stat."

Daniela Amodei, president and co-founder of Anthropic, during the Bloomberg Tech conference in San Francisco, California, US, on Thursday, June 4, 2026.
David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images
At Anthropic, business is all in the family.
Co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei are siblings. Holden Karnofsky, the spouse of Daniela Amodei, has worked at Anthropic since January 2025, receiving just over $430,000 in total compensation, excluding options and restricted stock units.
Earlier in his career, Karnofsky was co-founder of GiveWell, a nonprofit "dedicated to helping people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives."
More recently, Karnofsky was co-CEO of Open Philanthropy, which has since rebranded to Coefficient Giving. The nonprofit serves as an advisor to Good Ventures, a charity established by Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz and his wife, Cari Tuna.
Both GiveWell and Coefficient Giving have been closely associated with the effective altruism movement, which seeks to achieve the greatest good through the use of capital and other resources. Sam Bankman-Fried of bankrupt cryptocurrency exchange operator FTX contributed to effective altruism causes.
— Jordan Novet
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic breaks down its enterprise customer base
Leon Neal | Getty Images
Anthropic said that as of Sept. 30, its enterprise customer base includes more than 11,900 customers with $100,000 or more of revenue during the trailing twelve-month, or TTM, period.
It also includes more than 1,900 customers with $1 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis, and roughly 250 customers with $10 million or more of revenue on a TTM basis.
"The speed and depth of our enterprise customer adoption are powerful evidence of Claude's position at the frontier of AI," the filing says.
Anthropic said a growing number of its enterprise customers agree to "non-cancelable annual or multi-year contracts," which primarily result in consumption-based revenue.
Consumption-based revenue made up $13.1 billion, or 80% of total revenue, for the six months ended June 30, 2026, according to the filing. Anthropic reported subscription-based revenue of $3.2 billion, or 20% of total revenue, over the same period.
"We expect consumption-based revenue to continue to represent the substantial majority of total revenue for the foreseeable future," the filing says.
— Ashley Capoot
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic has 5,300 employees, referred to internally as 'Ants'
An Anthropic logo is displayed at Moscone Center during the Dreamforce 2026 technology summit in San Francisco, California, US, September 17, 2026.
Carlos Barria | Reuters
Anthropic said it had 5,300 employees as of Sept. 30, compared with 940 staffers as of Dec. 31, 2024.
The company said it logged $6.6 million in revenue per employee for the trailing 12 months, which it said is a "reflection of what we believe is the deepest concentration of AI research talent in the world."
The filing also touches on Anthropic's corporate culture. The company said it refers to its employees internally as "Ants," a nickname that "captures the collaborative, ego-light culture of the team."
"Claude compounds that impact further: Ants use Claude across every function to take on work that would otherwise require substantially larger teams — allowing us to remain remarkably lean relative to our output," according to the filing.
Anthropic said it's "one of the most intensive users of our own technology." More than 90% of contributions to its codebase in September "were written by Claude," the company said.
— Annie Palmer
11 Hours Ago
OpenAI and Google only named competitors
Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, left, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman arrive to the White House for a meeting with Vice President Kamala Harris on artificial intelligence, Thursday, May 4, 2023, in Washington.
Evan Vucci | AP
The only two companies Anthropic named as competitors in its prospectus are OpenAI and Google.
"We face direct competition from companies building frontier models for third-party software developers and enterprises, including OpenAI and Google, and large, well-capitalized technology companies investing to reach the frontier," Anthropic said.
Additionally, the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
— Ari Levy
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic says dependence on TSMC for chip manufacturing is a risk
A motorcycle is seen near a building of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which is a Taiwanese multinational semiconductor contract manufacturing and design company, in Hsinchu, Taiwan, on April 16, 2025.
Daniel Ceng | Anadolu | Getty Images
Anthropic said the geographic concentration of advanced chip manufacturing in Taiwan, particularly at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., is a risk to its business.
The company said it could be impacted by natural disasters in Taiwan, potential disruption from geopolitical tensions with China, disruptions to its power grid or other critical infrastructure as well as trade regulations or restrictions.
"Accordingly, any restrictions or delays on the supply of advanced chips out of Taiwan or TSMC would adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations."
— Ashley Capoot
11 Hours Ago
What is Founder LLC?
The Amodei siblings — Dario and Daniela — along with Anthropic's five other co-founders will be the "sole members of" Founder LLC, which will hold 50.1% of the voting power of outstanding shares, the filing said.
The other members of the LLC are:
Tom Brown, chief compute officer
Jack Clark, head of Anthropic Institute
Jared Kaplan, chief science officer
Sam McCandlish, chief architect
Christopher Olah, head of interpretability research efforts
The group owns in total about 1.7 billion Class A shares.
— Ari Levy
Correction: Sam McCandlish is chief architect of Anthropic. An earlier version misspelled his name.
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic agreed to pay SpaceX $3.1 billion per month for compute
Cheng Xin | Getty Images
Anthropic will pay SpaceX around $3.1 billion per month to "access compute powered by NVIDIA GPUs," once all promised capacity is delivered, the filing said. The company has agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion over a period extending into 2029.
Anthropic's filing said the company has other agreements with Microsoft, Nscale, Lambda and other cloud providers to provide "compute capacity powered by Nvidia GPUS."
SpaceX said in its third-quarter financial filing last week that a customer, which is Anthropic, paid the company just over $5 billion, or 34.5% of its total $14.58 billion in revenue for the quarter.
SpaceX previously said Anthropic would spend up to $1.25 billion per month on cloud compute capacity at the company's Colossus data centers in the area around Memphis, Tennessee.
— Lora Kolodny
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic could use net proceeds to 'acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies'
Anthropic said it intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for "general corporate purposes," including capital expenditures, working capital, operating expenses, and hiring and retention of "highly skilled personnel."
The company said it may also use a portion of the net proceeds to "acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies."
"However, we do not have agreements or commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time," the filing says.
— Ashley Capoot
11 Hours Ago
How much Anthropic's top brass gets paid
According to Monday's filing, Amodei's compensation totaled $17.96 million in 2025, with the vast majority coming from stock and options awards. His base salary was $654,167.
His sister, Daniela Amodei, was the second-highest paid executive at $16.4 million for 2025. Her base salary is the same as her brother's.
Both Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei received raises in 2025 and two pay bumps this year. Both executives' base salary was increased to $1.38 million, effective July 1, according to the release.
Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao earned a base salary of $706,250 in 2025, and following several salary increases, his base salary now reaches $1.25 million, effective July 1.
— Annie Palmer
11 Hours Ago
Anthropic has nearly $45 billion in commitments with Microsoft, which is also a rival
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a Microsoft Frontier Tour event in the CNIT building at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on October 20, 2026.
Dimitar Dilkoff | Afp | Getty Images
Microsoft announced plans to invest $5 billion in Anthropic last November in a funding round valuing the lab in the range of $350 billion. In May, Anthropic said it had raised funds at a $965 billion valuation, and weeks later, Microsoft disclosed a $3.2 billion gain on its stake.
At the time of its investment announcement last year, Microsoft said Anthropic would bring its Claude large language models to the Microsoft Azure cloud, widening access to software developers. Plus, Anthropic signed on to spend $30 billion on Azure and contracting as much as a gigawatt worth of additional computing power.
Anthropic and Microsoft have modified the November 2025 agreement such that Anthropic now intends to spend with Microsoft at least $44.9 billion between November 2026 and May 2033. The deal can't be canceled unless Microsoft has an uncured material breach or an undelivered tranche.
Anthropic said in Monday's prospectus that it pays fees to Microsoft — plus Amazon and Google — in a joint go-to-market arrangement to gain a direct relationship with customers.
Plus, Anthropic counts on Microsoft, as well as Amazon, Google and Broadcom, for computing power in relationships that "create dependencies and potential vulnerabilities."
Microsoft has integrated Claude models into the GitHub Copilot coding tool, the Foundry model garden and Copilot Cowork, a product that takes on complex productivity tasks. At the same time, Microsoft has been advertising the capabilities of models it has built in house, at times touting advantages over Anthropic alternatives.
"Amazon, Google, and Microsoft each offer AI services and develop and deploy competing AI models through their respective cloud platforms," Anthropic said.
Additionally, Christopher Liddell, a former Microsoft finance chief, joined Anthropic's board in February, according to the filing.
"To the extent these CSPs promote, integrate, prioritize, or provide customer access to our models, platform, and applications on terms that are less favorable than those applicable to their own competing offerings or to the offerings of other companies, including with respect to pricing, commercial terms, product placement, integration, or access to compute or sales incentives, our competitive position, customer adoption, and business results could be adversely affected," Anthropic said.
— Jordan Novet
12 Hours Ago
Anthropic says its capital and governance structure has 'no direct public company precedent'
Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos, Switzerland, on Tuesday, Jan. 20, 2026.
Krisztian Bocsi | Bloomberg | Getty Images
Anthropic said it has a novel capital and corporate governance structure that "has no direct public company precedent."
"Our governance structure is likely to have the effect of limiting the likelihood of an unsolicited merger proposal, unsolicited tender offer, or proxy contest for the removal of directors," the filing said. "As a result, our governance structure may make it more difficult to replace our directors and management and may have the effect of depriving our stockholders of an opportunity to sell their shares at a premium over prevailing market prices."
— Ashley Capoot
12 Hours Ago
MIT professor Sinan Aral says enterprise is key to Anthropic's success in the market
watch now
VIDEO5:5105:51
MIT's Sinan Aral on Anthropic IPO: Enterprise is key to its market success
Sinan Aral, MIT Sloan professor and AI investor, said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Anthropic's ability to be profitable in the enterprise space will determine whether it's an attractive prospect for investors.
"If you think about the $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation, that's approximately from the low to high end a 22 times to 30 times revenue multiple. So the future growth and the profit of this company are being priced in that kind of valuation," Aral said.
"The question is, where is the enduring value? And I think the enduring value is going to come from companies that can demonstrate enterprise profitability, productivity, and actual value add, rather than just providing intelligence. I think Anthropic is on the way to doing that ... and I think that is where it will succeed and fail."
— Caleigh Keating
12 Hours Ago
No single customer represents more than a tenth of Anthropic's revenue
Anthropic logo and a keyboard in this illustration taken October 19, 2026.
Dado Ruvic | Reuters
With so many firms relying on Anthropic, the company can say that its business has greater diversification than top artificial intelligence chipmaker Nvidia.
"No single customer represented more than 10% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026," Anthropic said in its IPO prospectus.
Nvidia, by comparison, had five clients that were contributing at least 10% of accounts receivable as of July, according to a filing.
Anthropic, for its part, reported that five customers accounted for about a quarter of its revenue for the first nine months of 2026.
"We anticipate that we will continue to derive a significant portion of our revenue from a limited number of customers for the foreseeable future, and in some cases, the portion of our revenue attributable to certain customers may increase in the future," the AI lab said in the prospectus.
At the end of 2025, revenue from customers that buy through cloud marketplaces represented 48% of revenue, the filing shows.
— Jordan Novet
12 Hours Ago
Anthropic lost $80.7 billion in the first half of this year
Anthropic said it lost a staggering $80.7 billion in the first six months of this year, after losing $12.9 billion over the same stretch in 2025.
The vast majority of its net loss in the first half of the year, about $72 billion, comes from accounting charges related to changes in the value of convertible notes, "resulting from an increase in our enterprise valuation during each of the respective periods," Anthropic said.
For all of 2025, the company lost about $41.9 billion, widening from a loss of $8.3 billion in 2024.
— Annie Palmer
12 Hours Ago
Anthropic reported $16.29 billion in revenue for first half of the year
Anthropic said revenue increased 1,304% to $16.29 billion in the six months ended June 30, up from $1.16 billion during the same period a year earlier. Revenue for all of last year jumped 1,089% to $4.59 billion.
— Ashley Capoot
12 Hours Ago
Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are Anthropic's top IPO underwriters
Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, April 10, 2026.
Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images
At the top of the prospectus for Anthropic's historic initial public offering, the two biggest investment banks for technology IPOs receive the largest billing. The lead left, as the term is called for the underwriter listed first, is Goldman Sachs. On the right is Morgan Stanley.
Others banks participating in the share float include JPMorgan, Citigroup, Barclays, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, RBC Capital Markets, UBS Investment Bank, BMO Capital Markets, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, Jefferies, Mizuho, MUFG, Societe Generale, TD Securities, BTIG, Cantor, Capital One Securities and Macquarie Capital.
— Jordan Novet
12 Hours Ago
Who is Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei?
Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during a Bloomberg Television interview in San Francisco, California, US, on Tuesday, Dec. 9, 2025.
David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images
Amodei grew up in San Francisco and earned his doctorate degree in biophysics from Princeton University.
Before starting Anthropic, Amodei, now 43, worked as a senior research scientist at Google Brain, which is now part of AI unit Google DeepMind. Amodei also spent more than four years at OpenAI, where he led the development of models including GPT-2 and GPT-3.
His sister, Daniela Amodei, is another Anthropic co-founder and serves as the company's president.
— Ashley Capoot
12 Hours Ago
Anthropic's most recent funding round
watch now
VIDEO1:3501:35
Anthropic raises $65B in latest funding round at $965B valuation
Anthropic closed its last funding round in May, when it raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation. The financing was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, and nearly tripled Anthropic's valuation from February, when the company was worth $380 billion.
The round was particularly notable because it pushed Anthropic's valuation above OpenAI's for the first time. OpenAI was valued at $852 billion in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round.

articles.title: Lãi suất 'hạ nhiệt', bất động sản có đón đầu chu kỳ tăng trưởng mới?
articles.text:
Lãi suất 'hạ nhiệt', bất động sản có đón đầu chu kỳ tăng trưởng mới?
Khi lãi suất đảo chiều sẽ kích thích dòng tiền nhàn rỗi dịch chuyển từ kênh tiết kiệm sang các kênh đầu tư sinh lời cao hơn. Trong đó, bất động sản là một “bến đỗ” chiến lược có độ trễ nhất định và cuộc chơi sẽ chuyển dịch sang trạng thái chuẩn bị đón đầu chu kỳ tăng trưởng mới.
- 26-10-2026Fed sắp họp chính sách, thị trường dự đoán 90% NHTW thực hiện điều này với lãi suất
- 26-10-2026Lãi suất ngày 26/10 tại MB, VPBank, Techcombank, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank,...
- 26-10-2026Lời khuyên cho người thích gửi tiết kiệm kỳ hạn ngắn: Linh hoạt hơn nhưng đừng bỏ qua 2 rủi ro này
Sẽ chuyển trạng thái
Ngân hàng Nhà nước vừa ban hành Văn bản số 9608/NHNN-CSTT về việc triển khai các giải pháp hoạt động của các tổ chức tín dụng. Theo đó, các ngân hàng thương mại thực hiện giảm tối thiểu 0,5%/năm lãi suất tiền gửi bình quân của các giao dịch phát sinh mới đối với các kỳ hạn từ 6 tháng trở lên trong các tháng cuối năm 2026 so với mức lãi suất của chính ngân hàng thương mại tại kỳ báo cáo ngày 11- 20/10.
Các ngân hàng tuyệt đối không đua tăng lãi suất huy động, cạnh tranh không lành mạnh, gây bất ổn đến an ninh tài chính tiền tệ.
Đối với lãi suất cho vay, Ngân hàng Nhà nước yêu cầu các tổ chức tín dụng triển khai giải pháp giảm lãi suất cho khách hàng, trong đó tập trung giảm từ 1,5 - 2%/năm đối với lĩnh vực sản xuất, kinh doanh và các lĩnh vực ưu tiên.
Trao đổi với PV Tiền Phong, ông Nguyễn Viết Hùng - Tổng Giám đốc Công ty H Holding - cho rằng, khi lãi suất hạ nhiệt, dòng tiền sẽ không chảy vào một kênh duy nhất mà mang tính phân bổ theo khẩu vị rủi ro và kỳ vọng lợi nhuận.
Cụ thể, kênh tiết kiệm sẽ giữ lại một phần dòng tiền của nhóm nhà đầu tư thận trọng, ưa chắc ăn, nhưng sức hút sẽ giảm dần khi lãi suất huy động thấp. Tuy nhiên, vẫn là một phần dự phòng thanh khoản nhanh trong ngắn hạn, phòng bị cho những biến động.
Với đầu tư chứng khoán thường là “kênh nhạy bén nhất” và phản ứng nhanh nhất ngay khi lãi suất hạ, dòng tiền ngắn hạn sẽ đổ vào đây trước để tìm kiếm sóng ngắn.
Trong khi đó, bất động sản, là “bến đỗ” của dòng vốn trung và dài hạn. Khi lãi suất hạ và ngấm dần vào nền kinh tế, dòng tiền lớn sẽ chảy mạnh vào bất động sản có giá trị thực, phục vụ nhu cầu ở thực hoặc khai thác thương mại được ngay.
Ông Hùng khẳng định, việc lãi suất cho vay hạ nhiệt - giảm từ 1,5 - 2%/năm - không chỉ đơn thuần là một con số giảm chi phí tài chính mà còn thay đổi kỳ vọng của toàn bộ thị trường. Trong giai đoạn trước, chi phí vốn đắt đỏ khiến dòng tiền thủ thế, nhà đầu tư e dè sử dụng đòn bẩy. Khi lãi suất đảo chiều, chi phí gánh nặng tài chính giảm xuống, kích thích dòng tiền nhàn rỗi dịch chuyển từ kênh an toàn (tiết kiệm) sang các kênh đầu tư sinh lời cao hơn, trong đó bất động sản là một “bến đỗ” chiến lược có độ trễ nhất định.
"Cuộc chơi sẽ chuyển dịch từ trạng thái “phòng thủ, thanh khoản chậm” sang trạng thái “chuẩn bị đón đầu chu kỳ tăng trưởng mới”, ông Hùng nhận định.
Cần chia sẻ khó khăn với doanh nghiệp
Trong khi đó, ông Lê Hoàng Châu - Chủ tịch Hiệp hội Bất động sản TPHCM (HoREA) cho biết, khi phải giảm lãi suất cho vay thực chất, các ngân hàng thương mại chia sẻ khó khăn với doanh nghiệp và khách hàng vay vốn. HoREA đã đề nghị Ngân hàng Nhà nước quyết liệt đôn đốc, kiểm tra các ngân hàng thương mại thực hiện chủ trương giảm lãi suất cho vay, nhằm hỗ trợ nền kinh tế.
“Các ngân hàng cần chia sẻ một phần lợi nhuận để giảm chi phí vốn cho khách hàng, thay vì chỉ trông chờ vào việc tiết giảm chi phí hoạt động”, ông Châu nói.
Theo HoREA, tại cuộc họp với các tổ chức tín dụng ngày 19/10, Thống đốc Ngân hàng Nhà nước Phạm Đức Ấn đã chỉ đạo quyết liệt việc giảm mặt bằng lãi suất để hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp và nền kinh tế.
Thống kê của HoREA cho thấy, phần lớn trong số 27 ngân hàng thương mại duy trì lợi nhuận khá cao và ổn định, với tổng lợi nhuận thường đạt khoảng 7 - 10 tỷ USD mỗi năm. So với tổng vốn điều lệ khoảng 922.000 tỷ đồng của 27 ngân hàng này, HoREA tính toán tỷ lệ lợi nhuận tương đương khoảng 19,7 - 28,2%/năm.
Trong khi đó, nhiều doanh nghiệp vẫn phải tiếp cận vốn với lãi suất cao. Đặc biệt, tại cuộc họp Ban Chỉ đạo Trung ương về chính sách nhà ở và thị trường bất động sản ngày 13/10, một số địa phương phản ánh có trường hợp lãi suất vay lên đến 18-19%/năm.
“Sự chênh lệch giữa mức lợi nhuận của các ngân hàng và chi phí vốn mà doanh nghiệp phải gánh chịu là vấn đề được HoREA đặt ra khi kiến nghị giảm lãi suất cho vay”, ông Châu nói.
Đáng chú ý, ông Châu cũng phản ánh tình trạng một số tổ chức tín dụng định giá tài sản thế chấp thấp hơn giá trị thực tế, có trường hợp chỉ bằng khoảng 70%, khiến doanh nghiệp và người vay khó tiếp cận đủ nguồn vốn cần thiết. Do đó, ông Châu đề nghị Ngân hàng Nhà nước tăng cường kiểm tra, giám sát, bảo đảm chủ trương giảm lãi suất được triển khai thực chất, mang lại lợi ích cho khách hàng vay vốn.
“Việc giảm lãi suất không chỉ áp dụng cho khách hàng vay mới mà còn đối với các khoản dư nợ hiện hữu. Điều này có ý nghĩa đối với những doanh nghiệp đang duy trì dư nợ lớn, phải trả lãi định kỳ và chịu áp lực chi phí tài chính trong hoạt động sản xuất, kinh doanh”, ông Châu lưu ý.
Tiền phong

            UK 10 Year Bond Yield - Summary
UK 10-year gilt yields edged down to 5.35% as investors awaited Wednesday’s budget, with expectations that Chancellor John Healey will adhere to fiscal rules helping ease pressure on government bonds. According to the Financial Times, the government plans to provide £20.4 billion in additional funding to the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank through extra borrowing. The National Wealth Fund is expected to receive £15.4 billion over five years, including £2 billion for renewable energy, while the British Business Bank will get £5 billion. However, borrowing is not due to begin until the 2028–29 fiscal year, limiting near-term concerns for bond markets. Healey has also pledged to give businesses more “breathing space,” raising expectations of potential cuts to electricity levies. Investors will also watch the Bank of England’s monetary indicators later this week, alongside policy decisions from the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank.
UK 10 Year Bond Yield - Stats
The yield on United Kingdom 10Y Bond Yield eased to 5.35% on October 26, 2026, marking a 0.02 percentage points decrease from the previous session. articles.title: Fanatics teams up with OpenAI for new AI-powered shopping suggestion feature
articles.text:
At any given moment, Fanatics offers more than 1.5 million unique SKUs for sports fans to buy — from jerseys and hats to team-branded streetwear and socks. The search for those items is getting easier with a new feature called "Shop the Look," created with the help of OpenAI's Codex.
Fanatics' product assortment reflects its rise into a massive sports-industry platform, with deals with nearly every major sports league and team worldwide. Each year, Fanatics Commerce manufactures more than 45 million items and sells them to customers in more than 180 countries.
But Justin Tsai, chief product officer for Fanatics Commerce, said that growth has also created a challenge for the company.
"One problem we just kept seeing was that our customers come to our sites, and we operate hundreds of these sites … their challenges are that they're always trying to look through our very large catalog to figure out what they can buy," he said.
Tsai said customers' shopping sessions routinely ran over 30 minutes on average, and that time kept compounding as Fanatics released upwards of a thousand new products each week.
"Shop the Look" suggests coordinated outfits on each product page, matching those items with other in-stock items based on team and intended style.
Traditional shopping curation strategies, like photo shoots and stylized outfits, have lead times that don't always work with Fanatics' rapidly increasing product pool, or for quickly-released items like championship shirts and hats, Tsai said.
Random suggestions don't work for sports fans either. "Nobody who is a Los Angeles Dodgers fan wants to be matched with a San Francisco Giants item … team and player alignment is extremely important in our world," he said.
Even as Fanatics has grown into a multibillion-dollar business, team merchandise remains its biggest revenue source. Fanatics founder and CEO Michael Rubin told CNBC's "Squawk Box" earlier this month that the company's commerce business will exceed $7 billion in revenue this year, compared with roughly $5.5 billion for its collectibles business, which includes Topps trading cards.
OpenAI has been experimenting with shopping tools for ChatGPT since the chatbot's launch, including a feature last fall that let users buy merchants' products directly within ChatGPT. However, it is ending the Instant Checkout effort and now is working directly with retailers to create dedicated apps within ChatGPT, according to CNBC reporting.
The new Fanatics feature is another way OpenAI is leveraging its technology across shopping. Rosemary DeAragon, head of industry GTM at OpenAI, said this personalization issue in retail "is an age-old problem." While the rise of e-commerce gave retailers new ways to "figure out the fingerprint of the customer" — whether that's past purchase history, where they are viewing the website from, or a logged-in account — those efforts still sometimes miss the mark.
"In the past we were trying to stitch together something that would be good to show a customer," DeAragon said. "With AI, you can do more deterministic matching to do personalization in this next-level way."
"Shop the Look" uses OpenAI's Codex to create a tool that parses product and catalog data to find compatible items and reevaluate recommendations, ultimately creating those looks that might suggest a hat, socks and other accessories to go with a jersey a fan is considering purchasing.
Tsai said that after rolling out the new feature, there was a 10% increase in views of recommended items. He also said the suggested items help shoppers have "more conviction" about the items they're thinking of buying, seeing how it may fit with other team gear.
DeAragon said that while there will always be room in the shopping experience for more curated looks and trying items on in person, the integration of AI into efforts like this — where it can help narrow down massive product selections and show what might work with a valuable purchase like an authentic team jersey — shows that there is a "really big opportunity to enhance the existing experience."

articles.title: This discount retailer is catching up to its main rival under its new CEO, UBS says
articles.text: Ross Stores is becoming more productive under new CEO James Conroy, which should help boost its stock, according to UBS. The investment bank upgraded the retailer to buy from neutral. It also raised its price target on shares to $315 from $239, implying 37% upside from Friday's close. "The ROST pivotal question is if its recent same store sales growth momentum can persist beyond this year. …The answer is yes," analyst Jay Sole said Monday in a note to clients. Ross has lagged TJ Maxx's productivity by a wide margin, but changes in merchandising, marketing and improved in-store operations should help it close the gap, according to UBS. Conroy joined Ross Stores in February 2025. By the end of that year, Ross' productivity rose 24% while that of its competitor jumped 44%, Sole said. "The market doesn't appreciate how much ROST closing this gap will drive [same-store sales] growth in [fiscal year 2027] and beyond," he said. As productivity improves, Ross should be able to grow its revenue at a compound annual growth rate of roughly 8.5% over the next two years, per UBS. That's about 260 basis points above the Street's consensus estimate for Ross' revenue, according to the bank. UBS' call falls in line with consensus on the Street. Of the 21 analysts covering Ross Stores, 14 have a buy or strong buy on the stock, while seven have a hold rating on it, LSEG data shows. Shares have fallen 4% over the past three months.

articles.title: Caregiving for adult relatives can cost thousands. AARP survey finds support could matter to midterm voters
articles.text:
For millions of families, caregiving is not just a personal responsibility; it is a growing affordability challenge. And the issue is emerging in the 2026 midterm elections.
Some 59 million Americans provide care for an adult family member, neighbor or friend, according to a recent report from AARP, a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization that advocates for people age 50 and older.
Many of those caregivers face mounting financial pressures as they balance the cost of helping loved ones with their own household expenses, jobs and retirement security. A new study from Edward Jones found that Americans caring for aging family members spend an average of $8,737 per year out of pocket and that their personal retirement savings and careers bear the brunt.
Results of a new AARP survey show that in 43 competitive congressional districts, most of the likely voters age 50 and older said they're more likely to vote for candidates who back policies that support unpaid caregivers helping loved ones. Because voters 50 and up comprise one of the most important voting blocs, the survey shows that support could make a difference in closely contested races.
Among those older surveyed voters, 77% said they would be more likely to vote for a candidate who advocated for a tax credit for unpaid family caregivers who help pay for a loved one's care. Nearly as many, 75%, said they would be more likely to vote for a candidate who advocated for support for unpaid family caregivers helping loved ones remain in their homes.
Fabrizio Ward and Impact Research conducted the survey for AARP, interviewing 1,368 likely voters age 18 and older, including 848 voters age 50 and older, from Oct. 1-5. The margin of error for the 1,368 sample was plus or minus 2.7 percentage points. The data was weighted to represent the voting population of the targeted congressional districts nationwide.
Voters ages 50 and above "are going to be the deciders in the election," said Matt Hogan, a partner at Impact Research, a public opinion research and consulting firm. "So for candidates looking to win over this critical voting bloc, a focus on helping caregivers would go a long way in helping them make inroads."
Caregivers face greater financial insecurity
Temple, Texas, resident Brittney Saunders Graves, a 33-year-old part-time counselor, is the primary family caregiver for her 62-year-old mother, Tracey Saunders, who had a debilitating stroke in 2020. Graves, a U.S. Army veteran who is also a stroke survivor, said she spends an average of $600 a month to help pay for her mother's care. Those expenses include transportation, copays and medications.
"After we set aside the necessities, leaving out medication [and] doctor's appointments, she only has around $400 to cover food," Graves said.
The financial impact of caregiving can extend well beyond immediate out-of-pocket expenses.
Caregivers are more likely than non-caregivers to have fewer financial assets and report debt problems, according to the Employee Benefit Research Institute's 2026 Retirement Confidence Survey. About one-third, 34%, of caregivers reported having less than $10,000 in savings and investments, compared with 25% of non-caregivers. More than two-thirds, 69%, of caregivers said debt is a problem, compared with 57% of non-caregivers.
These financial pressures can make it harder for caregivers to build savings, manage household expenses and prepare for retirement.
The challenges are especially significant for Americans in the so-called sandwich generation, who may support aging parents while also raising children or managing other family responsibilities, said Keesha Middlemass, a political science professor at Howard University.
"The sandwich generation is only going to get larger” as the population ages and lifespans increase, Middlemass said.
Sarah Smitley, a 50-year-old in Sylvania, Ohio, cares for her 20-year-old daughter with autism, and also helps her aging parents. Smitley works as a family navigator for a nonprofit organization that supports people with mental illness. She said she'd like political leaders to understand the affordability issues many caregivers face.
"Maybe we can't take off time, or we've run out of vacation pay, or we know medical costs are high even with insurance and just out of pocket that it's not easy to come up with another $50," Smitley said.
Medicaid cuts could add to caregiver strain
Some Medicaid cuts under President Donald Trump's "big beautiful bill" will take effect in January. Without government assistance, unpaid family caregivers, who often must cover their loved ones' expenses, would face greater financial challenges, Middlemass said.
"The future cuts, actually, that are going to come to Medicaid and Medicare in 2027 are going to be devastating for those in the lower incomes, but also workers that are in the care economy," she said.
Paula Bussard, a 71-year-old retiree in Carlisle, Pennsylvania, said she worries the cuts will mean fewer doctors, home health agencies and medical equipment providers will accept Medicaid.
Bussard cares for her 42-year-old son, Alex, who has complicated medical needs since surviving a brain tumor and brain hemorrhage. She said the family already spends $5,000 to $7,000 annually to care for their son at home, including accommodations and supplies not covered by Medicaid.
"Political candidates need to know that every human being deserves dignity, respect and health care," Bussard said. She added that Medicaid is crucial for millions of Americans who cannot work and "helps their families take care of them in the home."
But families already struggling with the cost of caregiving say campaign proposals may not necessarily translate into confidence that meaningful help is coming.
"When you look at, okay, this is being advertised, but then you peel it back, it's like, will this happen? Will this happen?" Graves said.

articles.title: Cracking AI trade has Wall Street looking for a hedge. An ex-Citadel quant may have the answer
articles.text:
As CoreWeave shares plummet, taking much of the AI complex with it, investors face a simple question: what's the best way to hedge AI risk?
An ex-Citadel quant might have the answer.
Jasper Zhang is an ex-Citadel Securities quantitative researcher who now leads Hyperbolic. It's a 50-person financial technology startup building a spot marketplace for tradable GPU computing power, a tool that would allow traders to hedge against a decline in AI demand.
The platform allows investors to buy and sell GPU clusters, the units that power AI compute. This is done through Hyperbolic's Forge software, which virtually logs into clusters worldwide and makes technical tweaks so that mismatched clusters work better together, allowing traders to not just buy and sell a standardized unit of compute, but also control the underlying GPUs for their own purposes.
Zhang says it's as good as being in the data center itself, and sees the technology as the first building block of "physically" settled GPU futures, which, upon settlement, would offer contract owners complete control over a cluster with known characteristics. In other words, it would allow investors a new way to hedge against a decline in AI demand by trading the hardware itself.
Currently, GPU architecture varies wildly depending on how they are assembled, leading to various levels of output. Every data center is different. Networking, memory, and security all affect GPU performance. At the same time, financing agreements often prevent builders from sharing prices, meaning a survey-based index may average setup costs while missing outlier expenses.
In the futures world, that's called "basis risk." It's a problem for market-makers to solve, and a void Zhang hopes Hyperbolic can fill.
The 31-year-old Zhang came to America with several Chinese math medals and finished a math doctorate at U.C. Berkeley in just two years before taking a job at Citadel Securities building trading models. Hyperbolic's head of finance, Hong Chan Kim is a hedge fund veteran, having worked at Point72, Balyasny Asset Management and Citadel LLC, the hedge fund. 
Hyperbolic has raised $20 million since its launch in 2022, is in the midst of another funding round, and expects a $150 million annualized run rate by year-end. As of today, the company says it has about 250,000 users and an estimated $200 million worth of annual GPU compute connected to its platform.
Emerging market
Other big players see a similar opportunity in the marketplace for AI hedging tools.
CME Group plans to offer a cash-settled futures product that is tied to GPU pricing maintained by Silicon Data, an index-provider backed by DRW, one of the biggest prop-trading firms in Chicago.
"There's a ton of demand and capital flowing into this ecosystem so there's a lot of risk," Don Wilson, founder and CEO of DRW, said in a call. "Cash futures are a great first building block. There are plenty of electricity futures that are cash-settled, oil futures that are cash-settled, so I think you can start these things either way."
The CME product is currently under review with the CFTC, but the commission recently extended that review period to November 9th, likely also tying up another futures contract proposed by Intercontinental Exchange and data-provider Ornn, backed by Andreessen Horowitz's a16z crypto fund.
"Our guess is when the cash-settled futures come out they're not going to be reflective of what's going on in reality," says Hyperbolic's Kim. "Physical usage is what will tether that connection between the reality and the derivatives."
The bigger issue is that cash futures are an imperfect hedge for real-world risk. If AI demand hits a wall, AI rent-a-centers like CoreWeave could end up sitting on billions of dollars in AI hardware with little to no way to cash out.
"Indices are a normalized global number," said Carmen Li, CEO of Silicon data and DRW-backed Compute Exchange, a marketplace for buying and selling GPUs that is also laying groundwork for physically-settled futures. "You get financially hedged, but if you're looking for procurement, that's not going to help you."
What the AI complex needs most – in particular smaller startups that don't have the capital or credit to risk making big hardware purchases – is a virtual pipeline to physical hardware, contends Zhang.
"CoreWeave's debt situation would be less concerning if providers had more ways to monetize available GPU capacity during a slowdown, especially when long-term contracts carry thin margins," said Zhang. "Cash-settled futures can help falling prices, but they do not by themselves put idle GPUs to work."
